definitions.note: 3rd person plural (they/you all) of "acabar" in the simple past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles acabaram o trabalho ontem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They finished the work yesterday.

definitions.note: Conditional form of “acabar” (used for hypotheticals).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu acabaria o trabalho hoje, mas estou doente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would finish the work today, but I'm sick.

definitions.note: Third-person singular (ele/ela/você) future tense of "acabar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O filme acabará às dez.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The movie will end at ten.

definitions.note: Imperfect subjunctive form of "acabar"; often used after "se" (if) or to express a wish/possibility in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se eu acabasse o trabalho cedo, iria ao cinema.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If I finished the work early, I would go to the movies.

definitions.note: Past tense of "acabar" for informal "tu" (2nd person singular).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Acabaste o teu trabalho ontem?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Did you finish your work yesterday?

definitions.note: Used with 'que' (present subjunctive) or as a command for você (imperative).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que você acabe o trabalho hoje.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you finish the work today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Acabei o trabalho cedo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I finished the work early.

definitions.note: Common in the structure “acabei de + infinitive” to talk about the very recent past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Acabei de chegar em casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I just got home.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive of "acabar" (also used for commands with "vocês").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que acabem o trabalho hoje.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope they finish the work today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu acabo o trabalho às cinco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I finish the work at five.

definitions.note: Used as an auxiliary in the structure “acabou de” + infinitive to say something happened very recently.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele acabou de chegar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He just arrived.

definitions.note: Commonly used to mean something is over; can also imply “that’s it.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O filme acabou.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The movie ended.

definitions.note: In Brazil, this is the most common everyday meaning.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu vou para a academia depois do trabalho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to the gym after work.

definitions.note: Refers to universities and academic life in general.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela quer seguir carreira na academia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She wants to pursue a career in academia.

definitions.note: Feminine form (used with feminine nouns or to refer to a woman).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela é uma pesquisadora acadêmica.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is an academic researcher.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele tem um estilo de escrita bem acadêmico.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He has a very academic writing style.

definitions.note: Relating to universities, scholarship, or education; can also refer to an academic person (scholar), depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O artigo acadêmico foi publicado em uma revista internacional.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The academic article was published in an international journal.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os acadêmicos publicaram um artigo sobre o tema.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The academics published an article on the topic.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Essa música me acalma.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That song calms me down.

definitions.note: Often used as “acalmar-se” = “to calm down.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tente acalmar o bebê antes de colocá-lo no berço.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Try to soothe the baby before putting him in the crib.

definitions.note: Often used as an imperative (command) or in the present subjunctive (e.g., after “que”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Acalme-se, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Calm down, please.

definitions.note: Usually used as a command (plural) or with "vocês" in the present subjunctive.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Acalmem-se e respirem fundo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Calm down and take a deep breath.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Depois da notícia, ele se acalmou.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the news, he calmed down.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Foi uma discussão acalorada sobre política.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It was a heated discussion about politics.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O acampamento fica perto do lago.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The campsite is near the lake.

definitions.note: Can be either simple past (pretérito perfeito) or present (presente) for "we".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No fim de semana, acampamos perto do rio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: On the weekend, we camped near the river.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vamos acampar perto do lago neste fim de semana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re going to camp near the lake this weekend.

definitions.note: Often used in questions as “por acaso…?” meaning “by any chance…?”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Você encontrou isso acaso?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Did you find this by chance?

definitions.note: Often used in the expression "por acaso" (= by chance).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Foi puro acaso que nos encontramos aqui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It was pure chance that we met here.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela aceita o convite.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She accepts the invitation.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O pedido foi aceitado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The request was accepted.

definitions.note: Third-person plural present tense (they/you all accept).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles aceitam o convite.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They accept the invitation.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nós aceitamos o convite para o jantar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We accept the invitation to dinner.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nós aceitamos as regras do jogo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We agree to the rules of the game.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu vou aceitar o convite.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to accept the invitation.

definitions.note: Often used with "aceitar" + noun/idea to mean agreeing to something (e.g., a plan, a proposal).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela não vai aceitar a proposta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She isn’t going to agree to the proposal.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito perfeito), 3rd person plural: “they/you (plural) accepted.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles aceitaram a proposta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They accepted the proposal.

definitions.note: First-person singular (eu) in the future tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu aceitarei a oferta amanhã.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will accept the offer tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu aceitaria o convite, mas já tenho planos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would accept the invitation, but I already have plans.

definitions.note: Third-person singular (ele/ela/você) in the future tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele aceitará a oferta amanhã.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He will accept the offer tomorrow.

definitions.note: Usually used with "tu" (informal "you"), common in Portugal and in some regions of Brazil.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu aceitas este acordo?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you accept this agreement?

definitions.note: Feminine plural form (past participle/adjective), used to agree with feminine plural nouns.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: As propostas foram aceitas pela equipe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The proposals were accepted by the team.

definitions.note: Often used after expressions like “espero que...”, “é importante que...”, or as a formal command (imperative) to “you”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que você aceite o convite.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you accept the invitation.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito perfeito) of “aceitar” in the 1st person singular (“I”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu aceitei o convite.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I accepted the invitation.

definitions.note: Formal/standard 3rd person plural present subjunctive of "aceitar"; also used for commands ("you all/them accept").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: É importante que vocês aceitem as regras.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s important that you all accept the rules.

definitions.note: Past participle of "aceitar"; also commonly used as an adjective meaning "accepted".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O seu pedido foi aceito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Your request was accepted.

definitions.note: Present indicative (1st person singular) of "aceitar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu aceito as suas condições.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I accept your conditions.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele aceitou o convite.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He accepted the invitation.

definitions.note: Common colloquial/informal spoken form of “aceitar” with the final -r dropped.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu vou aceitá a oferta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to accept the offer.

definitions.note: Present tense form of "acelerar" (also used as an informal command: "Speed up!").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele acelera quando a luz fica verde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He speeds up when the light turns green.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O ritmo desta música é muito acelerado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The rhythm of this song is very fast.

definitions.note: Present participle/gerund of “acelerar”; often used with “estar” to describe an ongoing action.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O carro está acelerando na estrada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The car is accelerating on the road.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O carro começou a acelerar na estrada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The car started to speed up on the road.

definitions.note: Can be used as a command (imperative, e.g. to you/you-all in formal address) or as present subjunctive (e.g. after 'espero que').
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Acelere, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Speed up, please.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O motorista acelerou quando o sinal ficou verde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The driver sped up when the light turned green.

definitions.note: Usually used as a present subjunctive form (also used for commands with você).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Por favor, acenda a luz.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please turn on the light.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (vocês/eles/elas). Often used after expressions like “que” or for requests/commands.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que acendam as luzes antes de começar a reunião.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope they turn on the lights before the meeting starts.

definitions.note: Often used for turning on a light or starting a flame.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela acende a luz da sala.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She turns on the living room light.

definitions.note: Gerund form ("-ing"); often used with "estar" to mean "to be turning on / lighting".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estou acendendo a luz da sala.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m turning on the living room light.

definitions.note: Often used for turning on lights or lighting a fire/cigarette.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vou acender a luz da sala.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to turn on the living room light.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles acenderam a luz quando escureceu.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They turned on the light when it got dark.

definitions.note: Imperfect subjunctive form of "acender", often used after phrases like "era importante que…" ("it was important that…").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Era importante que eu acendesse a luz.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It was important that I turned on the light.

definitions.note: Past tense (pretérito perfeito) of "acender".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela acendeu a luz da sala.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She turned on the living room light.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito perfeito) of "acender".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Acendi a luz do corredor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I turned on the hallway light.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela acenou para mim do outro lado da rua.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She waved to me from the other side of the street.

definitions.note: Also used for the written accent mark on a letter in Portuguese (e.g., ´, ˆ, ~).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela tem um acento forte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has a strong accent.

definitions.note: Often used in the fixed phrase “acerca de” (about).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Falamos acerca do trabalho ontem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We talked about work yesterday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela sempre acerta as respostas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She always gets the answers right.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele acerta o alvo na primeira tentativa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He hits the target on the first try.

definitions.note: Past participle of "acertar"; often used like an adjective to mean something is correct.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O cálculo está acertado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The calculation is correct.

definitions.native: we got (it) right, we guessed correctly
definitions.note: Can be either present ("we get it right") or past ("we got it right"), depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Acertamos a resposta na prova.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We got the answer right on the test.

definitions.note: Often used when you agree on a plan/time (e.g., an appointment).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Acertamos o horário da reunião.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We agreed on the time of the meeting.

definitions.native: to get right, to hit (a target)
definitions.note: Often used for getting something correct (an answer) or hitting a target.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele conseguiu acertar a resposta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He managed to get the answer right.

definitions.note: Common in phrases like "acertar detalhes" or "acertar uma data" (to settle/agree on details or a date).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vamos acertar os detalhes amanhã.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let’s settle the details tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles acertaram a resposta na prova.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They got the answer right on the test.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os jogadores acertaram a bola várias vezes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The players hit the ball several times.

definitions.note: Often used as an imperative (e.g., telling someone to get an answer right or to hit a target).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Acerte a resposta antes de enviar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Get the answer right before submitting.

definitions.native: I got it right, I hit it
definitions.note: Past (preterite) form meaning “I (did)”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Acertei a resposta na prova.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I got the answer right on the test.

definitions.note: Past tense (he/she/you formal/it) of "acertar"; often used for answers, guesses, or aiming at a target.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Você acertou a resposta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You got the answer right.

definitions.note: Feminine form; often used for lights or flames (e.g., “a luz está acesa”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A luz da cozinha está acesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The kitchen light is on.

definitions.note: Often used to talk about lights or candles being on.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: As luzes estão acesas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The lights are on.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Você pode acessar o site pelo celular.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You can access the website on your phone.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Você tem acesso à internet aqui?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you have access to the internet here?

definitions.note: Common on signs/labels, especially in phrases like “acesso principal” (main entrance).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O acesso principal fica do lado esquerdo do prédio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The main entrance is on the left side of the building.

definitions.note: often used to give or ask for an opinion
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela acha que o filme começa às oito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She thinks the movie starts at eight.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Depois de procurar um pouco, ele acha a chave.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After looking for a bit, he finds the key.

definitions.note: feminine form; used as the past participle of "achar" (e.g., with "ser" or "estar")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A carteira foi achada no parque.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The wallet was found in the park.

definitions.note: Past participle of "achar"; often used with "ser/estar" (e.g., "foi achado" = "was found").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O documento foi achado ontem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The document was found yesterday.

definitions.note: Present tense, 3rd person plural of "achar" (they/you plural think; they/you plural find).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles acham que vai chover hoje.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They think it’s going to rain today.

definitions.note: From the verb "achar"; often used to express an opinion ("to think").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Achamos que este restaurante é muito bom.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We think this restaurant is very good.

definitions.note: Present participle/gerund of "achar"; often used to mean "thinking" (opinion) or "finding" (discovering/locating), depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estou achando que ele vai se atrasar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I think he’s going to be late.

definitions.note: Very common in everyday speech to express an opinion (“I think…”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu achar que ele está em casa, mas não ter certeza.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I think he is at home, but I'm not sure.

definitions.note: Used for finding something (by searching or by discovery).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu achar minhas chaves no sofá.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I found my keys on the couch.

definitions.note: Past (preterite) form of "achar" used with "eles/elas/vocês".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles acharam as chaves no sofá.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They found the keys on the couch.

definitions.note: Future tense (1st person singular) of "achar"; often used for physical or factual “find.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Acharei minhas chaves depois do almoço.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will find my keys after lunch.

definitions.note: Future tense (1st person singular) of "achar"; very common in Portuguese meaning “to think/consider” (not “to achieve”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Acharei que essa é a melhor solução.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will think that this is the best solution.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive, 3rd person plural (used after expressions like “é possível que”, “talvez”, etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: É possível que eles acharem o caminho sozinhos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s possible that they find the way on their own.

definitions.note: Future tense (nós).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Acho que acharemos a solução amanhã.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I think we will find the solution tomorrow.

definitions.note: Future tense (nós). Used with this meaning in expressions like “achar que...” (= “to think that...”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Acharemos que foi a melhor decisão.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We will think it was the best decision.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu acharia isso estranho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would find that strange.

definitions.note: Usually the personal infinitive of "achar" (used after prepositions or expressions like "para" / "antes de"); can also be the future subjunctive "if/when we find" depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: É melhor acharmos uma solução juntos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s better for us to find a solution together.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se procurar bem, você achará as chaves.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you look carefully, you will find the keys.

definitions.note: Often used to express an opinion (similar to “to think”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele achará a ideia interessante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He will think the idea is interesting.

definitions.note: Second-person singular (tu) present tense of "achar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu achas que vai chover hoje?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you think it’s going to rain today?

definitions.note: Past (preterite) form of "achar" used with "tu" (informal "you").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Achaste as chaves?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Did you find the keys?

definitions.note: Imperfect past of "achar" (used for ongoing/repeated past actions or background description).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu achava que ele ia chegar mais cedo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I thought he was going to arrive earlier.

definitions.note: Imperfect past tense (they). Often means “thought” in everyday speech; can also mean “found” (discovered).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles achavam que o filme ia ser chato, mas gostaram muito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They thought the movie was going to be boring, but they liked it a lot.

definitions.note: Past tense (pretérito perfeito) of the verb “achar” in the 1st person singular: “eu achei” = “I found / I thought” depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu achei minhas chaves no sofá.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I found my keys on the couch.

definitions.note: Also from “achar”; in the past tense, “eu achei” often means “I thought” (opinion/impression).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu achei que você ia chegar mais cedo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I thought you were going to arrive earlier.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito perfeito), 1st person singular of "achar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Achei minhas chaves no sofá.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I found my keys on the couch.

definitions.note: Often used to express an opinion or guess ("I thought / I figured"). Simple past (pretérito perfeito), 1st person singular of "achar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Achei que você ia chegar mais cedo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I thought you were going to arrive earlier.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (vocês/eles/elas) of "achar"; often used after expressions like "Espero que..." or "É possível que...".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que achem uma solução rápida.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope they find a quick solution.

definitions.note: often used to give an opinion, as in “I think”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Acho que ele tem razão.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I think he is right.

definitions.note: in the sense of locating or discovering something
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sempre acho minhas chaves no sofá.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I always find my keys on the couch.

definitions.note: Simple past (ele/ela/você) of “achar”. In many contexts it can also mean “thought” (as in giving an opinion).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela achou as chaves no sofá.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She found the keys on the couch.

definitions.native: thought, found (in the sense of an opinion)
definitions.note: Used to express what someone thought/considered (ele/ela/você in the simple past).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu perguntei, e ele achou a ideia boa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I asked, and he thought the idea was good.

definitions.note: Informal/colloquial spelling of “achar” (dropping the final -r), common in some speech and in lyrics or casual writing.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vou achá a chave.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to find the key.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense; can also mean “used to think/believe.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nós achávamos que ele ia chegar cedo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We thought he was going to arrive early.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Desculpa, eu te liguei acidentalmente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Sorry, I called you accidentally.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Houve um acidente na estrada esta manhã.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There was an accident on the road this morning.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Houve muitos acidentes na estrada por causa da chuva.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There were many accidents on the road because of the rain.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O quadro está acima da cama.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The painting is above the bed.

definitions.native: to activate; to switch on; to trigger
definitions.note: Common with devices/mechanisms (e.g., alarm, button, lever): 'acionar' = make it operate.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ao ver fumaça, ele decidiu acionar o alarme.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When he saw smoke, he decided to activate the alarm.

definitions.note: Often used with 'acionar o freio', 'acionar uma alavanca', 'acionar o motor' (engage/operate).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Para parar o carro, ela precisou acionar o freio de mão.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: To stop the car, she needed to engage the handbrake.

definitions.note: Very common in formal/news contexts: 'acionar a polícia', 'acionar os bombeiros', 'acionar a assistência'.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Diante do acidente, eles foram acionar a polícia imediatamente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Given the accident, they went to call the police immediately.

definitions.note: Legal usage: 'acionar alguém na Justiça' = bring a lawsuit against someone.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A empresa decidiu acionar o fornecedor na Justiça por quebra de contrato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The company decided to sue the supplier for breach of contract.

definitions.note: Often used for putting things/people in a comfortable or suitable position (e.g., seats, objects).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vou acomodar os livros na estante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to arrange the books on the shelf.

definitions.note: In contexts like adjusting/adapting to someone’s needs or making room for someone.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O hotel consegue acomodar até cem hóspedes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The hotel can accommodate up to one hundred guests.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela acompanha a irmã até a escola.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She accompanies her sister to school.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele acompanha as notícias todos os dias.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He follows the news every day.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele chegou acompanhado da irmã.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He arrived accompanied by his sister.

definitions.native: with a side dish, served with something
definitions.note: Common on menus to indicate a dish comes with another item (like rice, salad, fries, etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O frango vem acompanhado de arroz e salada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The chicken comes with rice and salad.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele chegou acompanhado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He arrived accompanied.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O frango vem com acompanhamento de arroz e salada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The chicken comes with a side dish of rice and salad.

definitions.note: Often used for ongoing support or checking progress (e.g., medical or project follow-up).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela faz acompanhamento médico todos os meses.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has medical follow-ups every month.

definitions.note: Often refers to someone who goes with another person for company or assistance (e.g., at an event, appointment, or on a trip).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela foi ao médico com um acompanhante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She went to the doctor with a companion.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vou acompanhar você até a estação.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to accompany you to the station.

definitions.native: to follow, to keep up with
definitions.note: Often used for following news, a series, instructions, or someone’s progress.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu vou acompanhar as notícias todos os dias.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to follow the news every day.

definitions.note: Third-person singular future tense (ele/ela/você).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela acompanhará o amigo ao médico amanhã.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She will accompany her friend to the doctor tomorrow.

definitions.note: Imperfect subjunctive of "acompanhar"; often used after expressions like "se" (if) or "como se" (as if).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se ela me acompanhasse, eu me sentiria mais seguro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If she accompanied me, I would feel safer.

definitions.note: Often used as a command or suggestion (e.g., “Follow me/us”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Acompanhe o guia até a saída.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Follow the guide to the exit.

definitions.note: Often used as a polite invitation or request.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Por favor, acompanhe-me até a recepção.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please come with me to the reception desk.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Acompanhei minha amiga até a estação.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I accompanied my friend to the station.

definitions.note: Often used for keeping up with something (news, a story, a process) or going with someone.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu acompanho as notícias todos os dias.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I follow the news every day.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela acompanhou o amigo até a estação.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She accompanied her friend to the station.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele acompanhou as notícias durante a semana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He kept track of the news during the week.

definitions.note: Informal (especially Brazilian Portuguese) spelling/pronunciation of "acompanhar" (dropping the final -r in the infinitive).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vou acompanhá até a porta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll walk you to the door.

definitions.note: Often used for places or atmospheres (e.g., a room, a home, a café).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este apartamento é muito aconchegante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This apartment is very cozy.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela aconselha o aluno a estudar todos os dias.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She advises the student to study every day.

definitions.note: Often used in impersonal/passive constructions like “é aconselhado...” (“it is advised/recommended...”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Não é aconselhado nadar aqui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It is not advised to swim here.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu vou te aconselhar a descansar um pouco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to advise you to rest a little.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu aconselhei o meu amigo a descansar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I advised my friend to rest.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu aconselho você a descansar um pouco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I advise you to rest a bit.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela me aconselhou a descansar mais.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She advised me to rest more.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Isso acontece todos os dias.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That happens every day.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Coisas estranhas acontecem à noite.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Strange things happen at night.

definitions.note: Present participle/gerund of “acontecer”; often used with “estar” to mean “to be happening.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O que está acontecendo aqui?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What is happening here?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O que vai acontecer amanhã?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What is going to happen tomorrow?

definitions.note: Literary/formal; this is the simple pluperfect (mais-que-perfeito simples). In everyday speech, Portuguese usually uses “tinha acontecido”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quando eu cheguei, isso já acontecera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I arrived, that had already happened.

definitions.note: Can also be the future subjunctive form, often used after words like “se” (if) or “quando” (when): “se/quando isso acontecera” ≈ “if/when that happens”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se isso acontecera, ligue para mim.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If that happens, call me.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), 3rd person plural (they/you all).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Muitas coisas aconteceram ontem à noite.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Many things happened last night.

definitions.note: Conditional form (often used for hypotheticals).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu achei que isso aconteceria ontem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I thought that would happen yesterday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O evento acontecerá amanhã à noite.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The event will happen tomorrow night.

definitions.note: Past subjunctive (imperfect subjunctive) of “acontecer”; often used after expressions like “se” (if) or to talk about a hypothetical past situation.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se isso acontecesse, eu ficaria muito preocupado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If that happened, I would be very worried.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O acidente aconteceu perto da estação.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The accident happened near the station.

definitions.note: Imperfect past (pretérito imperfeito): describes an ongoing/repeated past action or background situation.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quando eu chegava em casa, isso acontecia sempre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I got home, that always happened.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nada disso tinha acontecido antes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: None of that had happened before.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Houve muitos acontecimentos importantes este ano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There were many important events this year.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive form of "acontecer" (used after expressions of doubt, desire, possibility, etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que isso não aconteça.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope that doesn't happen.

definitions.note: Often used for mechanical/technical contexts (joining parts together).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A acoplagem entre o motor e a bomba precisa ser ajustada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The coupling between the motor and the pump needs to be adjusted.

definitions.note: Often used for attaching or joining parts/devices together.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Você pode acoplar o reboque ao carro?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you couple the trailer to the car?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele sempre acorda cedo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He always wakes up early.

definitions.note: Informal command (tu).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Acorda! Já é tarde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Wake up! It’s already late.

definitions.note: feminine singular form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela está acordada desde cedo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has been awake since early.

definitions.note: feminine plural form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: As crianças já estão acordadas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The children are already awake.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estou acordado desde cedo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ve been awake since early.

definitions.note: Often used with verbs like estar/ficar (e.g., estar acordado = to be awake).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu estou acordado desde as seis.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ve been awake since six o’clock.

definitions.note: Used when something has been agreed on (often in contexts like “como foi acordado” = “as agreed”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O preço foi acordado ontem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The price was agreed on yesterday.

definitions.note: masculine plural; often used with verbs like "estar" (to be)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: As crianças ainda estão acordados.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The kids are still awake.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles acordam cedo todos os dias.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They wake up early every day.

definitions.note: Often used with a preposition, e.g. "acordar com" (agree with) or "acordar em" (agree on).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles acordam com a proposta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They agree with the proposal.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estou acordando agora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m waking up now.

definitions.note: Often used with "com" (e.g., "acordando com você").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estamos acordando com a proposta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re agreeing with the proposal.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu preciso acordar cedo amanhã.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to wake up early tomorrow.

definitions.note: Often used with “com” (to agree with someone) or “em” (to agree on something).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Precisamos acordar em um preço justo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need to agree on a fair price.

definitions.note: Third-person plural (they/you all) in the simple past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles acordaram cedo para pegar o ônibus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They woke up early to catch the bus.

definitions.native: used to wake up, was waking up
definitions.note: Imperfect past (ongoing/habitual action in the past).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu acordava cedo todos os dias.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I used to wake up early every day.

definitions.note: Used as a command (imperative) or in the present subjunctive (e.g., after expressions like “I hope that…”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Acorde cedo amanhã, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Wake up early tomorrow, please.

definitions.note: First-person singular (eu) in the simple past (pretérito perfeito).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Acordei cedo hoje.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I woke up early today.

definitions.note: Used for commands to a group (“Wake up!”) and also in the present subjunctive (“that they/you all wake up”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Acordem cedo amanhã.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Wake up early tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu acordo cedo todos os dias.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I wake up early every day.

definitions.note: Often used with “com” (acordo com você = I agree with you).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu acordo com você.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I agree with you.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Chegámos a um acordo sobre o preço.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We reached an agreement on the price.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), 3rd person singular of “acordar” (he/she/it woke up).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele acordou cedo hoje.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He woke up early today.

definitions.note: Common in informal speech/writing as a shortened form of “acordar” (especially in some Brazilian Portuguese varieties).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu preciso acordá cedo amanhã.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to wake up early tomorrow.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular of “acostumar”. Often used with an infinitive to express a habitual action.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela acostuma acordar cedo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She usually wakes up early.

definitions.note: feminine form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela já está acostumada a acordar cedo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is already used to waking up early.

definitions.note: Often followed by “a” + infinitive or noun (e.g., “acostumado a acordar cedo”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estou acostumado a acordar cedo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m used to waking up early.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles já estão acostumados ao frio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are already used to the cold.

definitions.native: getting used to, getting accustomed to
definitions.note: Gerund form of "acostumar"; often used with "a" before a verb (e.g., "acostumando a acordar cedo").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estou me acostumando ao novo trabalho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m getting used to the new job.

definitions.native: to get used to, to become accustomed to
definitions.note: Often used with “a” + infinitive or “a” + noun/pronoun (e.g., “acostumar-se a…” = “to get used to…”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu preciso me acostumar a acordar cedo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to get used to waking up early.

definitions.native: get used to, become accustomed to
definitions.note: Often used with "se" ("acostumar-se a") to mean "to get used to."
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que você se acostume ao novo trabalho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you get used to the new job.

definitions.native: I got used to, I became accustomed to
definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito perfeito) of "acostumar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu me acostumei com o clima daqui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I got used to the weather here.

definitions.native: got used to, became accustomed to
definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito perfeito) of "acostumar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela se acostumou ao novo trabalho rapidamente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She got used to the new job quickly.

definitions.note: Usually used with ele/ela/você (present tense).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela acredita em você.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She believes in you.

definitions.note: 3rd person plural (they/you all) present tense of "acreditar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles acreditam que vai chover amanhã.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They believe it’s going to rain tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Acreditamos que tudo vai dar certo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We believe that everything will work out.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Acreditamos em você.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We trust you.

definitions.note: gerund form; often used like “believing” or “thinking” in English
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estou acreditando que vai dar tudo certo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m believing that everything will work out.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu vou acreditar em você.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will believe in you.

definitions.native: to think / to suppose (to believe something is true)
definitions.note: Common in phrases like “acreditar que…”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu posso acreditar que isso seja verdade.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can believe that this is true.

definitions.native: to trust / to have faith (in someone or something)
definitions.note: Often used with “acreditar em”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela decidiu acreditar no amigo apesar dos rumores.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She decided to trust her friend despite the rumors.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles acreditaram na história.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They believed the story.

definitions.note: Often used in sentences like “se eles acreditarem...” (“if they believe...”) or “para eles acreditarem...” (“for them to believe...”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se eles acreditarem em você, tudo fica mais fácil.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If they believe in you, everything becomes easier.

definitions.note: Conditional form (used for hypotheticals or polite statements).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu acreditaria em você se você dissesse a verdade.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would believe you if you told the truth.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela acreditará na sua história.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She will believe your story.

definitions.note: Common in phrases like “acreditar que…” to express an opinion or assumption.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu acreditará que ele chega cedo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will think that he arrives early.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular (tu) form; common in Portugal and in informal contexts where "tu" is used.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Acreditas mesmo nisso?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you really believe that?

definitions.note: Used in the imperfect subjunctive (often after “se” = “if”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se eu acreditasse em você, eu ajudaria.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If I believed you, I would help.

definitions.note: Imperfect past; can describe an ongoing belief in the past or a habitual belief (“used to believe”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu acreditava que ele ia chegar cedo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I believed he was going to arrive early.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (they/you-pl believed; also used for ongoing/habitual past).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles acreditavam que tudo ia dar certo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They believed that everything would work out.

definitions.note: Often used as a command (“Believe me!”) or as a polite form in phrases like “acredite em mim”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Acredite em mim, vai dar tudo certo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Believe me, everything will work out.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito perfeito), 1st person singular.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Acreditei na sua história.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I believed your story.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (vocês/eles/elas) or affirmative command (vocês) of "acreditar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Acreditem em mim, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Believe me, please.

definitions.note: Present tense (eu). Often used to express an opinion or belief.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Acredito que ele está certo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I believe (that) he is right.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela acreditou na história dele.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She believed his story.

definitions.note: Imperfect past (we used to believe / we were believing), often used for ongoing or habitual past actions.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nós acreditávamos que tudo ia dar certo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We believed that everything was going to work out.

definitions.note: Often used for adding extra information, details, or items.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quero acrescentar uma coisa antes de terminar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to add one thing before finishing.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito perfeito) of “acrescentar” in the “eu” form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu acrescentei mais sal à sopa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I added more salt to the soup.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela acrescentou açúcar ao café.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She added sugar to the coffee.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estamos acumulando dinheiro para a viagem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We are accumulating money for the trip.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele acumulou muitas dívidas durante o ano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He accumulated a lot of debt during the year.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela faz acupuntura para aliviar a dor nas costas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She does acupuncture to relieve back pain.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O acusado falou com o advogado antes do julgamento.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The defendant spoke with the lawyer before the trial.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O homem acusado negou tudo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The accused man denied everything.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele foi acusado de roubo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was accused of theft.

definitions.note: Present participle/gerund of "acusar"; often used with "estar" to describe an ongoing action.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele está me acusando de mentir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is accusing me of lying.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele vai acusar o colega de roubo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is going to accuse his colleague of theft.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles acusaram o motorista de dirigir bêbado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They accused the driver of driving drunk.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A acusação contra ele foi retirada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The charge against him was dropped.

definitions.note: Often used in legal contexts; can also refer to non-legal allegations.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: As acusações contra ele foram retiradas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The charges against him were dropped.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu te acuso de mentir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I accuse you of lying.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele acusou o vizinho de roubo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He accused the neighbor of theft.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When there is a problem, we act quickly.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is acting strangely today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Em agosto, muita gente vai de férias.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope the food pleases everyone.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O filme agradou muita gente.

definitions.native: enduring, holding on, putting up with

definitions.note: Used to encourage someone or urge them to do something (common in European Portuguese).
