definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Por favor, pare de me chatear.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please stop bothering me.

definitions.note: Often used informally to complain about something or someone that is annoying or a hassle.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Que chatice ter que esperar tanto tempo!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What an annoyance to have to wait so long!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O filme foi muito chato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The movie was very boring.

definitions.note: Common in informal speech; can sound rude depending on tone.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Não convida o Pedro; ele é um chato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t invite Pedro; he’s a boring/annoying guy.

definitions.note: Plural form; used to describe people/things (masculine or mixed group).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Esses filmes são muito chatos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Those movies are very boring.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Perdi a chave de casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I lost the house key.

definitions.note: In Brazilian Portuguese, "chave" is also commonly used in tool names, like "chave de fenda" (screwdriver) and "chave inglesa" (adjustable wrench).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Você tem uma chave para apertar esse parafuso?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you have a wrench to tighten this screw?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Comprei um chaveiro novo para as chaves de casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought a new keychain for my house keys.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O chaveiro abriu a porta em poucos minutos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The locksmith opened the door in a few minutes.

definitions.note: Plural of "chave".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Onde estão as chaves do carro?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Where are the car keys?

definitions.note: Also commonly means “we check (something) out” in Brazilian Portuguese.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Checamos os documentos antes de assinar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We check the documents before signing.

definitions.note: Common in Brazilian Portuguese; in some contexts you can also use "verificar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vou checar o e-mail antes de sair.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to check the email before leaving.

definitions.note: Loanword from English; in Portuguese this is often written as “cheque”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele pagou com um check.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He paid with a check.

definitions.note: Nationality/demonym; can also be used as an adjective (“Czech”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O checo mora em Praga.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The Czech man lives in Prague.

definitions.note: Informal; from the verb “checar” (common in Brazilian Portuguese).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele checou o e-mail antes de sair.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He checked the email before leaving.

definitions.note: In Brazil, very common meaning is “boss” in workplaces. It can also mean “chief” (leader) more generally.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vou falar com o meu chefe depois do almoço.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'll talk to my boss after lunch.

definitions.note: Often used as a noun meaning “boss” or “manager.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este é o ingrediente chefe da receita.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This is the main ingredient in the recipe.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Meu chefe chega cedo todos os dias.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My boss arrives early every day.

definitions.note: Plural of "chefe".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os chefes estão em uma reunião agora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bosses are in a meeting right now.

definitions.note: Often refers to the people in charge (e.g., your bosses) or the act/role of leading.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A chefia pediu para entregarmos o relatório até sexta-feira.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Management asked us to submit the report by Friday.

definitions.note: Informal; can be used literally (at work) or jokingly/ironically.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O chefão chegou cedo hoje.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The big boss arrived early today.

definitions.note: Third-person singular present of "chegar"; can also be used for "you arrive/come" with "você".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O ônibus chega às oito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bus arrives at eight.

definitions.note: Common as an interjection meaning “that’s enough/stop.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Chega, eu já entendi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Enough, I already understood.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A chegada do ônibus foi atrasada por causa do trânsito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bus’s arrival was delayed because of traffic.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele tinha chegado cedo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He had arrived early.

definitions.note: Often used (especially in Brazil) to talk about people who are close to each other, like close friends.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles são muito chegados.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are very close (friends).

definitions.note: Third-person plural present of "chegar" (they arrive / you all arrive).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles chegam às oito todos os dias.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They arrive at eight every day.

definitions.note: Past (preterite) form of "chegar" with "we" (nós).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Chegamos ao aeroporto bem cedo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We arrived at the airport very early.

definitions.note: Present participle/gerund of "chegar"; often used after "estar" to mean "is/are arriving" or "is/are coming".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estou chegando em casa agora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m arriving home now.

definitions.note: Often used with a destination: chegar a/em algum lugar = to arrive at/in a place.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero chegar cedo ao trabalho amanhã.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope to arrive at work early tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles chegaram cedo ao aeroporto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They arrived early at the airport.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Chegarei cedo para a reunião.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will arrive early for the meeting.

definitions.note: Personal infinitive of "chegar" used after certain conjunctions/prepositions; typically means "(for them) to arrive" depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vamos esperar eles chegarem antes de começar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re going to wait for them to arrive before starting.

definitions.native: we will arrive, we will get there
definitions.note: First-person plural ("we") in the future tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Chegaremos ao aeroporto às oito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We will arrive at the airport at eight.

definitions.note: Conditional form of "chegar" (used for hypotheticals or polite statements).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu chegaria mais cedo se não houvesse trânsito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would arrive earlier if there weren’t traffic.

definitions.note: Often used after time/condition words like "quando" (when) or "se" (if), referring to a future situation.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quando chegarmos, eu te ligo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When we arrive, I'll call you.

definitions.note: Personal infinitive; often used after prepositions like "para" (in order to) or "até" (until).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vamos sair cedo para chegarmos a tempo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let's leave early so we can arrive on time.

definitions.note: Future tense (ele/ela/você).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O trem chegará às oito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The train will arrive at eight.

definitions.note: Future tense (ele/ela/você). Often used with "a" (e.g., chegar a algum lugar).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela chegará ao aeroporto cedo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She will get to the airport early.

definitions.note: Third-person plural (they/you all) simple future of “chegar”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles chegarão amanhã de manhã.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They will arrive tomorrow morning.

definitions.note: Imperfect subjunctive of "chegar"; used after expressions like "if" or "I wanted that" to talk about a hypothetical/desired past situation.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se ele chegasse mais cedo, nós sairíamos juntos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If he arrived earlier, we would go out together.

definitions.note: Second-person singular (tu) form; common in European Portuguese and in some regions of Brazil.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Chegaste tarde ontem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You arrived late yesterday.

definitions.note: Imperfect past (used for ongoing, habitual, or background actions in the past).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu chegava em casa por volta das seis todos os dias.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I arrived home around six every day.

definitions.native: I arrive, I get (to), I reach
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu chego em casa às seis.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I get home at six.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela chegou cedo à escola.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She arrived at school early.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive of "chegar" (also used for formal commands).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que você chegue cedo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you arrive early.

definitions.note: First-person singular in the past (pretérito perfeito) of "chegar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cheguei em casa às oito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I got home at eight.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (vocês/eles/elas) and also the affirmative command for vocês.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que cheguem a tempo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope they arrive on time.

definitions.note: Used in the present subjunctive (often after que) and in the affirmative imperative meaning “let’s arrive / let’s get there.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que cheguemos cedo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope we arrive early.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A garrafa está cheia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bottle is full.

definitions.note: Used especially in the expression “cheia do rio” (river flood).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A cheia do rio alagou a cidade.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The river flood flooded the city.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form of “cheio”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: As garrafas estão cheias de água.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bottles are full of water.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O copo está cheio de água.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The glass is full of water.

definitions.note: Used as a noun; often refers to the state of being full or the “full” side/part (e.g., in contrasts like “the full and the empty”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No tanque, o cheio indica o nível máximo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the tank, the full mark indicates the maximum level.

definitions.note: Plural masculine form of "cheio" (used with masculine plural nouns, or mixed-gender groups).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os copos estão cheios de água.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cups are full of water.

definitions.note: Usually used with "a" + noun: "cheira a" = "smells like".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este queijo cheira a mofo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This cheese smells like mold.

definitions.note: 3rd person plural (they/you all) of “cheirar”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: As flores cheiram bem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The flowers smell good.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O cachorro está cheirando o chão.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog is sniffing the ground.

definitions.note: Can mean either to sense an odor (with your nose) or to have a smell (give off an odor).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este queijo está a cheirar mal.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This cheese smells bad.

definitions.note: Imperfect past (used for ongoing, habitual, or background actions in the past).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A cozinha cheirava a pão fresco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The kitchen smelled like fresh bread.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive form of "cheirar" (also used in some formal commands, e.g., "Cheire isto.").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que eu cheire melhor amanhã.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope I smell better tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu cheiro as flores no jardim.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I smell the flowers in the garden.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Que cheiro bom de café!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What a nice smell of coffee!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gosto dos cheiros das flores na primavera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like the smells of the flowers in spring.

definitions.note: Often used as a formal command (for você), meaning “check/verify.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cheque as informações antes de confirmar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Check the information before confirming.

definitions.note: In Brazilian Portuguese, people often write "cheque" as "cheque"; in English, "cheque" is the British spelling.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele pagou com um cheque.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He paid with a check.

definitions.note: Past tense (pretérito perfeito), 1st-person singular.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu chequei meu e-mail antes de sair.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I checked my email before leaving.

definitions.note: Brazilian Portuguese spelling; European Portuguese often uses “cheques” as the standard plural spelling.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Preciso depositar estes cheques no banco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to deposit these checks at the bank.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Você tem um chiclete?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you have any chewing gum?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O cavaleiro carregava um chicote.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The rider was carrying a whip.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O boi tem chifres grandes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The ox has big horns.

definitions.note: Plural of "chifre".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O veado tem chifres grandes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The deer has big horns.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O chimpanzé comeu uma banana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The chimpanzee ate a banana.

definitions.note: Often refers to casual open footwear (like flip-flops).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Não esqueça de levar os chinelos para a piscina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t forget to bring your flip-flops to the pool.

definitions.note: feminine singular form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela é chinesa e mora no Brasil.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is Chinese and lives in Brazil.

definitions.note: feminine plural form (used for women or feminine plural nouns)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: As estudantes chinesas falam português muito bem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The Chinese students speak Portuguese very well.

definitions.note: plural masculine form of the adjective (also used for mixed-gender groups)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os restaurantes chineses desta rua são muito bons.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The Chinese restaurants on this street are very good.

definitions.note: Plural of "chinês"; can refer to a group of Chinese people (often men/mixed group depending on context).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Há muitos chineses morando aqui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are many Chinese people living here.

definitions.note: Can describe something from China or the Chinese language; as an adjective it agrees in gender/number with the noun it modifies.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu estudo chinês na escola.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I study Chinese at school.

definitions.note: Can refer to a Chinese person or, in some contexts, the Chinese language; here it’s used as a noun for a person.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O chinês mora aqui há dois anos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The Chinese man has lived here for two years.

definitions.note: As a noun, it can also mean the Chinese language.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu estou aprendendo chinês na escola.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am learning Chinese at school.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela estava muito chique na festa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She looked very chic at the party.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O chiqueiro fica atrás do celeiro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The pigsty is behind the barn.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela ficou chocada com a notícia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She was shocked by the news.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Fiquei chocado com a notícia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was shocked by the news.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A notícia foi chocante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The news was shocking.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu gosto de chocolate.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like chocolate.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Comprei chocolates para a festa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought chocolates for the party.

definitions.note: Often used with the sense of emotionally shocking/offending someone; can also mean causing a collision (crashed).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A notícia chocou muita gente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The news shocked a lot of people.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O acidente causou um choque entre dois carros.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The accident caused a collision between two cars.

definitions.note: Present tense form of “chorar” (to cry).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela chora quando vê filmes tristes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She cries when she watches sad movies.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu tenho chorado muito ultimamente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have cried a lot lately.

definitions.note: Present tense (they/you all cry).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: As crianças choram quando estão cansadas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The children cry when they are tired.

definitions.note: Can be present indicative (“we cry”) or simple past/preterite (“we cried”), depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ontem, choramos no fim do filme.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday, we cried at the end of the movie.

definitions.note: present participle/gerund of "chorar"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela está chorando porque perdeu o celular.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is crying because she lost her phone.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela começou a chorar quando ouviu a notícia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She started to cry when she heard the news.

definitions.note: Imperfect past (ação habitual ou contínua no passado).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quando eu era criança, eu chorava quando perdia meu brinquedo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I was a child, I used to cry when I lost my toy.

definitions.note: Don’t confuse with the English word “chore” (task).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que ela chore hoje.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope she cries today.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito perfeito) of "chorar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu chorei quando vi o filme.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I cried when I watched the movie.

definitions.note: Present tense (eu): “I cry” / “I weep”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Às vezes eu choro quando vejo um filme triste.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Sometimes I cry when I watch a sad movie.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O choro do bebê acordou todo mundo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The baby's crying woke everyone up.

definitions.note: Simple past (ele/ela/você).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele chorou no final do filme.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He cried at the end of the movie.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive of "chover"; used after expressions of doubt, desire, or conditions (e.g., "Espero que...").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que chova amanhã.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope it rains tomorrow.

definitions.note: 3rd-person singular present of "chover"; in Portuguese this verb is usually used impersonally (no real subject).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hoje chove o dia todo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It rains all day today.

definitions.note: Present participle/gerund of "chover"; commonly used with "estar" (e.g., "está chovendo").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Está chovendo muito hoje.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s raining a lot today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hoje vai chover à tarde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It's going to rain this afternoon.

definitions.note: Third-person singular future tense of "chover".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Amanhã choverá à tarde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow it will rain in the afternoon.

definitions.note: Past tense (preterite) of "chover"; often used impersonally (without a subject).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ontem choveu muito na cidade.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday it rained a lot in the city.

definitions.note: Imperfect past of "chover"; often used for ongoing or habitual past weather.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quando saí de casa, chovia muito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I left home, it was raining a lot.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tem chovido muito esta semana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It has rained a lot this week.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu gosto de chucrute no sanduíche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like sauerkraut on my sandwich.

definitions.note: Informal/slang.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Depois da caminhada, fiquei com um chulé terrível.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the walk, I had terrible foot odor.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O cano antigo é feito de chumbo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The old pipe is made of lead.

definitions.note: Also commonly used in casual speech as an insult/taunt (e.g., “Chupa!” = “Suck it!”), which is vulgar.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O bebê chupa o dedo para se acalmar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The baby sucks his thumb to calm down.

definitions.note: Often used for sucking something (like candy or a wound) or for sucking liquid through a straw.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O bebê gosta de chupar o dedo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The baby likes to suck its thumb.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele chupou um pirulito depois do almoço.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He sucked on a lollipop after lunch.

definitions.note: Especially common in Brazil; can refer both to the grilled meat and to the social event.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No domingo, fizemos um churrasco com a família.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: On Sunday, we had a barbecue with the family.

definitions.note: Often refers to a built-in or designated barbecue area (especially in Brazil/Portugal), not just a small portable grill.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vamos fazer carne na churrasqueira hoje à noite.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re going to cook meat on the grill tonight.

definitions.note: Also used informally to mean “take a guess.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele chuta a bola para o gol.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He kicks the ball toward the goal.

definitions.note: Informal; common in Brazilian Portuguese.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se você não sabe, chuta!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you don’t know, take a guess!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele está chutando a bola no quintal.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is kicking the ball in the backyard.

definitions.note: Informal (especially in Brazil): used when you don’t really know the answer and you’re taking a guess.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Não sei a resposta, estou chutando.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t know the answer; I’m guessing.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele vai chutar a bola para o gol.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is going to kick the ball toward the goal.

definitions.note: Common in informal speech, often used with "um palpite" (a guess).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se você não souber a resposta, pode chutar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you don’t know the answer, you can guess.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Chute a bola!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Kick the ball!

definitions.note: Informal: often used to mean “guess” (as in making a quick guess).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Chute um número de 1 a 10.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Guess a number from 1 to 10.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele deu um chute na bola.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: As crianças se comportaram bem na escola.

definitions.note: First-person singular (eu) present tense of "comprar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu compro pão na padaria todos os dias.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I buy bread at the bakery every day.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They know the city very well.

definitions.note: Usually means either (1) “we know” (a person/thing) or (2) “we met” (someone) depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nós conhecemos bem esta cidade.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We know this city well.

definitions.native: to know, to be familiar with
definitions.note: Used for knowing a person/place/thing or being familiar with something (not for knowing a fact).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quero conhecer bem esta cidade.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to know this city well.

definitions.note: Often used in the sense of meeting someone for the first time (e.g., “conhecer alguém”).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It was a pleasure to meet you.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles conheceram a professora ontem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They met the teacher yesterday.

definitions.note: Present tense (tu form).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu conheces a Maria?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you know Maria?

definitions.note: Imperfect subjunctive form; often used after “se” to mean “if (someone) knew.”

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If I knew the answer, I would tell you.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito perfeito) of “conhecer” for he/she/you (formal) / it.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela conheceu o marido na universidade.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She met her husband at university.

definitions.native: I met, I got to know
definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito perfeito) of “conhecer” (first-person singular).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu conheci a Ana ontem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I met Ana yesterday.

definitions.note: Imperfect past tense (used for ongoing/habitual past actions or background).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu conhecia bem aquela cidade quando era criança.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I knew that city well when I was a child.

definitions.note: Imperfect past tense (they/you plural) of “conhecer”; can also mean “used to know” or “were knowing” depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles conheciam a cidade muito bem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They knew the city very well.

definitions.note: feminine singular form (used with feminine nouns, e.g. ‘uma pessoa conhecida’)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela é uma artista muito conhecida no Brasil.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is a very well-known artist in Brazil.

definitions.note: Past participle of “conhecer”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela é muito conhecida na cidade.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is very well known in the city.

definitions.note: Often used to mean “familiar” or “someone you know” depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele é bem conhecido na cidade.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is well-known in the city.

definitions.note: Past participle of "conhecer"; often used as an adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele é muito conhecido na cidade.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is very well known in the city.

definitions.note: As a noun, it means someone you know (not necessarily a close friend).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele é um conhecido do meu pai.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is an acquaintance of my father.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela tem muito conhecimento sobre história do Brasil.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has a lot of knowledge about the history of Brazil.

definitions.note: Often used in the phrase “fazer conhecimento” (to meet/get to know someone).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele é um conhecimento do meu irmão.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is an acquaintance of my brother.

definitions.note: Plural of "conhecimento"; often refers to someone’s knowledge/skills in general.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela tem conhecimentos de informática.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has knowledge of computers.

definitions.note: This is a shortened/contracted form of “conhecer” used before some attached object pronouns (e.g., conhecê-lo = to know/meet him).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quero conhecê-lo melhor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to get to know him better.

definitions.note: Imperfect past ("we" form), often used for ongoing past states or habits.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nós conhecíamos bem aquele bairro antes de nos mudarmos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We knew that neighborhood well before we moved.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (also the formal command: “(you) meet/get to know”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que você conheça meus pais amanhã.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you meet my parents tomorrow.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (vocês/eles/elas); often used in suggestions/requests like “que vocês…” or after expressions like “espero que…”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que vocês conheçam a cidade um dia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you (all) get to know the city one day.

definitions.note: Used for knowing people, places, or being familiar with something; for knowing facts or information, Portuguese often uses "saber" instead.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu conheço bem este bairro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I know this neighborhood well.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este conjunto de regras é importante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This set of rules is important.

definitions.note: Used after prepositions (e.g., “com”) and often in phrases like “venha conosco” (“come with us”).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Come with us to the park.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A conquista do campeonato foi muito comemorada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The championship win was widely celebrated.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles querem conquistar o campeonato este ano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They want to win the championship this year.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito perfeito) form of “conquistar” (he/she/it won; you [formal] won).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela conquistou o campeonato este ano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She won the championship this year.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estou consciente do problema.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m aware of the problem.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tenho a consciência tranquila.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a clear conscience.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela tem consciência dos riscos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is aware of the risks.

definitions.note: Plural masculine form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Trabalhei três dias consecutivos sem folga.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I worked three consecutive days without a day off.

definitions.native: can, is able to, manages to

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She can finish the work today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele consegue um desconto na loja.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He gets a discount at the store.

definitions.native: can, are able to, manage to
definitions.note: Third-person plural (they/you all) present tense of "conseguir".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles conseguem terminar o trabalho hoje.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They can finish the work today.

definitions.note: Second-person singular (tu) present tense form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Consegues ajudar-me com isto?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you help me with this?

definitions.native: I managed to, I was able to, I got

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Consegui terminar o trabalho a tempo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I managed to finish the work on time.

definitions.note: Imperfect past; often implies a repeated/ongoing ability in the past ("used to be able to").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quando eu morava lá, conseguia ir a pé para o trabalho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I lived there, I could walk to work.

definitions.note: Past participle of "conseguir"; often used with "ter/haver" (e.g., "tenho conseguido" = "have been managing to").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu tenho conseguido dormir melhor esta semana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have been managing to sleep better this week.

definitions.native: we can, we manage to, we succeed in
definitions.note: First-person plural ("we") form of "conseguir"; often used to say you are able to do something or achieve something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Conseguimos terminar o trabalho a tempo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We managed to finish the work on time.

definitions.note: Gerund form, often used with "estar" to describe something in progress.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estou conseguindo terminar o trabalho a tempo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm managing to finish the work on time.

definitions.native: to manage to; to succeed in (doing something)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Você vai conseguir terminar o trabalho a tempo?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Will you manage to finish the work on time?

definitions.native: to be able to; to get to (a state/condition)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Depois de muito treino, ele conseguiu correr cinco quilômetros sem parar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After a lot of training, he was able to run five kilometers without stopping.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu não consegui um ingresso para o show.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I couldn’t get a ticket for the concert.

definitions.native: to arrange; to secure (something through effort)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela conseguiu uma entrevista de emprego para a semana que vem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She secured a job interview for next week.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito perfeito) of "conseguir" for "they/you all".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles conseguiram terminar o trabalho a tempo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They managed to finish the work on time.

definitions.native: I will be able to, I will manage to

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will be able to finish the work today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se eles conseguirem terminar hoje, vamos comemorar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If they manage to finish today, we’ll celebrate.

definitions.native: we will be able to, we will manage to
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se trabalharmos juntos, conseguiremos terminar o projeto a tempo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If we work together, we will be able to finish the project on time.

definitions.note: Conditional form of "conseguir" (often used for polite requests or hypothetical situations).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Você conseguiria me ajudar com isso?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Could you help me with this?

definitions.native: will be able to, will manage to
definitions.note: Third-person singular future (ele/ela/você).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela conseguirá terminar o trabalho hoje.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She will be able to finish the work today.

definitions.native: will be able to, will manage to
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles conseguirão terminar o trabalho até amanhã.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They will be able to finish the work by tomorrow.

definitions.note: Imperfect subjunctive of "conseguir"; often used after expressions like "se" (if) or "queria que" (I wanted that).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If I could find time, I would travel more.

definitions.note: Informal singular (tu) preterite: completed action in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Conseguiste terminar o trabalho a tempo?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Did you manage to finish the work on time?

definitions.native: managed to, succeeded in, was able to
definitions.note: Simple past (ele/ela/você) of "conseguir".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela conseguiu terminar o trabalho a tempo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She managed to finish the work on time.

definitions.note: Imperfect past ("we" form): often implies an ongoing or habitual ability in the past, or something that was possible then.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When we were kids, we could swim to the other side of the river.

definitions.note: Often used for an official or trusted person who gives advice (e.g., a government or organizational advisor).

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A decisão teve uma consequência inesperada.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele teve que lidar com as consequências das suas escolhas.

definitions.note: Plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Precisamos pensar nas conseqüências antes de tomar uma decisão.

definitions.note: Present tense form (also used for affirmative commands with “você”).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He fixes the computer at home.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O computador já foi consertado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The computer has already been fixed.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O carro já está consertado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The car is already fixed.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She studies piano at the city's conservatory.

definitions.note: Third-person singular present (also used for formal “you”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela considera mudar de emprego este ano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She considers changing jobs this year.

definitions.note: feminine singular past participle of "considerar"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela é considerada uma das melhores professoras da escola.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nós consideramos a sua proposta muito interessante.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: As suas palavras foram um grande consolo para mim.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Your words were a great comfort to me.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Be careful when crossing the street.

definitions.note: Plural form; often used for care or attention given to someone/something.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: How much is this book going to cost?

definitions.native: to be hard (to do), to take effort
definitions.note: Often used in expressions like “custar a” + infinitive.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vai-me custar aceitar a notícia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It will be hard for me to accept the news.

definitions.note: Past tense (they/you all) of "custar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os ingressos custaram cem reais.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The tickets cost one hundred reais.

definitions.note: Conditional form of "custar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quanto custaria consertar isso?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: How much would it cost to fix that?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quanto custará esta viagem?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: How much will this trip cost?

definitions.note: Often used with a person as an indirect object: “custar a alguém” = to be hard for someone / to take someone effort.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Custará algum tempo para terminar este trabalho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It will take some time to finish this work.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O custo da viagem foi alto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cost of the trip was high.

definitions.note: Plural of "custo".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Precisamos reduzir os custos do projeto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need to reduce the project's costs.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite) of “custar”: “it cost” / “it took (time)”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O ingresso custou cinquenta euros.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The ticket cost fifty euros.

definitions.note: Often used in legal contexts (e.g., child custody).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O juiz concedeu a custódia da criança à mãe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The judge granted custody of the child to the mother.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele me cutucou para eu olhar para o lado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He poked me so I would look to the side.

definitions.note: Very vulgar slang insult (offensive).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele foi um cuzão comigo ontem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was an asshole to me yesterday.

definitions.note: Often used in the expression “para cá” (“over here/toward here”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vem cá um minuto, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Come here for a minute, please.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Preciso fazer um cálculo rápido antes de decidir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to do a quick calculation before deciding.

definitions.note: Used especially for the school/university subject (math).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No ensino médio, eu tinha dificuldade com cálculo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In high school, I had trouble with calculus.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Preciso fazer alguns cálculos antes de decidir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to do some calculations before deciding.

definitions.note: Often used for a ceremonial or religious cup (e.g., in church).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O padre levantou o cálice durante a missa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The priest raised the chalice during the mass.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tomo duas cápsulas por dia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I take two capsules a day.

definitions.note: Often used in set phrases like “câmara municipal” (city council) or “câmara de comércio” (chamber of commerce).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A reunião vai ser na câmara do conselho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The meeting will be in the council chamber.

definitions.note: In Brazilian Portuguese, “câmera” is the more common spelling for this meaning.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A câmara do meu celular está quebrada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My phone’s camera is broken.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: As câmaras estavam desligadas durante a reunião.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cameras were turned off during the meeting.

definitions.note: Often used in formal or institutional contexts (e.g., legislative or municipal chambers).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: As câmaras aprovaram a nova lei.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The chambers approved the new law.

definitions.note: Used mainly in radio/phone communication to indicate you finished speaking and the other person can reply.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estou chegando em dez minutos, câmbio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll be there in ten minutes, over.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Comprei uma câmera nova para tirar fotos nas férias.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought a new camera to take photos on vacation.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: As câmeras estão ligadas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cameras are on.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Meu avô morreu de câncer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My grandfather died of cancer.

definitions.note: Plural of “cão” (dog).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os cães estão no parque.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dogs are in the park.

definitions.note: Usually refers to a male dog; as a generic word for “dog,” many speakers also use “cachorro.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O cão está a dormir no sofá.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog is sleeping on the sofa.

definitions.note: Diminutive of "cão"; often expresses affection or that the dog is small.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O cãozinho está dormindo no sofá.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The little dog is sleeping on the couch.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A célula é a menor unidade do corpo humano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cell is the smallest unit of the human body.

definitions.note: Plural of “célula”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os cientistas estudam as células no laboratório.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Scientists study cells in the laboratory.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O cérebro controla muitas funções do corpo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The brain controls many functions of the body.

definitions.note: Plural of "cérebro".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os cérebros dos estudantes estavam cansados depois da prova.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The students' brains were tired after the test.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele é cético em relação a promessas muito boas para ser verdade.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is skeptical about promises that are too good to be true.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O céu está limpo hoje.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The sky is clear today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela acredita no céu.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She believes in heaven.

definitions.note: Used as an exclamation to show surprise, shock, or emphasis (like “good heavens!”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Céus, eu não acredito no que aconteceu!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Heavens, I can’t believe what happened!

definitions.note: Plural of “céu” (sky/heaven).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os céus estavam nublados ontem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The skies were cloudy yesterday.

definitions.note: Used as an exclamation to express surprise, shock, or emphasis.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Céus! Eu esqueci a carteira em casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Heavens! I forgot my wallet at home.

definitions.note: Informal Brazilian Portuguese (spoken) short form of “você”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cê vai ao cinema hoje?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Are you going to the movies today?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Desenha um círculo no papel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Draw a circle on the paper.

definitions.note: Plural of "círculo".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Desenhei dois círculos no caderno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I drew two circles in the notebook.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O código está errado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The code is wrong.

definitions.note: Often used in a more formal/literary way than everyday “raiva.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele ficou com cólera quando ouviu a notícia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was filled with anger when he heard the news.

definitions.note: Also the name of a disease (medical context).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Houve um surto de cólera na região.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There was a cholera outbreak in the region.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Preciso de uma cópia do seu documento.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need a copy of your document.

definitions.note: plural of “cópia”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Preciso de três cópias deste documento.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need three copies of this document.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form of “cósmico”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A poeira cósmica pode viajar por milhões de anos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Cosmic dust can travel for millions of years.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A cômoda fica no quarto, ao lado da cama.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dresser is in the bedroom, next to the bed.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este sofá é muito cômodo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This sofa is very comfortable.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este apartamento tem três cômodos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This apartment has three rooms.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O apartamento tem três cômodos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The apartment has three rooms.

definitions.note: Vulgar/slang term.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele caiu de cú no chão.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He fell on his butt on the floor.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele foi cúmplice no roubo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was an accomplice in the robbery.

definitions.note: contraction of de + a
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela voltou da praia ontem à noite.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She came back from the beach last night.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form; often used like an adjective or as the past participle of "dar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A resposta já foi dada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The answer has already been given.

definitions.note: Past participle of "dar"; often used with "ter" or "ser" as an auxiliary.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A resposta já foi dada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The answer has already been given.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu perdi o dado de seis lados.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I lost the six-sided die.

definitions.note: Often used in the plural (dados) to mean “data.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Esse dado é importante para a pesquisa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That fact is important for the research.

definitions.note: Past participle of "dar" used as an adjective (often meaning something provided or specified).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O prazo dado foi curto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The given deadline was short.

definitions.note: Past participle of "dar"; often used with "ter/haver" or in the passive voice.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O livro foi dado a ela.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The book was given to her.

definitions.note: Often used as a plural noun meaning information (e.g., computer data).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os dados do relatório estão corretos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The data in the report is correct.

definitions.note: Plural of "dado" when it means a die (game piece).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Precisamos de dois dados para jogar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need two dice to play.

definitions.note: Past participle of "dar" used as an adjective (masculine plural).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os exemplos dados pelo professor foram claros.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The examples given by the teacher were clear.

definitions.note: Past participle (masculine plural) of "dar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os conselhos foram dados pelo professor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The advice was given by the teacher.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu vim dali há pouco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I came from there a little while ago.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Meu irmão é daltônico e não distingue bem o vermelho do verde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My brother is color-blind and he can’t distinguish red from green very well.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Aquela dama entrou na sala e cumprimentou todos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That lady entered the room and greeted everyone.

definitions.note: In the game of checkers, a "dama" is a piece that has been promoted and can move more freely.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu fiz uma dama e ganhei a partida de damas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I got a queen and won the checkers game.

definitions.note: Plural of "dama"; often used as a polite/formal way to address or refer to women.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Senhoras e damas, o espetáculo vai começar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Ladies and gentlemen, the show is about to begin.

definitions.note: Present tense (nós).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nós damos um presente à professora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We give a gift to the teacher.

definitions.note: Often used informally (sometimes affectionately) to talk about someone—especially a child—who is naughty or causes trouble.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O danado quebrou o vaso e saiu correndo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The little rascal broke the vase and ran off.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Que dia danado!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What a damn day!

definitions.note: Often used (especially in Brazil) to describe someone who causes trouble in a playful way.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O menino está danado hoje.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The boy is being naughty today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A chuva pode danar a pintura do carro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Rain can damage the car’s paint.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu dancei a noite toda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I danced all night.

definitions.note: Present participle/gerund of "dar" (used with "estar" or to mean "by" + verb, e.g., "by giving").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estou dando um presente para a minha irmã.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am giving a gift to my sister.

definitions.note: Often used in the subjunctive (e.g., after "espero que") or as a formal command ("você").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que isso não dane o seu computador.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope this doesn't ruin your computer.

definitions.note: Often used in the present subjunctive (e.g., after expressions like “espero que...”, “tomara que...”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que eles não danem o carro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope they don't ruin the car.

definitions.note: feminine form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A tela do meu celular está danificada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My phone screen is damaged.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O telefone chegou danificado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The phone arrived damaged.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A chuva danificou o telhado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The rain damaged the roof.

definitions.note: Plural feminine form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Essas substâncias são daninhas para a saúde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Those substances are harmful to health.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A queda causou um dano no carro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The fall caused damage to the car.

definitions.note: Plural of "dano".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O seguro cobre danos no carro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The insurance covers damage to the car.

definitions.note: Often informal/colloquial; can also mean something went wrong or stopped working.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O computador danou e parou de funcionar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The computer messed up and stopped working.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A dança começa às oito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dance starts at eight.

definitions.note: Commonly used as the 3rd-person singular present tense form of the verb “dançar” (also used in the imperative for “você”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela dança muito bem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She dances very well.

definitions.note: Present tense form of “dançar” (used with “eles/elas/vocês”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles dançam muito bem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They dance very well.

definitions.note: Present tense (nós).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Aos sábados, dançamos no parque.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: On Saturdays, we dance in the park.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito perfeito) (nós).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ontem, dançamos a noite toda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday, we danced all night.

definitions.note: Present participle/gerund form of “dançar”; often used with “estar” to mean “to be dancing.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela está dançando agora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is dancing now.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu gosto de dançar com os meus amigos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like to dance with my friends.

definitions.note: 3rd-person plural (they/you all) in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles dançaram a noite toda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They danced all night.

definitions.note: Female dancer; the masculine form is “dançarino”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A dançarina ensaiou por horas antes do espetáculo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dancer rehearsed for hours before the show.

definitions.note: Usually masculine; feminine is "dançarina".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele é dançarino e trabalha num teatro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is a dancer and works in a theater.

definitions.note: Plural of “dança”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: As danças tradicionais variam de região para região.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Traditional dances vary from region to region.

definitions.note: Imperfect past (pretérito imperfeito): used for ongoing/repeated actions or background in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu dançava todos os sábados quando era jovem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I danced every Saturday when I was young.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu danço muito bem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I dance very well.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela dançou a noite toda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She danced all night.

definitions.note: Feminine singular; contraction of “de” + “aquela”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu me lembro daquela viagem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I remember that trip.

definitions.note: Contraction of "de" + "aquela"; refers to something feminine singular ("that").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Não me lembro do nome daquela pessoa, mas lembro da voz dela.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't remember that person's name, but I remember her voice.

definitions.note: Contraction of "de" + "aquelas" (feminine plural).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu gosto daquelas flores amarelas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like those yellow flowers.

definitions.note: contraction of "de" + "aquelas" (feminine plural)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu não gosto daquelas coisas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't like those things.

definitions.note: Masculine singular form. Used with a noun (e.g., "daquele livro") or in expressions like "daquele jeito".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu não gosto daquele barulho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't like that noise.

definitions.note: Contraction of "de" + "aquele"; used with masculine singular.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu me lembro daquele dia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I remember that day.

definitions.note: Contraction of "de" + "aqueles" (masculine plural).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu lembro o nome daqueles alunos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I remember the names of those students.

definitions.note: Contraction of "de" + "aqueles" (masculine plural demonstrative).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu não gosto daqueles filmes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't like those movies.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Não sou daqui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm not from here.

definitions.note: Contraction of "de" + "aquilo"; refers to something not close to the speaker.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Não gosto daquilo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t like that.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quero dar um presente para a minha mãe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to give a present to my mother.

definitions.note: First-person singular ("I") future tense of "dar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu darei o livro a ela amanhã.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will give her the book tomorrow.

definitions.note: First-person plural ("we") future form of "dar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nós daremos o dinheiro amanhã.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We will give the money tomorrow.

definitions.note: Conditional form of "dar" (used for hypotheticals or polite requests).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu daria tudo para te ver feliz.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would give everything to see you happy.

definitions.note: Conditional tense (they/you all would give).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles dariam mais tempo se pudessem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They would give more time if they could.

definitions.note: Third-person singular (ele/ela/você) future tense of "dar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela dará um presente ao irmão amanhã.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She will give her brother a gift tomorrow.

definitions.note: Third-person plural (they/you all) future tense of "dar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles darão o dinheiro amanhã.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They will give the money tomorrow.

definitions.note: contraction of de + as, used before feminine plural nouns
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: As portas das casas estavam abertas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The doors of the houses were open.

definitions.note: Usually means a calendar date (day/month/year).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Qual é a data do seu aniversário?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What is the date of your birthday?

definitions.note: In this sense, Portuguese more commonly uses the plural “dados,” but “data” can appear (often in technical/business contexts) as an invariable loanword.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Precisamos proteger a data dos clientes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need to protect customer data.

definitions.note: Plural of "data" (in the calendar sense).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Preciso confirmar as datas da viagem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to confirm the dates of the trip.

definitions.note: Plural of "data"; in Portuguese, "data" is usually singular and "dados" is the plural when meaning "information".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os cientistas analisaram as datas do experimento.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The scientists analyzed the data from the experiment.

definitions.note: Often used for typing on a typewriter; in modern contexts, it can also mean typing in general, but it may sound a bit old-fashioned.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela aprendeu a datilografar na escola.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She learned to type in school.

definitions.note: Imperfect past (ongoing/repeated action in the past) of “dar” (“to give”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele sempre me dava um chocolate quando eu era criança.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He always gave me a chocolate when I was a child.

definitions.note: Often used to show cause or consequence: “that’s why/so.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu estava cansado, daí fui dormir cedo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was tired, so I went to bed early.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu quero um copo de água.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want a glass of water.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela veio de Lisboa ontem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She came from Lisbon yesterday.

definitions.note: Often used in the phrase “debaixo de” (“under/beneath”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O gato está debaixo da mesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cat is under the table.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O debate foi muito interessante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The debate was very interesting.

definitions.note: Often used for moral, social, or economic decline.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele está decidido a mudar de emprego.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is determined to change jobs.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s already decided: we’re traveling tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Preciso decidir hoje.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to decide today.

definitions.note: Third-person plural (they/you all).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles decidiram ficar em casa hoje.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They decided to stay home today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela decidiu viajar amanhã.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She decided to travel tomorrow.

definitions.note: Often used both for reading codes/handwriting and for figuring out something difficult to understand.

definitions.note: Plural of "decisão".

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O imposto já foi declarado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The tax has already been declared.

definitions.note: Often used in formal contexts (e.g., official statements, taxes, customs).

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Declaro que li e aceito os termos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I declare that I have read and accept the terms.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito perfeito) form: “(he/she/you formal) declared.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela declarou que não sabia de nada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She declared that she didn’t know anything.

definitions.note: Used especially for airplanes; also used for the launch of rockets.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A decolagem do avião atrasou por causa do mau tempo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The plane’s takeoff was delayed because of bad weather.

definitions.note: Used for planes/aircraft; also used figuratively (e.g., a project taking off).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O avião vai decolar às oito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The plane is going to take off at eight.

definitions.note: Used for an airplane (or other aircraft) taking off.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Decolaremos em dez minutos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We will take off in ten minutes.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O avião decolou às oito horas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The plane took off at eight o'clock.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estou decorando a sala para a festa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m decorating the living room for the party.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela está decorando as falas para a peça.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She’s memorizing her lines for the play.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela vai decorar a sala para a festa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is going to decorate the living room for the party.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to memorize this poem for tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A decoração da sala ficou muito bonita.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The living room decoration turned out very beautiful.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela decorou a sala para a festa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She decorated the living room for the party.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele decorou o poema em uma tarde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He memorized the poem in one afternoon.

definitions.note: feminine form

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is very dedicated to her work.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele é muito dedicado ao trabalho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is very dedicated to his work.

definitions.note: Often used with "a" (e.g., "dedicar algo a alguém/alguma coisa").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela decidiu dedicar mais tempo aos estudos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She decided to devote more time to her studies.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A dedicação dela ao trabalho é impressionante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Her dedication to work is impressive.

definitions.note: Present tense (eu).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu dedico este livro aos meus pais.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I dedicate this book to my parents.

definitions.note: Simple past (ele/ela/você) of "dedicar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela dedicou o livro ao pai.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She dedicated the book to her father.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dediquei este livro à minha avó.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I dedicated this book to my grandmother.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cortei o dedo a cozinhar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I cut my finger while cooking.

definitions.note: Plural of "dedo"; in Portuguese it can refer to both fingers and toes (often clarified with "dedos da mão" vs. "dedos do pé").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela machucou os dedos quando fechou a porta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She hurt her fingers when she closed the door.

definitions.note: Informal; often implies betraying someone by telling on them to an authority.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele vai dedurar o colega para o chefe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He’s going to rat his coworker out to the boss.

definitions.note: Informal; often means reporting someone to the police, authorities, or a person in charge.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele dedurou o colega para o chefe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He snitched on his coworker to the boss.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pelo que ele disse, posso deduzir que vai chover.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They give good advice to their children.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This product has a defect.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O produto tem alguns defeitos, mas ainda funciona bem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The product has some defects, but it still works well.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (they/you all) of “defender”; often used after expressions like “É importante que…”.
