definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela defende o irmão na escola.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She defends her brother at school.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nós defendemos os nossos direitos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We defend our rights.

definitions.note: Present participle/gerund form of "defender".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele está defendendo a irmã no tribunal.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is defending his sister in court.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vou defender os meus amigos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to defend my friends.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele defendeu o amigo na reunião.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He defended his friend in the meeting.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu defendi meu amigo na reunião.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I defended my friend in the meeting.

definitions.note: Informal/conversational shortened form of the infinitive “defender,” used before object pronouns (e.g., “defendê-lo” = “defend him/it”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vou defendê-lo no debate.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to defend him in the debate.

definitions.note: Often used for a person who supports or protects a cause, idea, or group; in legal contexts it can refer to a defense attorney.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela é uma defensora dos direitos humanos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is a defender of human rights.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A defesa do time foi muito boa no segundo tempo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The team's defense was very good in the second half.

definitions.note: Often used for defending an idea, a person, or a position (including in court).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele fez uma defesa forte do seu ponto de vista.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He made a strong defense of his point of view.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O prédio tem uma rampa para pessoas com deficiência.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The building has a ramp for people with disabilities.

definitions.note: Often used for a lack of something (e.g., nutrients, resources).

definitions.note: Used as a command (imperative) or in the present subjunctive for você/ele/ela.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Esta é a resposta definitiva.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This is the definitive answer.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu definitivamente quero ir ao cinema hoje.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I definitely want to go to the movies today.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He lies down on the couch after work.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The child is lying down on the couch.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cat is lying on the couch.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Deitem-se, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Lie down, please.

definitions.note: Usually means “lets/allows” (3rd person singular, present). It can also be used as an informal command meaning “leave it / stop it,” depending on context.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let the children play.

definitions.note: Third-person plural (they/you all) form of “deixar”; it can mean to leave something/someone somewhere or to allow/let something happen.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They leave the keys on the table.

definitions.note: From deixar; it can mean physically leaving something/someone or allowing/letting something happen.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Deixamos as chaves na mesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We left the keys on the table.

definitions.note: Present participle/gerund of “deixar”; often used like “leaving” or “letting” depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estou deixando as chaves na mesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m leaving the keys on the table.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vou deixar o livro na mesa.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela não quer deixar as crianças saírem sozinhas.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito perfeito), 3rd person plural: “they left.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles deixaram a cidade ontem à noite.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They left the city last night.

definitions.note: Often used with an object meaning “left something somewhere” or “let/allowed.” Simple past, 3rd person plural.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles deixaram as chaves na mesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They left the keys on the table.

definitions.note: Future tense (1st person singular) of "deixar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Deixarei as chaves na mesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will leave the keys on the table.

definitions.note: Often used as a personal infinitive meaning “for us to leave/let”.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s better for us to leave that for tomorrow.

definitions.note: Third-person singular future (ele/ela/você).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela deixará as chaves na mesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She will leave the keys on the table.

definitions.note: 3rd person plural (they/you all) future tense of “deixar”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles deixarão as malas no hotel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They will leave the suitcases at the hotel.

definitions.note: Present tense (tu). Informal “you” in many regions; in Brazil it’s mostly used in some dialects and in Portugal.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu deixas a porta aberta?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you leave the door open?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se eu deixasse a porta aberta, o gato fugia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If I left the door open, the cat would run away.

definitions.native: you left, you let, you allowed
definitions.note: Past tense (pretérito perfeito), informal singular (tu).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Deixaste a porta aberta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You left the door open.

definitions.note: Imperfect past (ongoing/habitual action in the past) of “deixar” (“to leave”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele deixava o carro na garagem todos os dias.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He left the car in the garage every day.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Deixe o copo na pia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Leave the glass in the sink.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Deixe as crianças brincarem no jardim.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let the children play in the garden.

definitions.native: I left, I let, I allowed
definitions.note: Past (pretérito perfeito), 1st person singular of “deixar”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Deixei o livro na mesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I left the book on the table.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (also used for commands with vocês).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Deixem as crianças brincar no parque.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let the children play in the park.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (also used for commands with vocês).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Leave the car here and come with me.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let’s leave the car here and go on foot.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que não deixes a porta aberta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you don't leave the door open.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu deixo o livro na mesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I leave the book on the table.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela deixou o livro na mesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She left the book on the table.

definitions.note: often used before another verb, as in letting someone do something
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O professor deixou os alunos saírem mais cedo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The teacher let the students leave earlier.

definitions.note: Colloquial shortened form of “deixar”, common in informal speech and lyrics (especially in Brazil).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vou deixá pra depois.

definitions.note: Used to indicate a starting point in time or place (often paired with “até” = “until”).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ve lived here since 2020.

definitions.note: Third-person singular present of "desejar" (ele/ela/você).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela deseja um carro novo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She wants a new car.

definitions.note: 3rd person plural (they/you all) present of “desejar”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles desejam um futuro melhor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They want a better future.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Desejamos muita saúde para você.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We wish you lots of health.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to wish you lots of health.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles desejaram um feliz aniversário para ela.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I wanted a coffee after lunch.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu desejei boa sorte a ela.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I wished her good luck.

definitions.note: Present tense (eu) form of the verb “desejar”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Desejo boa sorte a você.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He wished everyone good luck.

definitions.native: to disembark, to get off (a vehicle)

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito perfeito) of “desembarcar”.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He got off the bus at the next stop.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vou desempacotar as malas agora.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O desempenho da equipe melhorou muito este mês.

definitions.note: Feminine form (used when talking about a woman).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He has been unemployed since January.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O desemprego aumentou este ano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Unemployment increased this year.

definitions.note: Present tense (ele/ela/você).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela desenha um gato no caderno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She draws a cat in the notebook.

definitions.note: present participle/gerund of "desenhar"

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela gosta de desenhar flores.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She likes to draw flowers.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please draw a cat.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito perfeito), usually means “I drew.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu desenhei um gato no meu caderno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I drew a cat in my notebook.

definitions.note: Plural of "desenho".

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The children made drawings in art class.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito perfeito) of “desenhar” (to draw).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela desenhou um gato no caderno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She drew a cat in the notebook.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She started to unwrap the gift wrapping.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She developed an app for school.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O desenvolvimento da cidade foi muito rápido nos últimos anos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The city's development was very fast in recent years.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O deserto do Saara é muito quente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The Sahara desert is very hot.

definitions.note: Often used as an adjective; feminine form is 'deserta'.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O Saara é um deserto muito grande.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was miserable after losing his job.

definitions.note: Often used as a strong insult; can be offensive depending on tone and context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Aquele desgraçado roubou a minha carteira!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That bastard stole my wallet!

definitions.note: Often used with a negative or insulting tone, depending on context.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gosto do design desta cadeira.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The referee must be impartial.

definitions.note: Often used as a command (formal “you”) or as the present subjunctive (e.g., after expressions like “I hope that…”).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please, don’t give up now.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nós desistimos porque era muito difícil.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is giving up the course because he doesn’t have time.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele se despediu dos amigos na estação.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He said goodbye to his friends at the station.

definitions.note: Used when someone loses a job (more common than in English to use the same verb as “say goodbye”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A empresa o despediu sem aviso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The company fired him without notice.

definitions.note: Past (he/she/you formal) form of "despejar"; often used for liquids ("poured out") or for getting rid of something ("threw out").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela despejou a água no copo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She poured the water into the glass.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A despensa está cheia de arroz e feijão.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The pantry is full of rice and beans.

definitions.note: Often used in the expression “passar despercebido” (to go unnoticed).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O erro passou despercebido.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The mistake went unnoticed.

definitions.note: Usually used as a formal command (e.g., “Don’t waste...”) or in the present subjunctive after expressions like “I hope/it’s important that...”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Não desperdice água.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t waste water.

definitions.note: Present participle/gerund of "desperdiçar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Você está desperdiçando água ao deixar a torneira aberta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You are wasting water by leaving the tap on.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Não quero desperdiçar comida.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't want to waste food.

definitions.note: Often used for wasting resources like time, money, food, or water.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O desperdício de comida é um problema sério.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Food waste is a serious problem.

definitions.note: Present tense form of “despertar”; can also be used as an imperative (“wake up!”) depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela desperta cedo todos os dias.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She wakes up early every day.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu coloquei o despertador para as seis da manhã.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I set the alarm clock for six in the morning.

definitions.note: Present participle/gerund of "despertar"; often used with "estar" to describe an action in progress.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estou despertando cedo hoje.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m waking up early today.

definitions.note: Can be used both intransitively (“to wake up”) and transitively (“to wake someone up”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu costumo despertar cedo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I usually wake up early.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Despertei cedo hoje.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I woke up early today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela despertou cedo hoje.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She woke up early today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Essa despesa não estava no orçamento.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That expense wasn’t in the budget.

definitions.note: Plural of "despesa".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: As despesas do mês foram mais altas do que esperávamos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This month's expenses were higher than we expected.

definitions.note: Used when someone (often an employer) makes another person leave a job.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que o chefe não me despeça.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope the boss doesn’t fire me.

definitions.note: Used when you make a farewell to someone or send them off.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quando o ônibus chegar, despeça seu irmão na porta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When the bus arrives, say goodbye to your brother at the door.

definitions.native: we misled, we threw off (the trail)
definitions.note: Often used in the sense of throwing someone off your trail (e.g., the police, an opponent).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Despistamos a polícia mudando de rota.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We threw the police off by changing routes.

definitions.note: Common in European Portuguese; in Brazilian Portuguese, the usual word is "esporte".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gosto de praticar desporto ao ar livre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like to play sports outdoors.

definitions.note: Often used to describe someone who isn’t worried or stressed.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele parecia despreocupado apesar dos problemas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He seemed carefree despite the problems.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela despreza as regras do time.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She despises the team's rules.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu desprezo esse tipo de comportamento.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I despise that kind of behavior.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela falou com desprezo sobre os colegas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She spoke with contempt about her coworkers.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Achei desprezível a maneira como ele tratou o garçom.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I found it despicable the way he treated the waiter.

definitions.note: Often used with a direct object: desrespeitar alguém/algo.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: É importante não desrespeitar as pessoas mais velhas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It's important not to disrespect older people.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Falta de educação é uma forma de desrespeito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Rudeness is a form of disrespect.

definitions.note: Contraction of "de" + "essa" (feminine singular).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu me lembrei dessa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I remembered that.

definitions.note: Contraction of "de" + "essa"; feminine singular (used before a feminine noun).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gosto dessa música.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like that song.

definitions.note: Contraction of “de” + “essa” (feminine singular). Often used after verbs that take “de” (e.g., lembrar-se de).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu me lembro bem dessa história.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I remember that story well.

definitions.note: Feminine plural contraction of “de” + “essas” (used with feminine plural nouns).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Não gosto dessas ideias.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't like those ideas.

definitions.note: Contraction of "de" + "essas"; used with feminine plural things/ideas that are near the listener (or already mentioned).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu preciso de algumas dessas canetas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need some of those pens.

definitions.note: Imperfect subjunctive form of "dar"; often used in hypothetical "if" clauses (e.g., "Se eu...", "Se ele...").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se eu desse mais tempo, eu ajudaria você.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If I gave more time, I would help you.

definitions.note: Contraction of "de" + "esse" (masculine singular).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu não gostei desse filme.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I didn't like that movie.

definitions.note: Contraction of "de" + "esse"; used before a masculine singular noun (e.g., "desse livro").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu preciso desse documento hoje.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need that document today.

definitions.note: Contraction of "de" + "esse"; usually means "of/from that" (near the listener or previously mentioned).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu não gosto desse tipo de comida.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't like that kind of food.

definitions.note: Used in the imperfect subjunctive (e.g., after "se" or "que").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se eles dessem mais tempo, eu terminaria o trabalho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If they gave more time, I would finish the work.

definitions.note: Contraction of "de" + "esses" (masculine plural).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Não gosto desses filmes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't like those movies.

definitions.note: Contraction of "de" + "esses" (plural masculine). Used to refer to things near the listener or previously mentioned.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gosto desses livros que você recomendou.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like those books you recommended.

definitions.note: Contraction of "de" + "esses" (plural masculine: "those/these"), used to mean "of/from those/these".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Não gosto desses livros.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't like those books.

definitions.note: Contraction of "de" + "esta" (feminine singular).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gosto da cor desta camisa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like the color of this shirt.

definitions.note: feminine singular form; contraction of "de" + "esta".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gosto muito desta cidade.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I really like this city.

definitions.note: Contraction of “de” + “esta” (feminine singular).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gosto muito desta cidade.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like this city a lot.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela destaca na turma por ser muito dedicada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She stands out in the class because she is very dedicated.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O professor destaca os pontos principais da aula.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The teacher highlights the main points of the lesson.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O destaque do artigo é a entrevista com a cientista.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The highlight of the article is the interview with the scientist.

definitions.note: Contraction of "de" + "estas" (feminine plural).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gosto mais destas cores.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like these colors more.

definitions.note: Contraction of "de" + "estas" (feminine plural).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gosto mais destas do que daquelas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like these more than those.

definitions.note: Preterite (simple past) form used with “tu” (informal ‘you’ in some regions).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Deste um presente à tua irmã?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Did you give your sister a present?

definitions.note: Contraction of "de" + "este" (masculine singular).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gosto do som deste instrumento.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like the sound of this instrument.

definitions.note: Contraction of "de" + "este"; used before a masculine singular noun.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A capa deste livro é bonita.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cover of this book is pretty.

definitions.note: Contraction of "de" + "este" (masculine singular).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gosto mais deste livro do que daquele.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like this book more than that one.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele é um herói destemido.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is a fearless hero.

definitions.note: Contraction of "de" + "estes".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gosto destes livros.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like these books.

definitions.note: Contraction of "de" + "estes" (masculine plural).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gosto destes livros.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like these books.

definitions.note: Contraction of "de" + "estes".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Não gosto destes livros.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't like these books.

definitions.note: Often used with “a/para” to say who/what something is for; it can also mean “destined” depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este livro é destinado a crianças.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This book is intended for children.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Qual é o seu destino final?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What is your final destination?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela acredita que tudo está escrito no destino.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She believes that everything is written in fate.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A porta está destrancada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The door is unlocked.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele destrancou a porta e entrou.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He unlocked the door and went in.

definitions.note: Often used as a command (imperative) or as the present subjunctive form of “destravar.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Destrave a porta, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Unlock the door, please.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Meu irmão é destro, mas eu sou canhoto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My brother is right-handed, but I'm left-handed.

definitions.note: Third-person plural present tense (they destroy/you all destroy).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: As tempestades destroem muitas casas todos os anos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Storms destroy many houses every year.

definitions.note: Usually used after words like "que" ("I want you to...") or in commands/requests; from the verb "destruir".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que você não destrua o documento.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you don’t destroy the document.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O fogo está destruindo a floresta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The fire is destroying the forest.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O incêndio pode destruir a floresta inteira.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The fire can destroy the entire forest.

definitions.note: Conditional form (used for hypothetical situations).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu destruiria essa carta se fosse você.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would destroy that letter if I were you.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito perfeito) form of “destruir” (he/she/it destroyed).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O incêndio destruiu a casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The fire destroyed the house.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A destruição da floresta afetou muitos animais.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The destruction of the forest affected many animals.

definitions.note: feminine singular form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A crítica dela foi destrutiva e não ajudou em nada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Her criticism was destructive and didn’t help at all.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Destruí a carta antes que alguém a encontrasse.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I destroyed the letter before anyone could find it.

definitions.note: feminine singular past participle of “destruir” (often used with “ser/estar” or as an adjective)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A cidade ficou destruída após a tempestade.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The city was left destroyed after the storm.

definitions.note: past participle (feminine plural) of "destruir"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: As casas foram destruídas pela tempestade.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The houses were destroyed by the storm.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O prédio ficou destruído depois da tempestade.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The building was left destroyed after the storm.

definitions.note: Past participle of "destruir"; often used with "ser/estar" (e.g., "foi/está destruído").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O prédio foi destruído pelo incêndio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The building was destroyed by the fire.

definitions.note: Past participle (plural masculine) of "destruir"; often used with "ser" to form the passive or with "ter" as a compound tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os documentos foram destruídos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The documents were destroyed.

definitions.note: Third-person plural (they/you all) in the simple past (pretérito perfeito).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles destruíram a ponte durante a guerra.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They destroyed the bridge during the war.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A tempestade destrói muitas casas todos os anos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The storm destroys many houses every year.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A falta de experiência pode ser uma desvantagem na entrevista.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Lack of experience can be a disadvantage in the interview.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: As desvantagens desse plano são claras.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The disadvantages of this plan are clear.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O rio pode desviar o caminho por causa das chuvas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The river can divert its course because of the rains.

definitions.native: to swerve, to move out of the way
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tive que desviar para não bater no carro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I had to swerve so I wouldn’t hit the car.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Desviei o carro para evitar o buraco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I swerved the car to avoid the pothole.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito perfeito) of “desviar.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O carro desviou para evitar o buraco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The car swerved to avoid the pothole.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (also used for affirmative commands with você/a gente): e.g., “Desça as escadas.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Por favor, desça as escadas com cuidado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please go down the stairs carefully.

definitions.note: Used with "vocês" (you plural) in the present subjunctive or as a command (imperative).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Por favor, desçam do ônibus na próxima parada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please get off the bus at the next stop.

definitions.note: First-person singular present tense of "descer" (I go/come down).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu desço as escadas devagar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I go down the stairs slowly.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela escreveu uma explicação detalhada do problema.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She wrote a detailed explanation of the problem.

definitions.native: in detail, in a detailed way
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela explicou o problema detalhadamente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She explained the problem in detail.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O relatório está bem detalhado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The report is very detailed.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Esse detalhe é importante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That detail is important.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Não me lembro de todos os detalhes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t remember all the details.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Por favor, detenha o ônibus aqui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please stop the bus here.

definitions.note: Often used in formal contexts (e.g., police or authorities).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se necessário, a polícia detenha o suspeito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If necessary, the police detain the suspect.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (also used for commands addressed to vocês).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que vocês detenham a violência imediatamente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you stop the violence immediately.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (also used for commands addressed to vocês).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: É importante que eles detenham o suspeito sem violência.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s important that they detain the suspect without violence.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A polícia tentou deter os manifestantes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police tried to deter the protesters.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O juiz determina a pena.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The judge determines the sentence.

definitions.note: feminine singular form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela está determinada a terminar o curso este ano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is determined to finish the course this year.

definitions.note: Feminine singular past participle of "determinar"; often used with "ser/estar" in passive constructions.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A data da reunião foi determinada ontem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The date of the meeting was determined yesterday.

definitions.note: Often used like “a certain/specific (one)” in Portuguese.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Em determinado momento, tudo mudou.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At a certain moment, everything changed.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele está determinado a aprender português.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is determined to learn Portuguese.

definitions.note: Often used in formal contexts meaning to set/establish something (e.g., rules, deadlines) or to order something officially.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O juiz vai determinar uma nova data para a audiência.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The judge will set a new date for the hearing.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela mostrou muita determinação para terminar o curso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She showed a lot of determination to finish the course.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela detesta acordar cedo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She hates waking up early.

definitions.note: Present tense (they).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles detestam acordar cedo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They hate waking up early.

definitions.note: Conditional form (used for hypothetical situations).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu detestaria trabalhar aos domingos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would hate to work on Sundays.

definitions.note: Imperfect past tense (used for ongoing/repeated past actions or states).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu detestava acordar cedo quando era criança.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hated waking up early when I was a child.

definitions.note: Past (preterite) form meaning a completed action: “I hated / I disliked.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu detestei aquele filme.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hated that movie.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu detesto acordar cedo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hate waking up early.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O comportamento dele foi detestável.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His behavior was detestable.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A detetive encontrou uma pista importante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The detective found an important clue.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The detectives investigated the case all night long.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O suspeito foi detido pela polícia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The suspect was detained by the police.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police found a detonator near the site of the explosion.

definitions.native: to detonate, to set off (an explosion)

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police managed to detonate the explosive safely.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He managed to ruin the cellphone by dropping it on the floor.

definitions.note: Often used as “detrás de” + noun/pronoun (“behind” something).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O carro está detrás da casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The car is behind the house.

definitions.note: Often used in more formal contexts meaning to stop or restrain something/someone.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police tried to stop him before he ran away.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela me deu um presente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She gave me a gift.

definitions.note: Used as an interjection to express surprise, frustration, or emphasis (like “God!” or “Oh God!” in English).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Deus, eu esqueci as chaves!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: God, I forgot the keys!

definitions.note: Often capitalized (Deus) when referring to the monotheistic God.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Deus é amor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: God is love.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela se vestiu como uma deusa na festa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She dressed like a goddess at the party.

definitions.note: Plural of “deus”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os deuses da mitologia grega são famosos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The gods of Greek mythology are famous.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (ele/ela/você). Often used after expressions of necessity, recommendation, or doubt.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s important that he should apologize.

definitions.note: Subjunctive form of "dever", often used after expressions like "é possível que" or "não acho que".
