definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela embrulhou o presente com cuidado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She wrapped the gift carefully.

definitions.note: Often used with something as the subject: "Isso me embrulhou o estômago" = "That made me feel sick."
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A comida estragada embrulhou o estômago dele.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The spoiled food made his stomach feel sick.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Em caso de emergência, ligue para o 112.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In case of emergency, call 112.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O hospital está cheio de emergências hoje.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The hospital is full of emergencies today.

definitions.note: Usually used with “de” (from) and “para” (to).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Muitas pessoas emigraram de Portugal para o Brasil no século XX.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Many people emigrated from Portugal to Brazil in the 20th century.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela emigrou para o Canadá em 2015.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She emigrated to Canada in 2015.

definitions.note: Often used in phrases like "Sua Eminência" as a title of respect (especially for high-ranking clergy).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele é uma eminência na área da medicina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is an eminence in the field of medicine.

definitions.note: feminine form; often used to mean someone feels touched or excited.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela ficou emocionada com a surpresa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She was moved by the surprise.

definitions.note: Often used to mean feeling strong emotion (for example after good news, a speech, or a special moment).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estou emocionado com a notícia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m moved by the news.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela ficou muito emocional durante o filme.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She got very emotional during the movie.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estou emocionalmente exausto depois desta semana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m emotionally exhausted after this week.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Foi um jogo emocionante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It was an exciting game.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A música o emocionou.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The music moved him.

definitions.note: Often used for someone who shows emotion easily (can be neutral or slightly negative depending on context).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele ficou muito emotivo ao falar da família.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He got very emotional when talking about his family.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu senti uma grande emoção ao ver meus amigos de novo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I felt a great emotion when I saw my friends again.

definitions.note: Plural form of "emoção".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: As emoções podem mudar rapidamente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Emotions can change quickly.

definitions.note: Common in sports and competitions when there is no winner.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O jogo terminou em empate.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The game ended in a tie.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela demonstrou empatia ao ouvir o problema do amigo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She showed empathy when listening to her friend's problem.

definitions.note: Often used for doors, locks, drawers, or machines when they stop working because something is stuck.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A porta emperrou.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The door got stuck.

definitions.note: feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela está empolgada com a viagem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is excited about the trip.

definitions.note: Common in Brazil; it can also mean someone is getting carried away or overly hyped, depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estou empolgado com a viagem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m excited about the trip.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O final do filme foi empolgante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The ending of the movie was exciting.

definitions.note: Commonly used for a female domestic worker; for a more neutral term, you may also see “empregada doméstica” or “funcionária” depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A empregada limpa a casa todas as manhãs.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The housekeeper cleans the house every morning.

definitions.note: Plural feminine form; often refers to domestic workers (e.g., cleaning staff).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: As empregadas chegaram cedo para limpar a casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The maids arrived early to clean the house.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O empregado chegou cedo para começar o trabalho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The employee arrived early to start work.

definitions.note: Often also used as a noun meaning “employee,” but here it’s the adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele está empregado desde janeiro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He has been employed since January.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os empregados chegaram cedo hoje.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The employees arrived early today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A empresa vai empregar mais pessoas este ano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The company is going to hire more people this year.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele sabe empregar bem o tempo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He knows how to use his time well.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela está procurando um emprego novo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is looking for a new job.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Há muitos empregos disponíveis nesta área.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are many jobs available in this area.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A minha irmã trabalha numa empresa de tecnologia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My sister works at a technology company.

definitions.note: Third-person singular (ele/ela/você) present tense of "emprestar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele me empresta o carro no fim de semana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He lends me the car on the weekend.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A bicicleta está emprestada para a minha irmã.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bicycle is loaned to my sister.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: As ferramentas estão emprestadas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The tools are borrowed.

definitions.note: Often used in an adverb-like way with verbs such as "usar" (to use) to mean you are using something that belongs to someone else.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estou usando emprestado o carro do meu amigo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m using my friend’s car (which I borrowed).

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este livro é emprestado da biblioteca.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This book is borrowed from the library.

definitions.note: Often used like an adjective to say something is on loan / borrowed (sometimes implies it’s lent out).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O livro está emprestado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The book is borrowed (out).

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os emprestadores pediram documentos antes de aprovar o empréstimo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The lenders asked for documents before approving the loan.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os livros emprestados precisam ser devolvidos amanhã.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The borrowed books need to be returned tomorrow.

definitions.note: Often used with something being lent and (optionally) the person receiving it: emprestar algo (a alguém).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Você pode me emprestar o seu livro?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you lend me your book?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Amanhã eu emprestarei meu livro para você.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow I will lend my book to you.

definitions.note: Conditional form of "emprestar"; often used for polite requests or hypothetical situations.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu emprestaria meu carro, mas preciso dele hoje.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would lend my car, but I need it today.

definitions.note: Often used with the subjunctive (e.g., after expressions like “espero que...”) or as a formal command (to você).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que você me empreste seu livro amanhã.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you lend me your book tomorrow.

definitions.note: Past tense (pretérito perfeito): completed action in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Emprestei meu livro para um amigo ontem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I lent my book to a friend yesterday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu te empresto meu livro amanhã.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll lend you my book tomorrow.

definitions.note: Past tense (ele/ela/você).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela me emprestou um livro ontem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She lent me a book yesterday.

definitions.note: feminine form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A empresária abriu uma nova loja no centro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The businesswoman opened a new store downtown.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O empresário abriu uma nova loja no centro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The businessman opened a new store downtown.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele pediu um empréstimo ao banco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He asked the bank for a loan.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O banco oferece empréstimos com juros baixos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bank offers loans with low interest.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele empurra a porta para abrir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He pushes the door to open it.

definitions.note: Gerund form (used like “pushing” / “while pushing”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele está empurrando o carrinho de compras.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is pushing the shopping cart.

definitions.note: Verb (infinitive). Can mean physically pushing something/someone, or figuratively urging/pressing someone to do something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu vou empurrar a porta para abrir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to push the door to open it.

definitions.native: to push (an object forward), to move by pushing
definitions.note: Often used with objects like a cart, stroller, or car.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles precisam empurrar o carrinho até o carro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They need to push the cart to the car.

definitions.note: Figurative: to push someone into doing something; ‘to pressure’.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Não vou empurrar ninguém a aceitar essa ideia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m not going to pressure anyone to accept that idea.

definitions.note: Often used as a command (imperative) or after expressions like "é melhor que" or "talvez".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Empurre a porta com cuidado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Push the door carefully.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu empurrei a porta para abrir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I pushed the door to open it.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (vocês/eles/elas) or affirmative command for vocês.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quando o ônibus parar, empurrem a porta com cuidado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When the bus stops, push the door carefully.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele empurrou a porta para abrir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He pushed the door to open it.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele me deu um empurrão no metrô.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He gave me a push in the subway.

definitions.note: Often used to say something physically fits, or that it fits logically (makes sense).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Esta peça encaixa perfeitamente aqui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This piece fits perfectly here.

definitions.note: Often used for something physically fitting (a piece, lid, etc.) or for scheduling something into a time slot.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A tampa não consegue encaixar direito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The lid can’t fit properly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu encaixo a peça aqui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I fit the piece here.

definitions.note: Often used for forwarding messages/documents or referring someone/something to a person or place for the next step.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela encaminhou o e-mail para o gerente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She forwarded the email to the manager.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O encanador veio consertar o vazamento na cozinha.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The plumber came to fix the leak in the kitchen.

definitions.note: Often used like this: “Me encanta ...” = “I love ... / I really like ...” (literally, “... delights me”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me encanta este lugar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I love this place.

definitions.note: Often used as a polite greeting meaning “nice to meet you” (said by a woman).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Olá, eu sou a Ana. Encantada!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Hi, I’m Ana. Nice to meet you!

definitions.note: Often used as a polite greeting meaning “nice to meet you” (masculine singular).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Encantado em conhecê-lo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Nice to meet you.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O garçom foi muito encantador conosco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The waiter was very charming with us.

definitions.note: Feminine form (used with feminine nouns or to describe a woman/girl).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela é uma pessoa encantadora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is a charming person.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O encanto da cidade antiga atrai muitos turistas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The charm of the old town attracts many tourists.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela está encarando um grande desafio no trabalho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is facing a big challenge at work.

definitions.note: Often implies a direct, intense look (like staring).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele ficou me encarando durante a reunião.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He kept staring at me during the meeting.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela teve que encarar o problema de frente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She had to face the problem head-on.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele ficou a reunião inteira a encarar-me.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He spent the whole meeting staring at me.

definitions.note: Simple past (ele/ela/você) of "encarar"; often used for facing a situation or confronting someone directly.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela encarou o problema com coragem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She faced the problem with courage.

definitions.note: Often used for someone responsible for a task or area; in some contexts it can mean a manager or foreman.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Fale com o encarregado da obra para tirar dúvidas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Talk to the supervisor at the construction site to clear up doubts.

definitions.note: Often used with "de" (e.g., "encarregado de" + infinitive) to mean "responsible for".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele está encarregado de organizar a reunião.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is in charge of organizing the meeting.

definitions.note: Often refers to how a play, scene, or event is staged (direction, actors, setting).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A encenação da peça foi incrível.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The staging of the play was incredible.

definitions.note: Often used for store/office hours (“closes”) and for finishing something like a meeting or event (“ends”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A loja encerra às seis.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The store closes at six.

definitions.note: Often used for places (stores, offices) that are not open.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O museu está encerrado hoje.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The museum is closed today.

definitions.note: Often used for closing something officially (a business, an account, an event, a meeting).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vamos encerrar a reunião agora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We're going to end the meeting now.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O festival vai encerrar no domingo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The festival will end on Sunday.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito perfeito) of "encerrar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A loja encerrou às seis.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The store closed at six.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (also used for affirmative commands with você).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que você encha a garrafa com água.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you fill the bottle with water.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Depois da chuva, ela chegou em casa encharcada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the rain, she got home soaked.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Depois da chuva, ele ficou encharcado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the rain, he got soaked.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Depois da chuva, voltamos para casa com os sapatos encharcados.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the rain, we went home with our shoes soaked.

definitions.note: Present tense form of “encher” (also used as a formal command: “Fill!”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A chuva enche o rio rapidamente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The rain fills the river quickly.

definitions.note: Present tense, 3rd person plural (they/you all) of "encher".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles enchem a garrafa com água.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They fill the bottle with water.

definitions.note: Gerund form; often corresponds to English “(is/are) filling” depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estou enchendo a garrafa com água.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m filling the bottle with water.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A enchente alagou várias ruas da cidade.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The flood flooded several streets in the city.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Você pode encher este copo de água, por favor?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you fill this glass with water, please?

definitions.note: Third-person plural, simple past (pretérito perfeito): “they/you (plural)/you (formal, plural) filled.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles encheram o copo de água.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They filled the glass with water.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito perfeito) of “encher” (to fill).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele encheu a garrafa de água.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He filled the bottle with water.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Comprei uma enciclopédia para estudar em casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought an encyclopedia to study at home.

definitions.note: Often used for hiding something on purpose (e.g., a mistake or wrongdoing).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele tentou encobrir o erro, mas todos perceberam.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He tried to cover up the mistake, but everyone noticed.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito perfeito) of “encolher” (he/she/it shrank; you/formal shrank).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Com o frio, ele encolheu os ombros.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Because of the cold, he shrugged/pulled back his shoulders.

definitions.note: Often used for an order placed with a store (especially something to be delivered).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A minha encomenda chegou hoje de manhã.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My order was delivered this morning.

definitions.note: Plural form of "encomenda"; often used for online or store purchases that are ordered for delivery.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: As encomendas chegam amanhã de manhã.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The deliveries arrive tomorrow morning.

definitions.note: Often used for ordering something ahead of time (placing an order) rather than ordering in a restaurant.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Encomendei um bolo para o aniversário dela.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I ordered a cake for her birthday.

definitions.note: Usually means “placed an order” (e.g., food or a product).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela encomendou uma pizza para o jantar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She ordered a pizza for dinner.

definitions.note: Present tense form of “encontrar” (used with ele/ela/você).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela encontra as chaves na bolsa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She finds the keys in her bag.

definitions.note: Can also mean “meets” (to encounter someone). Present tense form (ele/ela/você).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele encontra os amigos no café.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He meets his friends at the café.

definitions.note: Feminine singular past participle of "encontrar"; often used with "ser/estar" (e.g., "foi/estava encontrada").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A carteira foi encontrada perto do banco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The wallet was found near the bench.

definitions.note: feminine plural form (often used as a past participle)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: As chaves foram encontradas no sofá.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The keys were found on the couch.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O anel foi encontrado no jardim.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The ring was found in the garden.

definitions.note: past participle (plural masculine) of “encontrar”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os documentos foram encontrados ontem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The documents were found yesterday.

definitions.note: 3rd person plural (they/you all) present tense of “encontrar”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles encontram as chaves na gaveta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They find the keys in the drawer.

definitions.note: Colloquial (especially Brazilian) spoken form of “encontramos” (final -s is dropped in speech and sometimes written that way).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A gente se encontramo na porta do cinema.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We met at the movie theater entrance.

definitions.note: Can mean either ‘we find’ (discover/locate) or ‘we meet’ (run into/arrange to see), depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nós encontramos as chaves na cozinha.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We found the keys in the kitchen.

definitions.note: Present participle/gerund of “encontrar”; often used with “estar” to mean “(to be) finding/meeting” (ongoing action).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estou encontrando meus amigos no parque agora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m meeting my friends at the park now.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Não consigo encontrar meu celular.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can't find my cell phone.

definitions.note: Often used with reflexive pronouns when people are meeting each other or meeting up.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vamos nos encontrar na estação às seis.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let's meet at the station at six.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), 3rd person plural (they/you all).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles encontraram uma solução para o problema.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They found a solution to the problem.

definitions.native: I will find, I will meet
definitions.note: Simple future (1st person singular) of "encontrar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu encontrarei a solução amanhã.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will find the solution tomorrow.

definitions.note: Future subjunctive form, used after certain conjunctions (e.g., quando, se) to talk about a future possibility/condition.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se eles encontrarem a chave, abrem a porta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If they find the key, they open the door.

definitions.native: we will find, we will meet
definitions.note: Future tense ("we" form). Can mean finding something or meeting someone, depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Amanhã encontraremos um bom lugar para almoçar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow we will find a good place to have lunch.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu encontraria você na estação, mas estou doente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would meet you at the station, but I’m sick.

definitions.native: (for us) to meet, (for us) to find
definitions.note: Personal infinitive (infinitivo pessoal), used with an explicit subject like “nós” (“we”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: É melhor encontrarmos um lugar tranquilo para conversar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s better for us to find a quiet place to talk.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Você encontrará a chave na gaveta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You will find the key in the drawer.

definitions.note: Third-person plural (they/you all) future tense of “encontrar”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles encontrarão um bom restaurante perto do hotel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They will find a good restaurant near the hotel.

definitions.note: Imperfect subjunctive form (used in hypothetical situations, often after “se” = “if”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se eu encontrasse as chaves, eu te avisaria.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If I found the keys, I would let you know.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Encontraste as chaves?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Did you find the keys?

definitions.note: Imperfect past tense; can describe an ongoing past action or a habitual past action.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu encontrava sempre as minhas chaves na mochila.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I always found my keys in my backpack.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (eu) or imperative (você) form of "encontrar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que eu encontre as chaves hoje.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope I find the keys today.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito perfeito) of "encontrar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Encontrei minhas chaves no sofá.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I found my keys on the couch.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive form (used after expressions of desire, doubt, or commands with que).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que vocês encontrem a chave.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you find the key.

definitions.note: Used with “we” in the present subjunctive (often after que) or as a “let’s …” command.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que encontremos uma solução.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope we find a solution.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu encontro minhas chaves na bolsa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I find my keys in my bag.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu encontro meus amigos no café.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I meet my friends at the café.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tenho um encontro às três da tarde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a meeting at three in the afternoon.

definitions.note: Often used for a romantic meeting.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela vai ter um encontro com o namorado hoje à noite.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She’s going on a date with her boyfriend tonight.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Temos encontros todas as semanas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have meetings every week.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito perfeito) of "encontrar"; often used for either finding something or meeting someone.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela encontrou as chaves no sofá.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She found the keys on the couch.

definitions.note: Informal/colloquial spelling (common in Brazil) representing the pronunciation of "encontrar" with the final -r dropped.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vou te encontrá amanhã.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to meet you tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela me encorajou a tentar de novo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She encouraged me to try again.

definitions.note: Informal/colloquial shortened form of the infinitive “encorajar”, most common in Brazilian Portuguese before object pronouns (e.g., “encorajá-lo”, “encorajá-la”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vou encorajá-lo a tentar de novo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to encourage him to try again.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele encosta a bicicleta na parede.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He leans the bike against the wall.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O quadro está encostado na parede.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The picture is leaning against the wall.

definitions.note: Informal (often used to describe someone who doesn't work and lives off other people).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele está encostado e não quer procurar emprego.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He’s being idle and doesn’t want to look for a job.

definitions.native: to lean (something/someone) against; to rest (something) on
definitions.note: Often used with a preposition like “em”, “na/no” (e.g., encostar na parede = lean against the wall).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele vai encostar a bicicleta na parede.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is going to lean the bicycle against the wall.

definitions.note: Often used as a command (to você), especially for drivers.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Por favor, encoste o carro no acostamento.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please pull the car over onto the shoulder.

definitions.note: Can be used as a command (to você) or in the present subjunctive.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Encoste a escada na parede com cuidado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Lean the ladder against the wall carefully.

definitions.note: Past action: first person singular ("I"). Often used with "em/na/no" to mean leaning against something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Encostei na parede para descansar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I leaned against the wall to rest.

definitions.note: Often used informally for being in trouble or having a difficult situation to deal with.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Isso vai dar encrenca.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That’s going to cause trouble.

definitions.note: Often used in Brazil to describe a difficult situation, a person who gets into problems, or something that’s hard to deal with.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estou encrencado porque perdi a carteira.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m in trouble because I lost my wallet.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Precisamos encurtar a reunião.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need to shorten the meeting.

definitions.note: Usually refers to a street address (where someone lives or where a place is).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Qual é o seu endereço?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What is your address?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Anotei os endereços no meu caderno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I wrote down the addresses in my notebook.

definitions.note: Past subjunctive form of “endireitar” (also used in some requests/suggestions with “que”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se eu endireite a cadeira, ela para de balançar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If I straighten the chair, it stops wobbling.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Preciso de mais energia para terminar o trabalho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need more energy to finish the work.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O filme foi tão enfadonho que eu quase adormeci.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The movie was so boring that I almost fell asleep.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Compramos enfeites para a árvore de Natal.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We bought decorations for the Christmas tree.

definitions.note: A hospital section/ward where patients stay (sometimes a smaller clinic infirmary).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele ficou internado na enfermaria por três dias.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He stayed in the hospital ward for three days.

definitions.note: female nurse
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A minha mãe é enfermeira no hospital.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My mother is a nurse at the hospital.

definitions.note: feminine plural of “enfermeira” (female nurse)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: As enfermeiras trabalham no hospital.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The nurses work at the hospital.

definitions.note: Male nurse; often used generically for “nurse” in some contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O enfermeiro mediu a minha pressão arterial.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The nurse took my blood pressure.

definitions.note: plural masculine form; can also refer to a mixed-gender group
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os enfermeiros trabalham no hospital.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The nurses work at the hospital.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele ficou em casa por causa de uma enfermidade.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He stayed home because of an illness.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A bicicleta está enferrujada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bicycle is rusty.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A bicicleta ficou enferrujado depois de ficar na chuva.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bicycle got rusty after being left in the rain.

definitions.note: Often implies inserting/pushing something into a tight space (like “shove in”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele enfia a chave na fechadura.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He puts the key in the lock.

definitions.native: to put in, to stick in, to shove in
definitions.note: Often used for putting something inside a tight space or in a forceful way.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele vai enfiar as mãos nos bolsos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is going to stick his hands in his pockets.

definitions.note: Often used as a command (imperative).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Enfie a chave na fechadura.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Stick the key in the lock.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Enfim chegamos em casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We finally got home.

definitions.note: Often used to wrap up what you’re saying or move on to the next point in conversation.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Enfim, vamos começar a reunião.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Anyway, let’s start the meeting.

definitions.native: stuck in, shoved in, put in
definitions.note: Past tense (he/she/it/you formal) of “enfiar”; often implies doing it quickly or forcefully.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele enfiou a chave na fechadura.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He stuck the key in the lock.

definitions.note: Past participle of "enforcar"; often used with "ser" to mean "to be hanged" (executed).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele foi enforcado na praça.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was hanged in the town square.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O enforcamento era uma forma de punição no passado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Hanging was a form of punishment in the past.

definitions.note: Usually used for execution or suicide; reflexive “se enforcar” = “to hang oneself.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vão enforcar o condenado ao amanhecer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are going to hang the condemned man at dawn.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele enforcou o quadro na parede.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He hung the picture on the wall.

definitions.note: Gerund form (ongoing action), often translated as “facing” or “confronting.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estamos enfrentando um problema difícil.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We are facing a difficult problem.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela teve de enfrentar muitos desafios no trabalho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She had to face many challenges at work.

definitions.note: Often used as a command (imperative) or in the present subjunctive of "enfrentar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Enfrente seus medos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Face your fears.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele enfrentou muitos desafios no trabalho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He faced many challenges at work.

definitions.note: Informal/colloquial spelling/pronunciation of "enfrentar" (dropping the final -r), common in speech and in casual writing.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu vou enfrentá amanhã.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to face it tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele ficou enfurecido com a mentira.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He got furious about the lie.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele engana todo mundo com essas histórias.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He deceives everyone with those stories.

definitions.note: feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela foi enganada pelo vendedor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She was fooled by the salesman.

definitions.note: Feminine singular past participle of "enganar"; often used like an adjective or with "ser/estar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela foi enganada pelo vendedor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She was tricked by the salesperson.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Você está enganado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You are mistaken.

definitions.note: Past participle of "enganar"; often used with "estar" to mean someone is mistaken.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Você está enganado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You are mistaken.

definitions.note: Past participle of "enganar"; can describe someone who was deceived.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele foi enganado pelo golpista.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was tricked by the scammer.

definitions.note: plural form; often used to describe people who were tricked or who believed something incorrect
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles estavam enganados sobre o horário da reunião.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They were mistaken about the time of the meeting.

definitions.note: Past participle (often used like an adjective).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Fomos enganados pelo vendedor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We were fooled by the salesperson.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles enganam os clientes com promessas falsas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They deceive the customers with false promises.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nós enganamos o turista com uma história falsa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We tricked the tourist with a false story.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Você está me enganando?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Are you tricking me?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele tentou me enganar, mas eu percebi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He tried to deceive me, but I noticed.

definitions.native: to make a mistake, to be wrong
definitions.note: Often used reflexively: "enganar-se" = "to be mistaken".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu fui me enganar sobre o horário da reunião.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I ended up being mistaken about the time of the meeting.

definitions.native: they deceived, they tricked, they fooled
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles enganaram o cliente com uma promessa falsa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They tricked the customer with a false promise.

definitions.note: Commonly used as a (formal) command (e.g., to você) or in the present subjunctive.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Por favor, não me engane.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please don't trick me.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Enganei o vendedor e paguei menos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I fooled the seller and paid less.

definitions.native: I made a mistake, I got it wrong
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Desculpa, enganei-me no número.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Sorry, I got the number wrong.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Desculpe, foi um engano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Sorry, it was a mistake.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele me enganou com aquela história.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He tricked me with that story.

definitions.note: Informal spoken/colloquial form of "enganar" (often dropping the final -r).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele tentou me engan, mas eu percebi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He tried to trick me, but I noticed.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Houve um engarrafamento enorme na estrada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There was a huge traffic jam on the road.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele engasga quando come muito rápido.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He chokes when he eats too fast.

definitions.note: Commonly used for choking on food/drink or gagging; can also be used figuratively (e.g., “choked up” while speaking).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele engasgou com um pedaço de pão.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He choked on a piece of bread.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela estuda engenharia na universidade.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She studies engineering at the university.

definitions.note: Feminine form; used for a woman engineer.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A minha irmã é engenheira e trabalha numa ponte nova.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My sister is an engineer and works on a new bridge.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Meu irmão é engenheiro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My brother is an engineer.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os engenheiros estão a construir uma ponte nova.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The engineers are building a new bridge.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O mecanismo engenhoso economiza tempo e trabalho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The ingenious mechanism saves time and work.

definitions.note: Physical act of swallowing food, drink, or medicine.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu vou engolir o comprimido com água.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to swallow the pill with water.

definitions.note: To swallow quickly, often in one go.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele tentou engolir o café muito rápido e se queimou.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He tried to gulp down the coffee too fast and burned himself.

definitions.note: To accept something unpleasant, criticism, or an insult without reacting.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela teve que engolir a crítica em silêncio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She had to swallow the criticism in silence.

definitions.note: To process or absorb what one sees or hears.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu demorei para engolir a notícia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It took me a while to take in the news.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele engoliu o comprimido com água.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He swallowed the pill with water.

definitions.note: Present participle/gerund form of "engordar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu estou engordando porque estou comendo muito doce.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m gaining weight because I’m eating a lot of sweets.

definitions.native: to gain weight; to put on weight; to fatten (oneself/someone/something up)
definitions.note: Used for people or animals; can also be used for things like food when it ‘fattens’ (makes you gain weight).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu comecei a engordar no ano passado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I started to gain weight last year.

definitions.note: Past tense (he/she/it/you formal) of “engordar”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele engordou no último ano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He gained weight in the last year.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela quer engravidar este ano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She wants to get pregnant this year.

definitions.note: Commonly used for becoming pregnant (often about a woman).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela engravidou no ano passado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She got pregnant last year.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vou engraxar os sapatos antes da entrevista.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to shine my shoes before the interview.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form of the adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela é muito engraçada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is very funny.

definitions.note: feminine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: As histórias dela são engraçadas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Her stories are funny.

definitions.note: Often used to describe something humorous, but it can also mean something is strange depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O filme foi muito engraçado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The movie was very funny.

definitions.note: Commonly used when something seems unusual or suspicious (tone and context matter).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: É engraçado ele não ter respondido.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s strange that he didn’t reply.

definitions.note: Plural masculine form. Can also mean “amusing” or “weird” depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles são muito engraçados.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are very funny.

definitions.note: Used as a command (imperative, e.g. for você) or as the present subjunctive form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Engula o remédio com água.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Swallow the medicine with water.

definitions.note: Often used figuratively (e.g., to ‘swallow’ your pride or accept something you don’t like).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu engulo o remédio com água.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I swallow the medicine with water.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A origem desse objeto é um enigma.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The origin of that object is a mystery.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Depois da viagem de ônibus, ele ficou enjoado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the bus trip, he felt nauseated.

definitions.note: Often used with "com" (e.g., "enjoado com" = fed up/bored with).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele está enjoado com a mesma comida todos os dias.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is fed up with the same food every day.

definitions.note: Often used for motion sickness (car/sea/air sickness).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Senti enjoo durante a viagem de carro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I felt nauseous during the car trip.

definitions.note: Often used for food that comes in a can.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Comprei sopa enlatada porque é mais rápida.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought canned soup because it’s quicker.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estou enlouquecendo com esse barulho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going crazy with this noise.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Esse barulho está me enlouquecendo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This noise is driving me crazy.

definitions.native: to go crazy, to lose one's mind
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Depois de tantas noites sem dormir, ele começou a enlouquecer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After so many nights without sleep, he started to go crazy.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Depois da notícia, ele enlouqueceu.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the news, he went crazy.

definitions.note: From the verb “enojar.” Often used with “me/te/lhe” (e.g., “isso me enoja” = “that disgusts me”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A sujeira na cozinha enoja muita gente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dirtiness in the kitchen disgusts a lot of people.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele ficou enojado com a situação.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He got angry about the situation.

definitions.note: It can also mean “disgust” depending on context. Not related to English “enjoy.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: As crianças enojam os pais com tanta bagunça.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The children annoy their parents with so much mess.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O prédio é enorme.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The building is huge.

definitions.note: Plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles têm problemas enormes para resolver.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They have huge problems to solve.

definitions.note: Often introduces an action happening at the same time as another.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Enquanto eu cozinho, ele põe a mesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: While I cook, he sets the table.

definitions.note: Used to contrast two ideas.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela gosta de café, enquanto eu prefiro chá.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She likes coffee, whereas I prefer tea.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gostei do enredo do filme.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I liked the plot of the movie.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O tapete está enrolado no canto da sala.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The rug is rolled up in the corner of the living room.

definitions.note: In informal Brazilian Portuguese, this often describes a situation (or sometimes a person) that is difficult or full of problems.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estou com tudo enrolado esta semana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have everything complicated/messy this week.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estou enrolando o cabo para guardar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m rolling up the cable to store it.

definitions.note: Common in Brazilian Portuguese in informal speech, meaning to delay or avoid doing something (or to keep someone waiting without a clear answer).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele está me enrolando e não diz se vai ou não.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He’s stalling me and won’t say whether he’s going or not.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vou enrolar o cabo para guardar na gaveta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to roll up the cable to store it in the drawer.

definitions.note: Informal; often means delaying on purpose or avoiding doing something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele vai enrolar para responder ao e-mail.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He’s going to stall before answering the email.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela enrolou o tapete e guardou no armário.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She rolled up the rug and put it away in the closet.

definitions.note: In everyday Brazilian Portuguese, "enrolar" is often used informally to mean delaying or stalling instead of doing something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele enrolou a entrega e só mandou o arquivo hoje.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He delayed the delivery and only sent the file today.

definitions.note: Often used for practicing a performance (music, theater, dance) or trying something out.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estamos ensaiando para o concerto de amanhã.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re rehearsing for tomorrow’s concert.

definitions.native: to rehearse, to practice (for a performance)

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re going to rehearse the play tomorrow.
