definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is very studious and always does his homework.

definitions.note: Often used as an adjective too (“studious”), but here it’s a noun.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O estudioso apresentou uma nova teoria sobre o tema.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The scholar presented a new theory on the topic.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: À noite, estudo em casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At night, I study at home.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O estudo é importante para passar no exame.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Studying is important to pass the exam.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Meus estudos são muito importantes para mim.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My studies are very important to me.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito perfeito): completed action in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela estudou para a prova ontem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She studied for the test yesterday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tomates crescem bem na estufa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomatoes grow well in the greenhouse.

definitions.note: In Brazilian Portuguese, this is the common word for a kitchen stove; in European Portuguese, it can also mean a heater.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A panela está no fogo da estufa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The pot is on the stove burner.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: As estufas ajudam a cultivar legumes no inverno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Greenhouses help grow vegetables in the winter.

definitions.note: In Brazil, this can refer to a portable heater used to warm a room.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No frio, ligamos as estufas para aquecer a casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the cold, we turn on the heaters to warm the house.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Foi uma estupidez eu ter esquecido o passaporte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It was stupid of me to forget my passport.

definitions.note: feminine singular past participle (used to describe a woman or girl)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela foi estuprada e procurou ajuda imediatamente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She was raped and sought help immediately.

definitions.note: Past participle of "estuprar"; often used with "ser"/"estar" (e.g., "foi/está estuprado").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele disse que foi estuprado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He said he was raped.

definitions.note: Strong, criminal term; avoid using casually.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele foi preso por estuprar uma mulher.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was arrested for raping a woman.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela denunciou o estupro à polícia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She reported the rape to the police.

definitions.note: used as an auxiliary with a gerund to form the present continuous
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela está lendo um livro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is reading a book.

definitions.note: From "estar"; often used for temporary states, ongoing actions, and location.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A chave está na mesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The key is on the table.

definitions.note: Form of the verb "estar" (used for location or temporary states).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele está em casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is at home.

definitions.note: Place where farm animals (especially horses) are kept.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os cavalos estão no estábulo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The horses are in the stable.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os cavalos ficam nos estábulos à noite.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The horses stay in the stables at night.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O jogo vai ser no estádio amanhã.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The game will be at the stadium tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela começou um estágio numa empresa de tecnologia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She started an internship at a tech company.

definitions.note: Second-person singular (tu) form; often used informally.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu estás em casa?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Are you at home?

definitions.note: Second-person singular (tu) form of "estar" (informal "you" in most of Brazil; common in Portugal).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu estás bem?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Are you okay?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Há uma estátua no centro da praça.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is a statue in the center of the square.

definitions.note: Plural of "estátua".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Há três estátuas na praça.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are three statues in the square.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (past), used for ongoing states/situations and as an auxiliary in compound tenses.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nós estávamos em casa quando ele chegou.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We were at home when he arrived.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense, 1st person plural ("we"); often implies an ongoing situation in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quando você ligou, estávamos em casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When you called, we were at home.

definitions.note: 2nd person plural (vós) imperfect of the auxiliary verb "estar"; used mainly in European Portuguese or formal contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quando chegámos, já estáveis prontos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When we arrived, you were already ready.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A situação está estável agora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The situation is stable now.

definitions.note: used as an auxiliary with a gerund to form the progressive, like English "are ...-ing"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles estão estudando para a prova.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are studying for the test.

definitions.note: Used for location and for states or conditions that are usually temporary.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os meus amigos estão no café.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My friends are at the café.

definitions.note: Often used to mean a fictional or made-up story (as opposed to “história,” which can also mean history).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele contou uma estória para as crianças antes de dormir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He told a story to the children before going to sleep.

definitions.note: Less common spelling; often used to emphasize fictional stories (as opposed to factual history).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele contou estórias para as crianças antes de dormir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He told stories to the children before going to sleep.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Meu estômago dói depois do almoço.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My stomach hurts after lunch.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O estúdio fica perto do centro da cidade.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The studio is near the city center.

definitions.note: Feminine form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Foi uma ideia estúpida.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It was a stupid idea.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Essas perguntas são estúpidas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Those questions are stupid.

definitions.note: Can be insulting; use carefully.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Isso foi estúpido de se dizer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That was stupid to say.

definitions.note: Plural masculine form; can be insulting.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Esses comentários são estúpidos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Those comments are stupid.

definitions.note: gerund form (like “-ing” in English), used to describe an action in progress
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estou esvaziando a caixa para reciclar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m emptying the box to recycle it.

definitions.note: Used for making something become empty (a container, a room, a bank account, etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Preciso esvaziar a caixa antes de fechar a loja.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to empty the box before closing the store.

definitions.note: Usually used as a command (imperative) or in the present subjunctive (e.g., after “que”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Por favor, esvazie a lixeira.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please empty the trash can.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele esvaziou a garrafa antes de jogar fora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He emptied the bottle before throwing it away.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A próxima etapa do projeto é fazer os testes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The next stage of the project is to do the tests.

definitions.note: Short for “et cetera”; used at the end of a list to mean there are more similar items.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Preciso comprar pão, leite, ovos, etc.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to buy bread, milk, eggs, etc.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form (used with feminine nouns).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela fez uma promessa eterna.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She made an eternal promise.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vou te amar eternamente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will love you forever.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Parece que estou esperando há uma eternidade.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It feels like I’ve been waiting for an eternity.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O amor de mãe parece eterno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A mother's love seems eternal.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Coloquei uma etiqueta na mala com o meu nome.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I put a label on the suitcase with my name.

definitions.note: Rules of polite behavior; often used in formal/social contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: É importante conhecer a etiqueta em eventos formais.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s important to know etiquette at formal events.

definitions.note: Often omitted in Portuguese when the subject is clear from the verb.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu moro em Lisboa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I live in Lisbon.

definitions.note: Currency used in many European countries.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este café custa dois euros.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This coffee costs two euros.

definitions.note: feminine singular form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela é europeia e mora em Lisboa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is European and lives in Lisbon.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele tem passaporte europeu.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He has a European passport.

definitions.note: Plural masculine form (also used for mixed-gender groups).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os turistas europeus visitaram Lisboa no verão.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The European tourists visited Lisbon in the summer.

definitions.note: plural masculine form; can also refer to a mixed-gender group
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Muitos europeus viajam de trem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Many Europeans travel by train.

definitions.note: Plural of euro (the currency).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tenho dez euros na carteira.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have ten euros in my wallet.

definitions.note: Past participle of "evacuar"; often used with "ser" (passive) or "ter" (compound tense).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O prédio foi evacuado por causa do incêndio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The building was evacuated because of the fire.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os bombeiros evacuaram o prédio por causa do incêndio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The firefighters evacuated the building because of the fire.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A evacuação do prédio começou às dez horas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The evacuation of the building started at ten o’clock.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (vocês/eles/elas) and also the formal command form (vocês).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Em caso de incêndio, evacuem o prédio imediatamente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In case of fire, evacuate the building immediately.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O evento começa às oito da noite.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The event starts at eight at night.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Há muitos eventos na cidade este fim de semana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are many events in the city this weekend.

definitions.note: In Portuguese, it often means “occasionally” or “from time to time,” not necessarily “in the end.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eventualmente, eu trabalho aos sábados.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Occasionally, I work on Saturdays.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela eventualmente vai ao cinema com os amigos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She occasionally goes to the movies with her friends.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: É evidente que precisamos de mais tempo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It's obvious that we need more time.

definitions.note: Often used to show something is clear or follows logically; can also suggest “apparently” depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Evidentemente, ele não leu o e-mail.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Evidently, he didn’t read the email.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A polícia encontrou evidência suficiente para prender o suspeito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police found enough evidence to arrest the suspect.

definitions.note: Plural.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A polícia reuniu várias evidências no local do crime.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police gathered various pieces of evidence at the crime scene.

definitions.note: Present tense form of "evitar" (he/she/it avoids; you avoid in formal address).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele evita conflitos no trabalho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He avoids conflicts at work.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O conflito foi evitado graças ao diálogo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The conflict was avoided thanks to dialogue.

definitions.note: Present participle/gerund of "evitar"; often used to mean "while avoiding" or after "estar" to form the progressive tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estou evitando comer açúcar esta semana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m avoiding eating sugar this week.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tento evitar comer açúcar durante a semana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I try to avoid eating sugar during the week.

definitions.note: Often used as a formal command (imperative) or as the present subjunctive form of “evitar.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Evite falar alto na biblioteca.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Avoid speaking loudly in the library.

definitions.note: Present tense (eu).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu evito comer açúcar durante a semana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I avoid eating sugar during the week.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele evitou falar sobre o assunto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He avoided talking about the subject.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A evolução da tecnologia mudou a nossa vida.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The evolution of technology changed our lives.

definitions.note: Often used to talk about improvement or how something changes over time (e.g., a situation, a disease, a project).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O médico ficou satisfeito com a evolução do paciente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The doctor was pleased with the patient's progress.

definitions.note: Used before a noun to refer to a person’s former partner (or, more generally, someone/something that used to be in that role). Often written with a hyphen: “ex-namorado”, “ex-marido”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O meu ex não vai à festa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My ex isn’t going to the party.

definitions.note: Used to refer to someone you used to date or be married to.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Encontrei a minha ex no supermercado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I ran into my ex at the supermarket.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele exagera quando conta histórias.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He exaggerates when he tells stories.

definitions.note: Present participle/gerund of "exagerar"; often used with "estar" to mean someone is in the act of exaggerating.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Você está exagerando na história.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You’re exaggerating in the story.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele tende a exagerar quando conta essa história.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He tends to exaggerate when he tells that story.

definitions.note: Used in the present subjunctive (e.g. after expressions like “não acho que…”) and can also be used as a formal command.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Não acho que ele exagere quando fala do problema.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't think he exaggerates when he talks about the problem.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Desculpa, exagerei na brincadeira.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Sorry, I overdid the joke.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Isso é um exagero.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is an exaggeration.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Você exagerou na quantidade de sal.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You exaggerated with the amount of salt.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tenho um exame amanhã.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have an exam tomorrow.

definitions.note: Often used for medical tests or examinations (e.g., blood tests, imaging).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O médico pediu um exame de sangue.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The doctor ordered a blood test.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tenho dois exames esta semana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have two exams this week.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O médico pediu alguns exames de sangue.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The doctor ordered some blood tests.

definitions.note: past participle of "examinar"; often used with "ser" (passive) or "ter" (perfect)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O paciente foi examinado pelo médico.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The patient was examined by the doctor.

definitions.note: Present participle/gerund form, often used with "estar" to express an action in progress.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O médico está examinando o paciente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The doctor is examining the patient.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O médico vai examinar o paciente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The doctor is going to examine the patient.

definitions.note: In Portuguese, this verb can also mean to test someone (e.g., by giving an exam).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O professor vai examinar os alunos amanhã.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The teacher is going to test the students tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O médico examine o paciente com atenção.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The doctor examines the patient carefully.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito perfeito) of “examinar” (ele/ela/você).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O médico examinou o paciente com cuidado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The doctor examined the patient carefully.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A resposta exata está no final do livro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The exact answer is at the end of the book.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: É exatamente isso que eu queria dizer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That’s exactly what I wanted to say.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Não sei a hora exato, mas é por volta das três.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't know the exact time, but it's around three.

definitions.note: Often used alone as an interjection to show agreement (like “exactly!” or “that’s right!”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: — Então a reunião é às três? — Exato!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: — So the meeting is at three? — Exactly!

definitions.note: feminine singular form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Depois do trabalho, ela ficou exausta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After work, she was exhausted.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Depois da viagem, fiquei exausto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the trip, I was exhausted.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Depois da caminhada, eles ficaram exaustos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the hike, they were exhausted.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O filme foi excelente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The movie was excellent.

definitions.note: Plural form (masculine or feminine), used with plural nouns.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os resultados foram excelentes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The results were excellent.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A excelência do serviço foi elogiada por todos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The excellence of the service was praised by everyone.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela fez um trabalho excepcional este semestre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She did an exceptional job this semester.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hoje, o trânsito está excepcionalmente calmo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today, traffic is exceptionally calm.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O excesso de açúcar faz mal à saúde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Too much sugar is bad for your health.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Todos vão à festa, exceto o João.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Everyone is going to the party, except João.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Há uma exceção a essa regra.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is an exception to that rule.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Há algumas exceções a essa regra.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are some exceptions to that rule.

definitions.note: Often used like English “excited,” but it can also mean “sexually aroused,” so be careful with context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estou excitada com a viagem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m excited about the trip.

definitions.note: It can also mean “sexually aroused,” so be careful with the context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estou muito excitado para a viagem amanhã.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m very excited for the trip tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Foi um jogo excitante até ao fim.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It was an exciting game until the end.

definitions.note: Often used with sexual meaning depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela achou o filme muito excitante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She found the movie very arousing.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Decidimos excluir esse item da lista.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We decided to exclude that item from the list.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito perfeito) of “excluir” (he/she/it excluded).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O professor excluiu o aluno do grupo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The teacher excluded the student from the group.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele foi excluído da lista.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was excluded from the list.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Fizemos uma excursão de um dia para a serra.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We took a one-day excursion to the mountains.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O professor é excêntrico, mas muito inteligente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The teacher is eccentric, but very intelligent.

definitions.note: Often used as a past participle in passive constructions.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O plano foi executado com sucesso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The plan was carried out successfully.

definitions.note: Often used with tasks, plans, commands, or procedures (e.g., executar um plano).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A equipe vai executar o plano amanhã.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The team will carry out the plan tomorrow.

definitions.note: Often used for the act of carrying out a plan or task (e.g., execução de um projeto). In legal contexts it can also mean execution (capital punishment), but that meaning is less common in everyday speech.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A execução do projeto começou ontem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The execution of the project started yesterday.

definitions.note: Often used to describe behavior, conduct, or performance that should be imitated.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela teve uma atitude exemplar durante a crise.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She had exemplary behavior during the crisis.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este é um bom exemplo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This is a good example.

definitions.note: Plural of "exemplo".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vou dar alguns exemplos para explicar melhor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to give some examples to explain better.

definitions.note: Often used for practicing a profession or carrying out a function/right (e.g., “exercer uma profissão”, “exercer um cargo”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela quer exercer a profissão de médica.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She wants to practice the profession of a doctor.

definitions.note: Often used for 3rd person singular (he/she exercises); it can also be used as an affirmative command to "tu" (informal): "Exercita!"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela se exercita todos os dias.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She exercises every day.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu tento exercitar todos os dias.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The word was spoken clearly.

definitions.note: Often used to mean someone/something is being discussed or rumored about (e.g., “bem falada”, “mal falada”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela é muito falada na cidade.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is talked about a lot in the town.

definitions.note: past participle (feminine plural) of "falar"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: As palavras foram faladas em voz baixa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The words were spoken in a low voice.

definitions.note: Often used in set phrases like “língua falada” (spoken language).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O português falado no Brasil é diferente do português falado em Portugal.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The Portuguese spoken in Brazil is different from the Portuguese spoken in Portugal.

definitions.note: Past participle of "falar"; often used with "ter/haver" (compound tenses) or as an adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu tenho falado com ela todos os dias.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have spoken with her every day.

definitions.note: Past participle (plural masculine) of "falar"; often used with "ser" in the passive voice.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Esses assuntos já foram falados na reunião.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Those topics have already been spoken about in the meeting.

definitions.note: Third-person plural present (or second-person plural in European Portuguese, formal).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles falam português em casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They speak Portuguese at home.

definitions.note: Present tense ("we").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nós falamos português em casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We speak Portuguese at home.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite) ("we").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ontem falamos com o professor depois da aula.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday we talked to the teacher after class.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estamos falando sobre o filme.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We are talking about the movie.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela é muito falante e faz amigos com facilidade.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is very talkative and makes friends easily.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O falante respondeu às perguntas no final da palestra.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The speaker answered the questions at the end of the talk.

definitions.note: Usually refers to people who speak a language.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Há muitos falantes de português no Brasil.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are many Portuguese speakers in Brazil.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu gosto de falar com meus amigos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like to talk with my friends.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito perfeito), 3rd person plural: “they” (or “you all” in some regions).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles falaram comigo ontem à noite.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They spoke with me last night.

definitions.note: First-person singular ("I") in the simple future.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Amanhã falarei com ela sobre o projeto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow I will speak with her about the project.

definitions.native: (for them) to speak, (for them) to talk
definitions.note: Personal infinitive form of “falar”, used with an explicit or implied subject (e.g., “eles/elas”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: É melhor eles falarem com o professor amanhã.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s better for them to talk to the teacher tomorrow.

definitions.native: we will speak, we will talk
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Falaremos amanhã sobre o projeto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We will talk tomorrow about the project.

definitions.note: Conditional form of “falar”; often used for hypothetical situations or polite/indirect statements.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu falaria com ela, mas não tenho o número.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would speak with her, but I don't have her number.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive, 1st person plural (nós). Often used after expressions like “é importante que…”, “querem que…”, “antes que…”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: É importante que falarmos com calma.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s important that we speak calmly.

definitions.native: for us to speak, for us to talk
definitions.note: Personal infinitive (infinitivo pessoal), 1st person plural. Often used after prepositions like “para” and “sem”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles chamaram a reunião para falarmos sobre o projeto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They called the meeting for us to talk about the project.

definitions.note: Third-person singular (he/she/it/you formal) in the future tense of "falar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele falará com você amanhã.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He will speak with you tomorrow.

definitions.note: Plural of "fala" (noun). Often used for spoken lines in a play/movie or in conversation.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: As falas dos atores estavam bem decoradas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The actors’ lines were well memorized.

definitions.note: Second-person singular (tu) form; informal in many regions (especially common in Portugal).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu falas muito depressa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You speak very fast.

definitions.note: Imperfect subjunctive of “falar”; often used after expressions like “se” (if) or “como se” (as if).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se eu falasse mais devagar, você entenderia melhor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If I spoke more slowly, you would understand better.

definitions.note: Imperfect subjunctive (they/you all). Often used after expressions of doubt, desire, or conditions (e.g., 'se', 'queria que').
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu queria que eles falassem mais devagar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I wanted them to speak more slowly.

definitions.note: Informal singular (tu) past tense (pretérito perfeito). Common in Portugal; in Brazil, "você falou" is more common.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Falaste com a Maria ontem à noite?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Did you talk to Maria last night?

definitions.note: Imperfect past of “falar”: describes an ongoing/repeated action in the past (often “used to”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu falava com ela todos os dias.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I used to talk to her every day.

definitions.note: Imperfect past tense (they/you all were talking/used to talk).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles falavam baixo para não acordar o bebê.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They were speaking quietly so they wouldn’t wake the baby.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O falcão voou alto no céu.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The falcon flew high in the sky.

definitions.note: Most commonly the present subjunctive (você/ele/ela) or an affirmative command meaning “speak/talk!” (você).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Por favor, fale mais devagar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please, speak more slowly.

definitions.note: Commonly used in formal contexts (e.g., news, obituaries) to say someone passed away.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O meu avô faleceu no ano passado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My grandfather died last year.

definitions.note: Used to refer respectfully to a woman who has died (often: “a falecida” = “the deceased woman”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A falecida era muito querida pela família.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The deceased woman was very loved by the family.

definitions.note: Usually used in formal contexts to refer to someone who has died.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O falecido senhor Almeida era muito respeitado na cidade.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The late Mr. Almeida was very respected in the city.

definitions.note: Past (preterite) form of “falar” used to talk about a finished action in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu falei com a professora ontem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I spoke with the teacher yesterday.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (or imperative for vocês).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que vocês falem mais devagar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you speak more slowly.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive form of "falar"; commonly used to make suggestions (often after "vamos").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vamos falemos disso amanhã com calma.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let's talk about that tomorrow calmly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Houve uma falha no sistema.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There was a failure in the system.

definitions.note: Past participle of "falhar"; often used as an adjective meaning unsuccessful.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O plano falhado custou muito dinheiro à empresa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The failed plan cost the company a lot of money.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nós falhamos no teste.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We failed the test.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O plano pode falhar se não tivermos tempo suficiente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The plan can fail if we don’t have enough time.

definitions.note: Third-person plural (they/you all) past tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles falharam no teste.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They failed the test.

definitions.note: Often used for missing a shot/goal or not hitting a target.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles falharam o pênalti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They missed the penalty kick.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O relatório aponta várias falhas no sistema.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The report points out several flaws in the system.

definitions.note: Used after expressions like "espero que..." (subjunctive) or as a command like "não falhe" (imperative).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que você não falhe na prova.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you don’t fail the test.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu falhei na prova de matemática.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I failed the math test.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O plano falhou no último minuto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The plan failed at the last minute.

definitions.note: Often used about businesses, banks, or financial plans.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Muitas empresas faliram durante a crise.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Many companies went bankrupt during the crisis.

definitions.note: Past tense (simple past) form of “falir” used for he/she/it/you (formal).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A empresa faliu no ano passado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The company went bankrupt last year.

definitions.note: Present tense (eu) form of "falar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu falo português todos os dias.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I speak Portuguese every day.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito perfeito) form of "falar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele falou comigo ontem à noite.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He spoke with me last night.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Essa história é falsa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That story is false.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: As informações são falsas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The information is false.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A notícia era uma falsidade.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The news was a falsehood.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a crime to forge documents.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police investigated the forgery of documents.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele comprou um relógio falso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He bought a fake watch.

definitions.note: Often used to describe a person who pretends to be something they’re not.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele é um falso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He’s a fake.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Esses documentos são falsos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Those documents are false.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A falta de água é um problema aqui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The lack of water is a problem here.

definitions.note: Common in expressions like "por falta de" (= due to a lack of) and "foi falta minha" (= it was my fault).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Sorry, it was my fault.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele teve duas faltas esta semana.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Falta dinheiro para terminar o projeto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There isn’t enough money to finish the project.

definitions.note: Often used to talk about someone missing class, work, or an appointment.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She misses school today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Está faltando açúcar para o bolo.

definitions.note: Often used for missing something that is needed (e.g., time, money, an item).

definitions.note: Past tense (they/you all): often used to say something was missing or that people didn’t show up.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Two chairs were missing in the room.

definitions.note: Imperfect past (used for ongoing/repeated situations in the past).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There wasn’t enough money to pay the bill.

definitions.note: Imperfect past (used for ongoing/repeated situations in the past).

definitions.note: Often used to say something/someone was missing, or that there wasn’t enough of something.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There wasn’t enough money to pay the bill.

definitions.note: Often used to say someone missed an appointment/class or didn’t come.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She missed the meeting yesterday.

definitions.note: Often written with an accent in standard Portuguese: família.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My family is big.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este lugar me parece familiar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This place seems familiar to me.

definitions.note: Plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vou visitar os meus familiares neste fim de semana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to visit my relatives this weekend.

definitions.note: Often used with “com” (e.g., “familiarizado com”).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m familiar with the new system.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estou faminta depois da caminhada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m hungry after the walk.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the hike, I was starving.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is a famous singer in Brazil.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele é um cantor famoso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is a famous singer.

definitions.note: plural masculine (or mixed-gender) form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles são famosos no Brasil.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are famous in Brazil.

definitions.note: can be used as a noun meaning "famous people"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os famosos chegaram ao tapete vermelho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The celebrities arrived on the red carpet.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Minha família mora em Lisboa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My family lives in Lisbon.

definitions.note: Plural of "família".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: As famílias se reuniram para celebrar o aniversário da avó.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The families got together to celebrate the grandmother’s birthday.

definitions.note: Often used for a costume for a party or Carnival.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to buy a costume for Carnival.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A fantasia faz parte da infância.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Fantasy is part of childhood.

definitions.note: Plural. Often refers to costumes for parties/carnival; can also mean fictional imaginings depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: As crianças escolheram fantasias para o carnaval.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The children chose costumes for carnival.

definitions.note: As an adjective, it often means something is not real or exists only as a front (e.g., "empresa fantasma" = shell company). It doesn’t change form for masculine/feminine.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles descobriram que era uma empresa fantasma.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They found out it was a shell company.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela disse que viu um fantasma na casa antiga.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She said she saw a ghost in the old house.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: À noite, algumas pessoas dizem que veem fantasmas na casa antiga.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At night, some people say they see ghosts in the old house.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A viagem foi fantástica.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The trip was fantastic.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O filme foi fantástico.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The movie was fantastic.

definitions.note: Plural masculine form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os filmes foram fantásticos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The movies were fantastic.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He carried a bale of hay to the barn.

definitions.note: Also used figuratively for an emotional or moral weight.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Guardar esse segredo virou um fardo para ela.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Keeping that secret became a burden for her.

definitions.native: I will do, I will make

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Amanhã faremos o trabalho juntos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow we will do the work together.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would do that if I had time.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles fariam isso se tivessem tempo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They would do that if they had time.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What would you do if you won the lottery?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O cão tem um faro incrível.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My grandfather loves watching western movies.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O farol guia os navios durante a noite.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The lighthouse guides ships during the night.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The car’s headlight isn’t working.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the exam, we had a wild night out until dawn.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tudo isso foi uma farsa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: All of this was a farce.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form of "farto".

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After lunch, I'm full.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm fed up with waiting.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este relatório tem um gráfico muito claro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This report has a very clear graphic.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este gráfico mostra as vendas do último mês.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This chart shows last month's sales.

definitions.note: Often used after the noun: "entrada grátis" = "free entry".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A entrada é grátis.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Entry is free.

definitions.note: Used mainly for women.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela está grávida de quatro meses.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is four months pregnant.

definitions.note: Feminine form (used with women).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela está grávida de três meses.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is three months pregnant.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este pão tem grãos de trigo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This bread has wheat grains.

definitions.note: Plural of "grão"; often used for cereal grains or coffee beans depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Comprei grãos de café para fazer um café mais fresco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought coffee beans to make fresher coffee.

definitions.native: guaraná (a caffeine-rich Amazonian fruit); guaraná soda
definitions.note: In Brazil, it often refers to a popular soft drink made from (or flavored like) guaraná.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vou tomar um guaraná com gelo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to have a guaraná with ice.

definitions.note: Often used for a person whose job is to protect or watch over a place (e.g., a security guard). It can be used with either article: o guarda / a guarda.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O guarda está na entrada do prédio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The guard is at the entrance of the building.

definitions.note: From the verb "guardar"; often used for keeping/storing something in a place.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela guarda as chaves na bolsa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She keeps the keys in her bag.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Levei o guarda-chuva porque estava chovendo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I took the umbrella because it was raining.

definitions.note: Often used to mean something has been put away or saved for later.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O documento está guardado na pasta correta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The document is stored in the correct folder.

definitions.note: Past participle of "guardar"; often used with "ser/estar" or as an adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O documento foi guardado em uma pasta segura.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The document was saved in a safe folder.

definitions.note: Can also mean “we guard” or “we save,” depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Guardamos os documentos na gaveta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We keep the documents in the drawer.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Você pode me passar um guardanapo, por favor?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you pass me a napkin, please?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Preciso de dois guardanapos, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need two napkins, please.

definitions.note: Present participle/gerund of "guardar" (often used to mean "while keeping/storing" or "(is) keeping/storing").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estou guardando os documentos na gaveta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m keeping the documents in the drawer.

definitions.note: Present participle/gerund of "guardar" (often used to mean "while watching over" or "(is) looking after").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela está guardando as crianças enquanto eu trabalho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She’s looking after the kids while I work.

definitions.note: Often used for putting something away in a safe place or saving it for later.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vou guardar estas fotos numa caixa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to keep these photos in a box.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O cão vai guardar a casa à noite.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog will guard the house at night.

definitions.native: I will keep, I will save
definitions.note: First person singular (eu) in the future tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Guardarei este documento para você.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will keep this document for you.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os guardas vigiam a entrada do prédio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The guards watch the entrance to the building.

definitions.native: kept, was keeping, used to keep
definitions.note: Imperfect past form of "guardar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu guardava as chaves na gaveta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I used to keep the keys in the drawer.

definitions.note: Usually a formal command (“you” singular) or the present subjunctive (e.g., after expressions like “é importante que…”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Guarde este recibo, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please keep this receipt.

definitions.native: I kept, I saved, I put away
definitions.note: Past tense (pretérito perfeito) of "guardar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Guardei o dinheiro na carteira.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I put the money away in my wallet.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (vocês/eles/elas) or affirmative imperative (vocês) of "guardar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Guardem os documentos em um lugar seguro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Keep the documents in a safe place.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O guardião do museu fechou as portas às seis.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The museum’s guardian closed the doors at six.

definitions.note: Plural of "guardião".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os guardiões do parque fecham os portões às seis.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The park’s guardians close the gates at six.

definitions.note: Often used in the sense of keeping/storing something for later.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu guardo este documento no meu computador.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I keep this document on my computer.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito perfeito) of “guardar” (ele/ela/você).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela guardou as chaves na bolsa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She kept the keys in her purse.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito perfeito) of “guardar” (ele/ela/você).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele guardou os brinquedos depois de brincar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He put away the toys after playing.

definitions.note: Common colloquial spoken form of “guardar” (to keep/store), especially in Brazilian Portuguese.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pode guardá isso pra mim?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you keep this for me?

definitions.note: Often used for the food served alongside the main dish.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O peixe vem com arroz e salada como guarnição.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The fish comes with rice and salad as a side dish.

definitions.note: In a military context, it refers to the soldiers stationed in a place.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A cidade tinha uma guarnição pequena.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The city had a small garrison.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ontem à noite, vimos um guaxinim perto do lixo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Last night, we saw a raccoon near the trash.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A guerra acabou depois de muitos anos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The war ended after many years.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: As guerras mudaram a história do país.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The wars changed the country’s history.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O guerreiro voltou para casa depois da batalha.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The warrior returned home after the battle.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os guerreiros voltaram para a aldeia depois da batalha.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The warriors returned to the village after the battle.

definitions.note: Often refers to irregular armed groups or the type of fighting they use.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A guerrilha controlava algumas áreas remotas do país.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The guerrillas controlled some remote areas of the country.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O guia explicou a história da cidade.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The guide explained the history of the city.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Comprei um guia de viagem para o Porto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought a travel guidebook for Porto.

definitions.note: Present participle/gerund form of "guiar"; often used with "estar" to talk about an action in progress.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela está guiando o grupo pelo museu.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is guiding the group through the museum.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O professor vai guiar os alunos durante a visita ao museu.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The teacher is going to guide the students during the visit to the museum.

definitions.note: Common in contexts like driving a car (especially in European Portuguese).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela sabe guiar muito bem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She knows how to drive very well.

definitions.note: Plural of “guia”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os guias do museu falam inglês e português.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The museum guides speak English and Portuguese.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O guincho chegou para levar o carro quebrado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The tow truck arrived to take the broken-down car.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O guincho puxou o barco para fora da água.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The winch pulled the boat out of the water.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O guindaste levantou a viga de aço com cuidado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The crane lifted the steel beam carefully.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito perfeito) of “guiar” for ele/ela/você.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela guiou o grupo até a entrada do museu.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She guided the group to the museum entrance.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hoje vamos comer um guisado de carne com batatas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today we’re going to eat a meat stew with potatoes.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu toco guitarra todos os dias.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I play guitar every day.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A guitarrista toca muito bem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The guitarist plays very well.

definitions.note: Common in Brazilian Portuguese as a colloquial shortened form of "guiar" in speech or informal writing.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Deixa eu te guiá até a saída.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let me guide you to the exit.

definitions.note: Common in southern Brazil (especially Rio Grande do Sul); informal.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O guri está brincando na rua.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The boy is playing in the street.

definitions.note: Usually masculine: o gás.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O gás acabou e precisamos comprar outro botijão.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The gas ran out and we need to buy another gas cylinder.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O gângster foi preso pela polícia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The gangster was arrested by the police.

definitions.note: Feminine form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela tem uma irmã gêmea.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has a twin sister.

definitions.note: feminine plural; can refer to twin girls/women or to the twins (feminine form).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: As gêmeas estudam na mesma escola.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The twins study at the same school.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form; used for twin girls/women or feminine plural nouns.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: As irmãs são gêmeas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The sisters are twins.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O meu irmão é gêmeo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My brother is a twin.

definitions.note: Plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os gêmeos têm o mesmo aniversário.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The twins have the same birthday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Na ficha, você precisa indicar seu gênero.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: On the form, you need to indicate your gender.

definitions.note: Common for categories like music, movies, and books.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Qual é o gênero desse filme?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What genre is this movie?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela é um gênio em matemática.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is a genius at math.

definitions.note: Used for a magical being (like in stories); in Portuguese, this sense is less common than “gênio” = “genius”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No filme, o gênio sai da lâmpada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the movie, the genie comes out of the lamp.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Passeamos de gôndola pelos canais de Veneza.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We took a gondola ride through the canals of Venice.

definitions.note: Common in stores/supermarkets in Brazil to refer to the shelving units where products are displayed.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O arroz fica na gôndola do corredor três.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The rice is on the shelf in aisle three.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela tem muita habilidade para resolver problemas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has a lot of skill in solving problems.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela tem muitas habilidades em programação.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has many programming skills.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele é um cozinheiro muito habilidoso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is a very skillful cook.

definitions.note: Often used for professional or legal eligibility (e.g., qualification to do a job or to drive).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela tem a habilitação necessária para o cargo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has the qualification required for the position.

definitions.note: In Brazil, this commonly refers to the driver’s license (CNH).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Esqueci minha habilitação em casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I forgot my driver’s license at home.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os habitantes desta cidade são muito simpáticos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The inhabitants of this city are very friendly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: É habitual ele chegar cedo ao trabalho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s usual for him to arrive early to work.

definitions.note: Often refers either to a computer expert (can be positive) or someone who illegally breaks into systems (negative), depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele é um hacker e trabalha com segurança digital.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is a hacker and works with digital security.

definitions.note: Borrowed from English; often refers to people who break into computer systems (sometimes also used more broadly for skilled programmers).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A polícia prendeu dois hackers depois do ataque ao site.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police arrested two hackers after the attack on the website.

definitions.note: Used mainly in the subjunctive (often after que, like in “Espero que haja…”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que haja tempo para conversar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope there is time to talk.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu quero um hambúrguer com queijo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want a hamburger with cheese.

definitions.note: Plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nós pedimos dois hambúrgueres e uma batata frita.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We ordered two burgers and a portion of fries.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A harmonia entre os membros da equipa melhorou muito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The harmony among the team members improved a lot.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela toca harpa na orquestra.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She plays the harp in the orchestra.

definitions.note: Used mainly as a Japanese loanword in anime/manga contexts (especially Demon Slayer) to refer to an elite warrior/rank.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No anime, a Shinobu é uma hashira.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the anime, Shinobu is a Hashira.

definitions.note: Often used impersonally (like “there being …”), especially in formal written Portuguese.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Havendo vagas, entraremos em contato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If there are vacancies, we will get in touch.

definitions.note: Can introduce a cause/condition in more formal Portuguese (similar to “having done/being …”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Havendo terminado o trabalho, fomos embora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Having finished the work, we left.

definitions.note: Often used impersonally (3rd person singular) with the sense of “there is/are/was/were.” In more formal registers it can also function as an auxiliary similar to “ter” (e.g., “havia dito”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pode haver um problema.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There may be a problem.

definitions.note: Conditional form of haver; common in formal or written Portuguese.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se eu tivesse mais tempo, haveria mais reuniões esta semana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If I had more time, there would be more meetings this week.

definitions.note: Future tense of "haver" used in the impersonal sense (like "there is/are").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Haverá uma reunião amanhã.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There will be a meeting tomorrow.

definitions.note: Imperfect past of the auxiliary verb "haver" used impersonally to mean "there was/there were" (often in more formal Portuguese).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Havia muitas pessoas na festa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There were many people at the party.

definitions.note: Often used impersonally to mean “there was/there were.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Havia muita gente na praça.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There were a lot of people in the square.

definitions.note: Used as an auxiliary with a past participle (like English “had + past participle”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela havia terminado o trabalho antes do almoço.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She had finished the work before lunch.

definitions.note: Often used in impersonal expressions meaning “there was/there were,” especially in writing; in everyday speech many people use “tinha” instead.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Haviam muitas pessoas na rua.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There were many people in the street.

definitions.note: Imperfect past of "haver" used impersonally to mean "there were" (existence).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Naquela época, haviam muitas pessoas na praça.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At that time, there were many people in the square.

definitions.note: Past participle of "haver", commonly used in expressions like "tem/tinha havido" = "there has/have/had been".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tem havido muitos problemas ultimamente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There have been many problems lately.

definitions.note: Commonly written as “HD” in Portuguese.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O hd do meu computador está cheio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My computer’s hard drive is full.

definitions.note: Often used when talking about video/image quality; commonly written as “HD”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este vídeo está em hd.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This video is in HD.

definitions.note: Can refer to the Hebrew language or a Hebrew person (often in historical/biblical contexts).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu estudo hebraico na universidade.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I study Hebrew at the university.

definitions.note: Strongly negative; often used for crimes, smells, or actions considered extremely unpleasant or shocking.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O cheiro no lixo estava hediondo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The smell in the trash was hideous.

definitions.note: Used to get someone’s attention or as an informal greeting.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hei, você pode me ajudar?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Hey, can you help me?

definitions.note: Used mainly in the expression “Heil Hitler”, associated with Nazi ideology; considered offensive.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O professor explicou o significado histórico da expressão “Heil Hitler”.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The teacher explained the historical meaning of the expression “Heil Hitler”.

definitions.note: Used in informal speech to show you didn’t understand, didn’t hear, or to ask for confirmation (similar to “huh?” or “eh?”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Heim? Não entendi o que você disse.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Huh? I didn’t understand what you said.

definitions.note: Used to ask someone to repeat what they said, show surprise/confusion, or ask for confirmation (similar to “huh?”/“eh?” in English).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hein? Eu não entendi o que você disse.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Huh? I didn't understand what you said.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O helicóptero pousou perto do hospital.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The helicopter landed near the hospital.

definitions.note: Used to ask someone to repeat, or to show you didn’t understand / to ask for confirmation.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hem? Não entendi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Huh? I didn’t understand.

definitions.note: In everyday Portuguese, people often say "hematoma" for a larger or more serious bruise.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He ended up with a big bruise on his leg.

definitions.note: Medical term; commonly used in serious contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O médico disse que a hemorragia precisava ser controlada rapidamente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The doctor said the hemorrhage needed to be controlled quickly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela recebeu uma herança do avô.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She received an inheritance from her grandfather.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O herdeiro recebeu a casa do avô.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The heir received his grandfather’s house.

definitions.note: plural of "herdeiro"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os herdeiros assinaram os documentos da herança.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The heirs signed the inheritance documents.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela herdou a casa dos avós.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She inherited her grandparents’ house.

definitions.note: Female hero; can also mean the drug “heroin” in Portuguese, but that sense is not covered here.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A heroína do filme salva a cidade no final.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The heroine of the movie saves the city at the end.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O herói salvou a cidade.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The hero saved the city.

definitions.note: plural of “herói”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os heróis da história são muito corajosos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The heroes in the story are very brave.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was hesitant before answering.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Não vou hesitar em pedir ajuda se precisar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I won’t hesitate to ask for help if I need it.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t hesitate to call me if you need help.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She hesitated before answering.

definitions.note: Used to get someone's attention or greet someone (informal).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hey, tudo bem?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Hey, how are you?

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I do water aerobics twice a week.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Water is made up of hydrogen and oxygen.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A higiene é importante para a saúde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Hygiene is important for health.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O filme é hilário.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The movie is hilarious.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are many Hindus in India.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles fizeram uma hipoteca para comprar a casa.
