definitions.example_sentence_target_language: As almofadas estão macias.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The pillows are soft.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A macieira do quintal já está cheia de maçãs.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The apple tree in the backyard is already full of apples.

definitions.note: Plural of "macieira".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Há muitas macieiras no pomar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are many apple trees in the orchard.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este sofá é muito macio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This sofa is very soft.

definitions.note: Informal/common term; refers to cannabis used as a drug.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele foi preso por vender maconha.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was arrested for selling marijuana.

definitions.note: Used as a polite form of address for a woman; in Portuguese it’s often used with a French feel and is less common than "senhora" in everyday speech.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Madame, posso ajudá-la?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Madam, can I help you?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Esta mesa é de madeira.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This table is made of wood.

definitions.note: Proper noun: the name of a Portuguese island/region.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vamos visitar a Madeira no verão.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re going to visit Madeira in the summer.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A minha madrasta é muito simpática.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My stepmother is very nice.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A minha madrinha me deu um presente no meu aniversário.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My godmother gave me a present on my birthday.

definitions.note: In weddings, this can mean a bridesmaid; it often refers to the maid of honor.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A madrinha ajudou a noiva a se preparar antes da cerimônia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The maid of honor helped the bride get ready before the ceremony.

definitions.native: dawn, early hours of the morning
definitions.note: Refers to the period after midnight and before daybreak; often used for “late at night/very early in the morning.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Acordei na madrugada para pegar o voo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I woke up in the early hours of the morning to catch the flight.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form of "maduro".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A banana já está madura.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The banana is already ripe.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form of the adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: As bananas estão maduras.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bananas are ripe.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O abacate está maduro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The avocado is ripe.

definitions.note: Used for a person’s age, attitude, or behavior (not just for fruit).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele é muito maduro para a idade dele.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is very mature for his age.

definitions.note: Used mainly for the conductor/music director, especially in classical music.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O maestro começou o concerto com um gesto silencioso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The conductor started the concert with a silent gesture.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Aquele truque parece magia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That trick seems like magic.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form (used with feminine nouns).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A vista daqui é magnífica.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The view from here is magnificent.

definitions.note: feminine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: As vistas do topo da montanha são magníficas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The views from the top of the mountain are magnificent.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O palácio é magnífico.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The palace is magnificent.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O mago fez um truque de magia para as crianças.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The magician did a magic trick for the children.

definitions.note: Verb form of magoar. Not to be confused with the noun “mágoa” (with an accent), meaning “hurt/resentment.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Isso me magoa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That hurts me.

definitions.note: Often used for hurting someone’s feelings (emotional hurt), but it can also refer to physical hurt depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Não quero te magoar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t want to hurt you.

definitions.note: Often used for hurting someone’s feelings (emotionally), but can also mean hurting physically depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele me magoou com aquelas palavras.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He hurt me with those words.

definitions.note: Plural of "mago".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os magos fizeram um show incrível na praça.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The magicians put on an incredible show in the square.

definitions.note: Form of the verb "magoar" used before an object pronoun (dropping the final -r and adding an accent), e.g. "magoá-lo" = "to hurt him".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu não queria magoá-lo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I didn’t want to hurt him.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form of “magro”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela é magra, mas muito forte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is thin, but very strong.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele é muito magro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is very thin.

definitions.note: A tile-based game, usually written with a capital M in English (Mahjong).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles jogaram mahjong depois do jantar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They played mahjong after dinner.

definitions.note: Commonly used in Brazilian Portuguese, often as a loanword referring specifically to email.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vou te mandar um mail mais tarde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'll send you an email later.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Recebi muitos mails hoje.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I received a lot of emails today.

definitions.note: Informal, affectionate term for "mãe" (used especially in parts of Brazil).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vou ligar para a mainha mais tarde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to call mom later.

definitions.note: The month of the year.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Meu aniversário é em maio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My birthday is in May.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu quero um sanduíche com maionese.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want a sandwich with mayonnaise.

definitions.note: Comparative form of "grande"; often used for age as well as size.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Meu irmão é maior do que eu.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My brother is older than me.

definitions.note: Comparative form of "grande"; agrees with a plural noun.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os apartamentos maiores são mais caros.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bigger apartments are more expensive.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A maioria dos alunos chegou cedo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The majority of the students arrived early.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela quer estudar mais.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She wants to study more.

definitions.note: Used for comparisons, quantities, or to intensify something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hoje está mais frio do que ontem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today it is colder than yesterday.

definitions.note: Used in addition and arithmetic.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dois mais dois são quatro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Two plus two are four.

definitions.note: Used to request an additional unit of something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quero mais um café, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want another coffee, please.

definitions.note: Common in questions like “O que mais…?” meaning “What else…?”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O que mais você quer dizer?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What else do you want to say?

definitions.note: In the pattern “não … mais” to indicate something has stopped.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu não quero mais discutir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't want to argue anymore.

definitions.note: In the structure “não só … mas/como também …”, Portuguese often includes “mas também” or “mas sim”; “mais” can appear as “mas mais” in some contexts, though it is less common.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele não só pediu desculpa, mas mais tarde também ajudou a consertar o erro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He not only apologized, but later he also helped fix the mistake.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quero mais água.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want more water.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quero mais água, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want more water, please.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Preciso de mais um dia para terminar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need one more day to finish.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Comprei um maiô novo para a praia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought a new one-piece swimsuit for the beach.

definitions.note: Plural feminine form; often used to refer to capital letters in general.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Por favor, escreva o seu nome em letras maiúsculas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please write your name in capital letters.

definitions.note: Used especially as a form of address for a king or queen (like “Your Majesty”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vossa Majestade, o jantar está pronto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Your Majesty, dinner is ready.

definitions.note: Often spelled in English as “mahjong”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nós jogamos majong depois do jantar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We played mahjong after dinner.

definitions.note: Usually refers to the military rank (especially in Brazilian Portuguese).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele é major do Exército.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is a major in the Army.

definitions.note: As an adverb, mal contrasts with the adjective mau ("bad").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela canta mal.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She sings badly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu mal consegui dormir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I could barely sleep.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O mal pode causar muito sofrimento.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Evil can cause a lot of suffering.

definitions.note: Used before masculine singular nouns (e.g., "mal dia"); otherwise the form is usually "mau".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele teve um mal dia no trabalho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He had a bad day at work.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vou levar uma mala pequena na viagem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to take a small suitcase on the trip.

definitions.note: Used to describe a woman or girl (feminine form of “mau”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela não é mala; só está cansada hoje.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She isn’t bad; she’s just tired today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele fez malabarismo com três bolas no semáforo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He juggled three balls at the traffic light.

definitions.note: Often used figuratively to mean “having to juggle” tasks, time, or problems.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O artista fez malabarismos com três bolas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The performer juggled three balls.

definitions.note: Often describes someone sly or street-smart; depending on context it can be playful or insulting.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele é um malandro e sempre tenta levar vantagem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He’s a trickster and always tries to take advantage.

definitions.note: Plural of “mala”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: As malas estão no porta-malas do carro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The suitcases are in the trunk of the car.

definitions.note: plural of "mala" (a suitcase or travel bag)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: As malas já estão no carro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The suitcases are already in the car.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Não entendo tanta maldade nas redes sociais.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t understand so much meanness on social media.

definitions.note: Often used as a strong insult or expletive; can also literally mean “cursed.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tire a maldita mão daí!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Get your damn hand out of there!

definitions.note: Feminine plural form. Often used as a strong negative expression (similar to “damn”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Essas malditas regras mudam toda semana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Those damned rules change every week.

definitions.note: Often used as a strong insult or expression of annoyance; can also be used more literally as “cursed.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Esse maldito barulho não me deixa dormir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That damned noise won’t let me sleep.

definitions.note: Offensive insult; used to refer to someone you’re angry at.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Aquele maldito me enganou de novo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That bastard tricked me again.

definitions.note: Often used as an insult or to express anger/frustration; can be offensive depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Esses mosquitos malditos não me deixam dormir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Those damned mosquitoes won’t let me sleep.

definitions.note: Often used as an insult or strong expression of anger; can sound harsh.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os malditos destruíram tudo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The damned ones destroyed everything.

definitions.note: An exclamation used to show anger, frustration, or disappointment.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Maldição! Esqueci as chaves em casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Damn! I forgot the keys at home.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Isso parece uma maldição.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That looks like a curse.

definitions.note: Plural of "mal".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele falou dos males da guerra.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He talked about the evils of war.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vou levar uma maleta pequena para a viagem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to take a small suitcase for the trip.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form. Often informal; depending on context it can be playful or insulting.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela é maluca, mas é muito divertida.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She’s crazy, but she’s really fun.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: As ideias delas são malucas, mas funcionam.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Their ideas are crazy, but they work.

definitions.note: Often informal; can be joking/affectionate depending on context, but it can also sound insulting.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Esse filme é maluco!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That movie is crazy!

definitions.note: Common in Brazilian Portuguese; can be insulting or used informally to mean “guy/dude,” depending on tone and context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Aquele maluco gritou comigo na rua.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That crazy guy yelled at me in the street.

definitions.note: Informal; can be playful or insulting depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles são malucos por esportes radicais.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They’re crazy about extreme sports.

definitions.note: Informal; often used for something silly or absurd (not necessarily a medical condition).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Que maluquice foi essa?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What kind of craziness was that?

definitions.note: Feminine singular adjective; can also be used as a noun meaning “evil/wicked woman.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela é malvada com os colegas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is mean to her classmates.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele é um homem malvado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is an evil man.

definitions.note: Often used when talking about breastfeeding or about an animal’s teat; it does not mean “mom” in standard Portuguese.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O bebê pegou na mama e começou a mamar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The baby latched onto the breast and started nursing.

definitions.note: Common, affectionate way to say “mother” (often used by children or within the family).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mamãe, você pode me ajudar com a lição de casa?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Mom, can you help me with my homework?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O golfinho é um mamífero.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dolphin is a mammal.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os mamíferos alimentam os seus filhotes com leite.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Mammals feed their young with milk.

definitions.note: Usually refers to a group of animals.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A manada atravessou a estrada devagar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The herd crossed the road slowly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Essa camisa tem uma mancha de café.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That shirt has a coffee stain.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A minha camisa ficou manchada de café.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My shirt got stained with coffee.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O sofá está manchado de vinho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The sofa is stained with wine.

definitions.note: Plural of "mancha".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Essas manchas na camisa não saem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These stains on the shirt won’t come out.

definitions.note: Most common in journalism (newspapers, websites, TV news).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A manchete do jornal fala sobre a eleição.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The newspaper headline is about the election.

definitions.note: Often refers to someone who has difficulty walking because of an injured leg or foot.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Depois da queda, ele ficou manco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the fall, he was left limping.

definitions.native: send, order, tell (someone to do something)
definitions.note: Present tense form of "mandar" (often used with "você/ele/ela"). Also used as an informal imperative meaning “send!” or “go ahead!”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele manda uma mensagem depois do trabalho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He sends a message after work.

definitions.note: Often used in legal contexts (e.g., arrest warrant: “mandado de prisão”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A polícia tinha um mandado de prisão.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police had an arrest warrant.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O mandado do diretor deve ser cumprido.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The director’s order must be obeyed.

definitions.note: Past participle of "mandar" (often used with auxiliaries like "ter/haver" or "ser").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele já tinha mandado o e-mail.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He had already sent the email.

definitions.note: Present tense form meaning “they/you all (formal) send/order.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles mandam uma mensagem todos os dias.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They send a message every day.

definitions.note: This form can mean either present tense (“we send / we order”) or simple past (“we sent / we ordered”), depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nós mandamos o e-mail hoje de manhã.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We sent the email this morning.

definitions.note: Present participle/gerund of "mandar"; often used to mean “sending” (e.g., messages, emails) or “ordering/commanding” someone to do something, depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estou mandando um e-mail para a professora agora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m sending an email to the teacher now.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vou mandar uma mensagem para a Ana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to send Ana a message.

definitions.native: to order, to tell (someone) to do something
definitions.note: Often used for giving commands or instructions.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O chefe vai mandar-nos terminar o relatório hoje.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The boss is going to tell us to finish the report today.

definitions.note: Third-person plural (they) simple past (pretérito perfeito) of "mandar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles mandaram uma mensagem ontem à noite.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They sent a message last night.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mandarei o e-mail amanhã de manhã.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will send the email tomorrow morning.

definitions.native: will order, will tell (someone to do something)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mandarei o técnico vir hoje.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will have the technician come today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela fala mandarim em casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She speaks Mandarin at home.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Comprei mandarim no mercado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought tangerines at the market.

definitions.native: was sending, was ordering, used to send, used to order
definitions.note: Imperfect past tense of "mandar" (ongoing or habitual past action).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu mandava mensagens todos os dias.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I used to send messages every day.

definitions.note: Used with você/ele/ela as a command (imperative) or in the present subjunctive.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Por favor, mande a mensagem agora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please send the message now.

definitions.note: Used with você/ele/ela as a command (imperative) or in the present subjunctive.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mande o relatório ainda hoje.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Order the report to be done today / Have the report sent in today.

definitions.native: I sent, I told, I ordered
definitions.note: Past (pretérito perfeito) form of "mandar" for "I".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mandei uma mensagem para a minha mãe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I sent a message to my mom.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (vocês/eles/elas) or imperative for vocês of "mandar"; often used for requests ("please send").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mandem os documentos por e-mail, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please send the documents by email.

definitions.note: Often used to mean telling someone to do something (to give an order/command).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mando um e-mail para você hoje.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I send you an email today.

definitions.note: Past tense (ele/ela/você form) of "mandar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele mandou uma mensagem para a mãe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He sent a message to his mother.

definitions.note: Common informal spelling/pronunciation of “mandar” (often representing dropped final -r in speech).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vou mandá uma mensagem pra você mais tarde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to send you a message later.

definitions.note: Describes someone (usually a person) who likes to give orders and control others.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele é muito mandão e quer mandar em todo mundo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is very bossy and wants to boss everyone around.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele fraturou a mandíbula no acidente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He fractured his jaw in the accident.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Não gosto da maneira como ele falou comigo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't like the way he spoke to me.

definitions.note: Often used in the expression “de maneira que…” meaning “so that / in such a way that…”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele explicou de uma maneira simples.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He explained it in a simple way.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Existem várias maneiras de fazer isso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are several ways to do that.

definitions.note: Informal; very common in Brazilian Portuguese.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O seu carro é muito maneiro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Your car is really cool.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A manga da minha camisa rasgou.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The sleeve of my shirt tore.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu comprei uma manga no mercado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought a mango at the market.

definitions.note: Often used for Japanese-style comics; plural is usually “mangás”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela gosta de ler manga.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She likes reading manga.

definitions.note: Not to be confused with English “manga” (Japanese comics). In Portuguese, “mangá” (with an accent) is the comics meaning.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: As mangas da minha camisa estão molhadas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The sleeves of my shirt are wet.

definitions.note: Not to be confused with English “manga” (Japanese comics). In Portuguese, “mangá” (with an accent) is the comics meaning.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Comprei duas mangas no mercado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought two mangoes at the market.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I thought about her all day.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I thought about them all afternoon.

definitions.note: Contraction of “em” + “ele”; also used for masculine “it” (referring to a masculine noun).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I thought about him all day.

definitions.note: Contraction of "em" + "eles".

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I thought about them all day.

definitions.note: Often used for emphasis before a verb; in English it is frequently translated as “didn't even” or similar.

definitions.note: Used to negate the existence/quantity of something; often appears with “não” (e.g., “não tenho nenhum…”).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't have any money with me.

definitions.note: Used to negate the existence/quantity of something (often before a noun).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Não tenho nenhum dinheiro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't have any money.

definitions.note: Feminine form of "nenhum"; used before a feminine noun.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t have any doubt.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form of “nenhum/nenhuma” (used with feminine singular nouns).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Não tenho nenhuma dúvida.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t have any doubts.

definitions.note: Common in Brazilian Portuguese as a cute/affectionate way to refer to a baby (and sometimes to a young child).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The baby is sleeping in the crib.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My nerves are on edge before the interview.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form (used with a feminine noun or a woman/girl).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is nervous before the test.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: As alunas ficaram nervosas antes da prova.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The students got nervous before the test.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Antes da apresentação, senti muito nervosismo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Before the presentation, I felt very nervous.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estou nervoso antes da entrevista.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m nervous before the interview.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He got angry about the delay.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles estão nervosos antes da prova.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are nervous before the test.

definitions.note: Contraction of "em" + "essa"; used with feminine singular nouns.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nessa sala, faz muito frio no inverno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In that room, it’s very cold in the winter.

definitions.note: Contraction of "em" + "essa" (feminine).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nessa cidade, o transporte público é bom.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In that city, public transportation is good.

definitions.note: Contraction of "em" + "essa"; feminine singular.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu moro nessa rua há dois anos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ve lived on this/that street for two years.

definitions.native: in this, on this, at this
definitions.note: Contraction of "em" + "essa"; feminine singular. Refers to something near the listener or already mentioned.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: On this street there’s a very good café.

definitions.note: Contraction of "em" + "essas" (feminine plural).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pensei nessas duas opções antes de decidir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I thought about those two options before deciding.

definitions.note: Contraction of "em" + "essas" (in those) or "em" + "essas" used with "essa/essas" (those/these, feminine plural). Which meaning applies depends on context.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In those/these stores, the prices are lower.

definitions.note: Contraction of “em” + “esse” (masculine singular).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In this restaurant, the food is very good.

definitions.note: Contraction of “em” + “esse” (masculine singular); used before a masculine singular noun.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In that book, there are many photos.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I thought about it at that moment.

definitions.note: Contraction of “em” + “esses”; informal/colloquial.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We talk about it and, in these moments, everything seems easier.

definitions.note: Contraction of “em” + “esta” (feminine singular).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nesta rua há muito trânsito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is a lot of traffic on this street.

definitions.note: Contraction of "em" + "estas".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nestas fotos, você parece feliz.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In these photos, you look happy.

definitions.note: Contraction of "em" + "este"; used with masculine singular nouns.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Neste momento, não posso falar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At this moment, I can't talk.

definitions.note: Contraction of “em + estes” (masculine plural).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nestes dias, estou muito ocupado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These days, I’m very busy.

definitions.note: Contraction of "em" + "estes"; used with masculine plural nouns.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nestes dias, vou estudar mais.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In these days, I'm going to study more.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A neta dela tem cinco anos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Her granddaughter is five years old.

definitions.note: Plural of "neta" (female grandchild).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: As minhas netas gostam de ouvir histórias antes de dormir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My granddaughters like to listen to stories before going to sleep.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O neto visita os avós todos os domingos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The grandson visits his grandparents every Sunday.

definitions.note: Plural of “neto”. Can refer to grandsons specifically, or to grandchildren in general when the group includes at least one male.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tenho dois netos e uma neta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have two grandsons and a granddaughter.

definitions.note: Female form; refers to a woman neurosurgeon.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A neurocirurgiã explicou os riscos da operação.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The neurosurgeon explained the risks of the operation.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O país manteve-se neutro durante o conflito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The country remained neutral during the conflict.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No inverno, neva muito nesta cidade.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In winter, it snows a lot in this city.

definitions.note: Present participle (gerund) of “nevar”; often used with “estar” (e.g., “está nevando”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Está nevando lá fora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s snowing outside.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vai nevar amanhã.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s going to snow tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A nevasca fechou várias estradas na serra.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The snowstorm closed several roads in the mountains.

definitions.note: Used mainly in the present subjunctive after expressions like "espero que" ("I hope that").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que neve amanhã.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope it snows tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A neve cobriu a rua durante a noite.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The snow covered the street overnight.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: De manhã, havia muito nevoeiro na estrada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the morning, there was a lot of fog on the road.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ontem nevou na serra.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday it snowed in the mountains.

definitions.note: Often used about gently rocking a baby or child to help them fall asleep.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela costuma ninar o bebê antes de dormir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She usually lulls the baby to sleep before bedtime.

definitions.note: Used for people (not things). Often appears with a double negative in Portuguese (e.g., "Não vi ninguém" = "I didn’t see anyone").

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t know anyone here.

definitions.note: Used to refer to people, not things.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ninguém sabe a resposta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: No one knows the answer.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O pássaro construiu um ninho na árvore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bird built a nest in the tree.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Na primavera, vemos ninhos nas árvores do parque.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In spring, we see nests in the trees in the park.

definitions.note: Used for a (typically Japanese) ninja; also used informally for someone very skilled at something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele se vestiu de ninja no carnaval.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He dressed up as a ninja for Carnival.

definitions.note: Contraction of “em” + “isso”; used to refer back to something previously mentioned.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Não acredito nisso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't believe in that.

definitions.note: Contraction of “em” + “isto”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pensei nisto a manhã toda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I thought about this all morning.

definitions.native: in the, on the, at the

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The book is in the car.

definitions.note: In standard Portuguese, this is usually spelled “não”.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: — Are you coming tomorrow? — No.

definitions.note: Clitic direct object pronoun form of “o”, used after verbs ending in -m, -ão, or -õe, usually written with a hyphen (e.g., viram-no).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They saw him yesterday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A noite está silenciosa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The night is quiet.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The nights here are very quiet.

definitions.note: feminine form; often also used as a noun meaning “bride.”

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O noivado deles durou um ano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Their engagement lasted a year.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The groom is very happy.

definitions.note: Used for a man who is engaged to be married.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O noivo chegou cedo para a cerimônia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The groom arrived early for the ceremony.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela está sendo nojenta comigo hoje.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That bathroom is disgusting.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A minha nora é muito simpática.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The north of Portugal is very green.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He speaks Norwegian.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The Norwegian man lives in Oslo.

definitions.native: in the, on the, at the

definitions.note: unstressed object or reflexive pronoun
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela nos viu ontem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She saw us yesterday.

definitions.note: Common Brazilian Portuguese interjection expressing surprise, admiration, or shock.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Wow, what a scare!

definitions.note: used before a feminine singular noun

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Our house is small.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form (used with feminine singular nouns).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Our house is small.

definitions.note: used with a masculine singular noun

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estou me sentindo nostálgico hoje.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m feeling nostalgic today.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I wrote a note to my teacher.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He notices the mistake quickly.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I watch the news every night.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He made a perfect pass to the striker.

definitions.note: Often used for public transportation tickets (e.g., a monthly pass).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Preciso comprar um passe mensal de metrô.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to buy a monthly subway pass.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estou passeando no parque com meu cachorro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m strolling in the park with my dog.

definitions.native: to take a walk, to go for a stroll

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vamos dar um passeio no parque depois do jantar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let’s go for a walk in the park after dinner.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The newspaper talked about a crime of passion.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele ficou passivo durante a discussão.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He stayed passive during the discussion.

definitions.note: Plural of "passo".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dei alguns passos para trás.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I took a few steps back.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito perfeito) of "passar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O ônibus passou às oito horas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bus passed by at eight o'clock.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vou fazer pasta para o jantar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to make pasta for dinner.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: As vacas estão no pasto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cows are in the pasture.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The pastor spoke with the family after the service.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O pastor levou as ovelhas para o campo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The shepherd took the sheep to the field.

definitions.note: Usually refers to an animal’s paw/leg (especially a four-legged animal).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog hurt its paw.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O cachorro sujou as patas na lama.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog got its paws dirty in the mud.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A empresa registrou uma patente para a nova tecnologia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The company registered a patent for the new technology.

definitions.note: Present participle/gerund of "patinar"; used to talk about an action in progress.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela está patinando no gelo agora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is skating on the ice now.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu gosto de patinar no parque aos domingos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like to skate in the park on Sundays.

definitions.note: Often used for vehicles (e.g., tires) losing traction.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O carro começou a patinar na estrada molhada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The car started to skid on the wet road.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O pato está nadando no lago.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The duck is swimming in the lake.

definitions.note: Plural of "pato".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Há patos no lago.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are ducks in the lake.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele fez um discurso patriótico no feriado nacional.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He gave a patriotic speech on the national holiday.

definitions.note: Informal; can refer to a woman who is the boss or the female owner/manager of a business.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A patroa pediu para eu chegar mais cedo amanhã.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The (female) boss asked me to arrive earlier tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A patrulha passou pela rua duas vezes hoje.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The patrol went down the street twice today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O patrão está no escritório agora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The boss is in the office now.

definitions.note: Diminutive of “patrão”; can sound affectionate, ironic, or slightly mocking depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O patrãozinho chegou e começou a dar ordens.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The little boss arrived and started giving orders.

definitions.note: Plural of “patrão”. Often refers to one’s employer(s) or the people in charge.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os patrões disseram que teremos uma reunião amanhã.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bosses said we’ll have a meeting tomorrow.

definitions.note: Can mean “pitiful” or “ridiculous,” depending on context; “pathetic” in Portuguese often has a stronger negative tone than English.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Achei patética a desculpa dele.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I thought his excuse was pathetic.

definitions.note: Often used to mean “pitiful” or “lame” (a negative judgment), not “emotionally moving.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Achei patético ele mentir por causa de uma coisa tão pequena.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I thought it was pathetic that he lied over something so small.

definitions.note: Often used for a stick/club or a piece of wood; in some contexts it can also be a vulgar slang term for the male genitalia.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele pegou um pau do chão para se apoiar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He picked up a stick from the ground to lean on.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os paus estavam no chão depois da tempestade.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The sticks were on the ground after the storm.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vamos fazer uma pausa de cinco minutos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let’s take a five-minute break.

definitions.note: Plural of "pauzinho"; can refer to small sticks like toothpicks or chopsticks depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pegue dois pauzinhos para prender o papel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Take two little sticks to hold the paper in place.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela sentiu pavor quando ouviu o barulho no escuro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She felt terror when she heard the noise in the dark.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Queremos viver em paz.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We want to live in peace.

definitions.note: Plural of "paz"; often used in fixed expressions like "em paz" (at peace) or "fazer as pazes" (make up).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Depois de tanta discussão, eles finalmente fizeram as pazes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After so much arguing, they finally made up.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O Brasil é um país grande.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Brazil is a large country.

definitions.note: Plural of "país".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela já visitou muitos países.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has already visited many countries.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mentir é um pecado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Lying is a sin.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He repented because he felt like a sinner.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela se descreveu como uma pecadora que quer mudar de vida.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She described herself as a sinner who wants to change her life.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele confessou os pecados ao padre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He confessed his sins to the priest.

definitions.note: Often used when negotiating a lower price, especially in markets or informal shopping situations.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele sempre tenta pechinchar o preço no mercado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He always tries to bargain for the price at the market.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela tem um jeito peculiar de contar histórias.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has a peculiar way of telling stories.

definitions.note: Diminutive of "pedaço"; often used to sound affectionate or to emphasize smallness.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Você quer um pedacinho de bolo?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you want a small piece of cake?

definitions.note: Plural form of "pedacinho"; often used as an affectionate way to say “little pieces/bits.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cortei o pão em pedacinhos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I cut the bread into little pieces.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quero um pedaço de bolo, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d like a piece of cake, please.

definitions.note: Plural of "pedaço".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cortei o bolo em pedaços.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I cut the cake into pieces.

definitions.note: Present tense (ele/ela/você) of "pedir".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela pede ajuda ao professor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She asks the teacher for help.

definitions.note: Present tense (they/you all) form of "pedir".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles pedem ajuda ao professor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They ask the teacher for help.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A estátua está em cima de um pedestal.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The statue is on top of a pedestal.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os pedestres devem atravessar na faixa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Pedestrians should cross at the crosswalk.

definitions.note: Past tense (pretérito perfeito) of “pedir” for “eu”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pedi um café, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I asked for a coffee, please.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu pedia ajuda quando precisava.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I asked for help when I needed it.

definitions.note: Commonly used for ordering food or making a formal request.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Fiz um pedido no restaurante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I placed an order at the restaurant.

definitions.note: Past participle of "pedir".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O relatório foi pedido ontem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The report was requested yesterday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os pedidos chegaram hoje de manhã.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The orders arrived this morning.

definitions.note: Present tense (nós) of "pedir".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nós pedimos ajuda ao professor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We ask the teacher for help.

definitions.note: Present participle/gerund form of "pedir" (used like “asking/requesting”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estou pedindo ajuda ao professor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am asking the teacher for help.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vou pedir um café, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to ask for a coffee, please.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Depois do jantar, ela vai pedir a sobremesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After dinner, she is going to order dessert.

definitions.note: Past tense (simple past) form meaning “they asked for / they requested.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles pediram ajuda depois do acidente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They asked for help after the accident.

definitions.native: I will ask (for), I will request
definitions.note: 1st-person singular future tense of "pedir".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pedirei ajuda se eu precisar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will ask for help if I need it.

definitions.note: 3rd person plural, future subjunctive of "pedir"; often used after "quando", "se", or "caso".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se pedirem ajuda, eu explico tudo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If they ask for help, I’ll explain everything.

definitions.note: Conditional form of "pedir" (used for polite requests or hypothetical situations).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu pediria uma pizza, mas não estou com fome.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would ask for a pizza, but I'm not hungry.

definitions.note: Form used as (1) future subjunctive (often after “quando”, “se”) or (2) personal infinitive (often after a preposition like “antes de”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se pedirmos ajuda, eles vão nos ouvir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If we ask for help, they will listen to us.

definitions.note: Past subjunctive form, used in hypothetical or dependent clauses (often with “se”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se eu pedisse ajuda, você viria?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela pediu ajuda ontem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She asked for help yesterday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No restaurante, ele pediu peixe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At the restaurant, he ordered fish.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He picked up a stone from the ground.

definitions.note: Plural of "pedra".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Há muitas pedras no caminho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are many stones on the path.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O caminho estava coberto de pedregulho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The path was covered with gravel.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O pedreiro está construindo um muro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bricklayer is building a wall.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A pega construiu o ninho naquela árvore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The magpie built the nest in that tree.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele pega o ônibus às oito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He takes the bus at eight.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vi uma pegada de cachorro na lama.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I saw a dog's footprint in the mud.

definitions.note: Often used when talking about tires, shoes, or how well something holds onto a surface.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este pneu tem boa pegada na estrada molhada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This tire has good grip on the wet road.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: As pegadas na areia mostram que alguém passou por aqui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The footprints in the sand show that someone passed by here.

definitions.note: Often used for lighthearted jokes or tricks; can also refer to a “gotcha”/trap question in a quiz.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles fizeram uma pegadinha comigo no trabalho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They played a prank on me at work.

definitions.note: Often used to mean something is stuck/glued to something else.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The sticker got stuck on the glass.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He’s down with a bad flu.

definitions.note: Third-person plural (they/you all) present tense of “pegar”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles pegam o ônibus às sete.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They take the bus at seven.

definitions.native: we got, we caught, we took
definitions.note: Often used meaning “we got/caught” (e.g., a bus, a cold) or “we took/grabbed.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pegamos o ônibus às sete.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We caught the bus at seven.

definitions.note: Often used with "estar" to form the ongoing action (progressive), like "estou pegando" = "I am getting/taking".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estou pegando o ônibus agora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m catching the bus now.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vou pegar o copo que está na mesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to pick up the glass that's on the table.

definitions.note: Often used for transportation or illnesses.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Preciso pegar o ônibus às sete.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to catch the bus at seven.

definitions.native: they took, they grabbed, they picked up
definitions.note: Past (completed action): third-person plural of "pegar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles pegaram o ônibus cedo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They took the bus early.

definitions.note: Often used for catching something (like a ball) or catching an illness.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles pegaram a bola no ar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They caught the ball in the air.

definitions.native: will take, will get, will catch
definitions.note: Future tense of "pegar"; often used for taking/getting something or catching transportation (e.g., a bus).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Amanhã pegarei o ônibus cedo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow I will catch the bus early.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s better for them to take a taxi.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Amanhã pegaremos o ônibus cedo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow we’ll catch the bus early.

definitions.note: Conditional form of "pegar" (used for hypotheticals, often translated as "would").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu pegaria o ônibus mais cedo se pudesse.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would take the bus earlier if I could.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele pegará o ônibus às oito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He will take the bus at eight.

definitions.note: Usually used with "tu" (informal singular), common in Portugal and in some regions of Brazil.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu pegas no meu casaco, por favor?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you grab my coat, please?

definitions.note: Imperfect past: often means “used to …” (habit) or “was …-ing” (ongoing action), depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu pegava o ônibus às oito todos os dias.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I used to take the bus at eight every day.

definitions.note: Past participle of "pegar" used as an adjective (often in passive constructions like "foi pego").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O ladrão foi pego pela polícia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The thief was caught by the police.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu pego o ônibus às oito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I take the bus at eight.

definitions.note: Often used with estar/ficar (e.g., estar pego no trânsito = to be stuck in traffic).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We got stuck in traffic for two hours.

definitions.note: Past participle (plural). Often used with "ser" to mean "to be caught".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles foram pegos pela polícia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They were caught by the police.

definitions.note: Simple past (ele/ela/você form) of "pegar".

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He picked up the book from the table.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Take the book, please.

definitions.native: I got, I took, I caught
definitions.note: Past tense (eu) of "pegar"; often used for getting/taking something, or catching something (like a bus or a cold).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Peguei o ônibus às oito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I caught the bus at eight.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (or affirmative command) form of "pegar" for "vocês".

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Take the books and come with me.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to grab the coat because it’s cold.

definitions.note: Informal/vulgar.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He farted and ran off.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele sentiu uma dor no peito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He felt a pain in his chest.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Deixei as chaves no peitoril da janela.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I left the keys on the windowsill.

definitions.note: Plural of "peito". In everyday speech it can mean either the chest (body part) or breasts, depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele sentiu uma dor nos peitos ao respirar fundo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He felt a pain in his chest when taking a deep breath.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu gosto de comer peixe no jantar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like to eat fish for dinner.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Look at the little fish in the aquarium!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: As crianças ficaram pelados na praia.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The two men are bald.

definitions.native: by the, through the, for the

definitions.note: Often used in conversation to introduce an explanation or conclusion (like “so…”).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Well, I don't know what to say.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm not going out because I'm tired.

definitions.note: Usually used with the article: a policia (“the police”).

definitions.note: Plural form of the adjective.

definitions.note: Plural form.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Na turma, há três poliglotas.

definitions.note: Feminine form of the adjective.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My teacher is Polish.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form of the adjective.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The Polish tourists arrived yesterday.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He speaks Polish at home.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu falo um pouco de polonês.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I speak a little Polish.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele sentou-se na poltrona para ler.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A poluição do ar está piorando na cidade.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O rio está poluído.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The river is polluted.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No aquário, vimos um polvo enorme.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No aquário, vimos vários polvos.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Esse assunto é muito polêmico.

definitions.note: Usually refers to the police force; for an individual officer, Portuguese more often uses policial.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police arrived quickly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela estuda política na universidade.

definitions.note: Often used for an organization’s or government’s set of rules or plans (e.g., company policy, public policy).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The company changed its vacation policy.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form of the adjective.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os políticos discutiram novas leis no parlamento.

definitions.note: Often used for medicinal creams, especially thicker ones.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O pomar fica atrás da casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The orchard is behind the house.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Uma pomba branca pousou na janela.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Há muitos pombos na praça.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are many pigeons in the square.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estou pondo a mesa para o jantar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m setting the table for dinner.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: É melhor que vocês ponham o celular no silencioso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s better that you put your phone on silent.

definitions.note: First-person singular present indicative of “pôr” (I put).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu ponho o livro na mesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I put the book on the table.

definitions.note: Often refers to the pointed/outermost part of something (like a pencil, knife, or shoe).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The tip of the pencil broke.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele tem boa pontaria.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He has good aim.

definitions.note: Plural of "ponta".

definitions.note: Plural of "ponte".

definitions.note: Plural of “ponto”.

definitions.note: Plural form (masculine or feminine).

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A pontualidade é importante no trabalho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Punctuality is important at work.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O trem chegou pontualmente às 8h.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A pontuação deste texto está correta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The punctuation in this text is correct.

definitions.note: Often used for points in a game, test, or competition.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Our score in the game was very high.

definitions.note: Often used to describe music, culture, or style associated with pop culture or pop music.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She likes pop music.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A popa do navio ficou danificada na tempestade.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The ship’s stern was damaged in the storm.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela é muito popular na escola.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is very popular at school.

definitions.note: Often used in contexts like "música popular" (folk/popular music) or "cultura popular" (popular/folk culture).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They study Brazil's popular (folk) culture.

definitions.note: Plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Esses livros são muito populares entre os adolescentes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Those books are very popular among teenagers.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A popularidade do cantor aumentou muito depois do novo álbum.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The singer's popularity increased a lot after the new album.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A população da cidade cresceu muito nos últimos anos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The city's population has grown a lot in recent years.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lisboa é uma cidade populosa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Lisbon is a populous city.

definitions.note: Often contrasts with para; por commonly expresses cause, exchange, duration, or means.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Obrigado por tudo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Thank you for everything.

definitions.note: Commonly used to indicate the agent in passive sentences.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O livro foi escrito por ela.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The book was written by her.

definitions.note: Used for movement through a place or point.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We went through a tunnel.

definitions.note: Often followed by a verb in the infinitive (por + infinitive).

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A porca e os leitões estão no celeiro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The sow and the piglets are in the barn.

definitions.note: In Portuguese, this is the metal piece that a bolt screws into.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A porca do parafuso está frouxa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The nut on the bolt is loose.

definitions.note: Feminine form of the adjective (used with feminine nouns).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The kitchen is filthy today.

definitions.note: Often used informally to complain about something dirty or in bad condition.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Que porcaria de quarto!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What a mess of a room!

definitions.note: Informal; used for something of poor quality or to show annoyance.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Esse celular é uma porcaria.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That cell phone is junk.

definitions.note: Describes something physically dirty or, informally, someone’s gross/unclean behavior. (Masc. singular form: porco; fem.: porca; plural: porcos/porcas.)

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After messing with the soil, his hand got all dirty.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Gross! I’m not going to eat that.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O porco está no curral.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The pig is in the pen.

definitions.note: Often used as an insult to describe someone as dirty or gross.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele é um porco; nunca limpa a cozinha.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He’s a filthy person; he never cleans the kitchen.

definitions.note: Plural of "porco".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os porcos estão no campo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The pigs are in the field.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t want to see porn on my phone.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Fiquei em casa porque estava cansado.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ninguém sabe o porquê da decisão.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Nobody knows the reason for the decision.

definitions.note: Usually used as a noun (often with an article): "o porquê" = "the reason". ("porque" without an accent is used for "because".)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ninguém explicou o porquê da mudança.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Nobody explained the reason for the change.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The school has a big portal at the entrance.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu falo português em casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I speak Portuguese at home.
