definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estou com pressa e preciso sair agora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm in a hurry and I need to leave now.

definitions.note: Usually used in the expression “com pressas” (“in a hurry”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Saí de casa com pressas e esqueci a carteira.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I left home in a hurry and forgot my wallet.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tive um pressentimento de que algo ia dar errado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I had a premonition that something was going to go wrong.

definitions.note: present participle/gerund of "pressionar"; often used with "estar" to mean "is/are pressing" or to describe doing something while something else happens.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estou pressionando o botão vermelho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am pressing the red button.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Você precisa pressionar este botão para ligar o aparelho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You need to press this button to turn on the device.

definitions.native: to pressure, to put pressure on
definitions.note: Often used in the sense of pressuring someone to do something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles tentaram pressionar o gerente a baixar os preços.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They tried to pressure the manager to lower the prices.

definitions.note: Often used as a formal command (to você), like on signs or instructions.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pressione o botão para abrir a porta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Press the button to open the door.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele pressionou o botão e a porta abriu.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He pressed the button and the door opened.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sinto muita pressão no trabalho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I feel a lot of pressure at work.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela presta um ótimo serviço aos clientes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She provides excellent service to the customers.

definitions.note: Commonly used with “atenção”: “prestar atenção” = “to pay attention”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele presta atenção na aula.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He pays attention in class.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele me devolveu o dinheiro que eu tinha prestado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He gave me back the money that I had lent.

definitions.note: Common in set phrases like "serviço prestado" (service provided).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Agradecemos o serviço prestado pela equipe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We appreciate the service provided by the team.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela está prestando ajuda aos vizinhos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is providing help to the neighbors.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estou prestando meu carro ao meu irmão por uma semana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m lending my car to my brother for a week.

definitions.note: Often used with services, help, or attention (e.g., prestar um serviço, prestar ajuda, prestar atenção).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele vai prestar ajuda aos vizinhos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is going to provide help to the neighbors.

definitions.note: Used especially in Brazil in expressions like prestar dinheiro (to lend money).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Você pode me prestar cinquenta reais?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you lend me fifty reais?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles prestaram ajuda depois do acidente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They provided help after the accident.

definitions.note: Common in Brazil: “prestar” + “prova/vestibular/concurso” = to take/sit an exam.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles prestaram o concurso no domingo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They took the exam on Sunday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele é muito prestativo com os colegas de trabalho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is very helpful with his coworkers.

definitions.note: Very commonly used in the phrase “prestar atenção” = “pay attention.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que você preste atenção na explicação.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you pay attention to the explanation.

definitions.note: Often used in the phrase “prestar atenção” = “pay attention.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Prestem atenção, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please pay attention.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela prestou ajuda quando eu mais precisava.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She provided help when I needed it most.

definitions.note: Commonly used with exams, e.g. “prestar vestibular / ENEM / concurso”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele prestou o concurso no ano passado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He took the civil service exam last year.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Presumi que você já tinha chegado em casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I assumed you had already gotten home.

definitions.note: Often used to express a reasonable guess (like “I suppose”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Presumo que ele chegue mais tarde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I assume he’ll arrive later.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu comprei presunto para fazer um sanduíche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought ham to make a sandwich.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele é muito presunçoso e fala como se soubesse tudo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is very conceited and talks as if he knew everything.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form (used with feminine nouns or to describe a female).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela tem uma camiseta preta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has a black T-shirt.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form of the adjective “preto”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: As camisas pretas são minhas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The black shirts are mine.

definitions.note: Often a false friend for English “pretend” (fingir).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela pretende mudar de emprego este ano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She intends to change jobs this year.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles pretendem viajar no próximo mês.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They intend to travel next month.

definitions.note: In Portuguese, pretender usually means “to intend/plan” (not “to pretend”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pretendemos viajar no próximo mês.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We intend to travel next month.

definitions.note: Imperfect past (eu/ele/ela/você): often used for a past intention or desire that was ongoing or not completed.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu pretendia ligar para você ontem, mas fiquei sem tempo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I intended to call you yesterday, but I ran out of time.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pretendo estudar português todos os dias.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I plan to study Portuguese every day.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele é muito pretensioso e vive falando das próprias conquistas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is very pretentious and is always talking about his own achievements.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O gato preto dorme no sofá.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The black cat sleeps on the couch.

definitions.note: As a noun, it usually refers to the color black (e.g., in clothing, design, printing).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu prefiro o preto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I prefer black.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os sapatos são pretos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The shoes are black.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No final, a justiça prevalece.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the end, justice prevails.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lavar as mãos ajuda a prevenir doenças.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Washing your hands helps prevent diseases.

definitions.note: Often used in the expression “prevenir alguém (de) que…” meaning “to warn someone (that…)”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vou te prevenir: a estrada está perigosa hoje.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to warn you: the road is dangerous today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A prevenção é melhor do que o tratamento.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Prevention is better than treatment.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: É difícil prever o que vai acontecer amanhã.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s hard to predict what will happen tomorrow.

definitions.note: Often used in more formal contexts to talk about something planned or foreseen (e.g., costs, dates, results).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O custo previsto é alto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The expected cost is high.

definitions.note: Past participle of “prever”; often used with “estar” (e.g., “está previsto”) meaning “is expected/planned.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Isso já estava previsto no contrato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That was already foreseen in the contract.

definitions.note: Often used for weather forecasts (previsão do tempo).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A previsão do tempo diz que vai chover amanhã.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The weather forecast says it’s going to rain tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O final do filme foi muito previsível.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The ending of the movie was very predictable.

definitions.note: Past tense (he/she/it/you formal).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O meteorologista previu chuva para amanhã.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The meteorologist predicted rain for tomorrow.

definitions.note: Often used to say that something (a plan, report, law, etc.) predicts or provides for something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O relatório prevê um aumento de preços.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The report predicts a rise in prices.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Qual é o preço deste livro?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What is the price of this book?

definitions.note: Plural of "preço".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os preços estão mais altos este ano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Prices are higher this year.

definitions.note: Female cousin; male cousin is "primo".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A minha prima mora em Lisboa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My cousin lives in Lisbon.

definitions.note: Feminine plural of "prima". For male cousins, use "primos"; for a mixed group, "primos" is common.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vou visitar as minhas primas no fim de semana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to visit my (female) cousins this weekend.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A primavera começa em setembro no Brasil.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Spring starts in September in Brazil.

definitions.note: Feminine form; used to refer to the first person/thing (female or feminine noun).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A primeira da fila chegou cedo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The first one in line arrived early.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form of "primeiro".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela foi a primeira pessoa a chegar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She was the first person to arrive.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Primeiramente, vamos ler o texto e depois responder às perguntas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: First, let's read the text and then answer the questions.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form of the adjective “primeiro”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: As primeiras aulas começam amanhã.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The first classes start tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este é o meu primeiro dia no trabalho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This is my first day at work.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Primeiro, vamos tomar um café.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: First, let's have a coffee.

definitions.note: Often used as an ordinal (“first”) or as a noun meaning “the first one/person/thing,” depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O primeiro da fila vai entrar agora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The first in line is going to go in now.

definitions.note: masculine plural form of the adjective
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os primeiros dias foram difíceis.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The first days were difficult.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A tecnologia daquela tribo era bem primitivo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That tribe’s technology was very primitive.

definitions.note: Male cousin; feminine form: prima.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O meu primo mora no Porto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My cousin lives in Porto.

definitions.note: Plural of "primo" (male or mixed group).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os meus primos moram em Lisboa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My cousins live in Lisbon.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form of the adjective (e.g., with a feminine noun like “escola”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A escola primária fica perto da minha casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The primary school is close to my house.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A princesa mora no castelo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The princess lives in the castle.

definitions.note: Diminutive of "princesa"; often used as an affectionate nickname for a girl.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A Ana é a princesinha do papai.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Ana is daddy’s little princess.

definitions.note: Plural form; used before plural nouns.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: As principais razões estão no relatório.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The main reasons are in the report.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O objetivo principal é aprender português.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The main goal is to learn Portuguese.

definitions.note: Often used as an adjective meaning “main” (e.g., 'a razão principal' = 'the main reason').
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O principal do problema é a falta de comunicação.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The main thing about the problem is the lack of communication.

definitions.note: In Portuguese, this is usually expressed as 'diretor/diretora' rather than 'principal'.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele é o principal da escola.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is the school principal.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu gosto principalmente de filmes de comédia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I mainly like comedy movies.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este curso é para principiantes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This course is for beginners.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Honestidade é um princípio importante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Honesty is an important principle.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No princípio do filme, eu não entendi a história.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At the beginning of the movie, I didn’t understand the story.

definitions.note: Often used for moral or ethical principles (e.g., having strong principles).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela tem princípios muito fortes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has very strong principles.

definitions.note: Plural of "princípio" can also mean the beginning of something, especially in the phrase "no(s) princípios" (at the beginning).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nos princípios do projeto, tudo parecia fácil.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At the beginning of the project, everything seemed easy.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Minha prioridade agora é estudar português todos os dias.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My priority right now is to study Portuguese every day.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Temos outras prioridades agora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have other priorities now.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Precisamos priorizar as tarefas mais urgentes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need to prioritize the most urgent tasks.

definitions.note: Used to describe something related to a prison system or prison environment (e.g., "sistema prisional").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O sistema prisional precisa de mais recursos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The prison system needs more resources.

definitions.note: As an adjective, it means “imprisoned/held captive.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele ficou prisioneiro por três dias.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was held prisoner for three days.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O prisioneiro foi levado para a cela.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The prisoner was taken to the cell.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os prisioneiros voltaram para as suas celas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The prisoners went back to their cells.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele foi enviado para a prisão por roubo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was sent to prison for theft.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Respeitamos a sua privacidade.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We respect your privacy.

definitions.note: Common in Brazil; in Portugal, “sanita” is more common.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Preciso usar a privada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to use the toilet.

definitions.note: feminine form of "privado"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela trabalha em uma empresa privada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She works at a private company.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este é um assunto privado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This is a private matter.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ter acesso a essa área é um privilégio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Having access to that area is a privilege.

definitions.note: Contraction of “para o” (used before a masculine singular noun). Very common in speech and informal writing.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vou pro trabalho agora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to work now.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A proa do navio apontava para o norte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bow of the ship was pointing north.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Há uma alta probabilidade de chover amanhã.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is a high probability that it will rain tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Temos um problema com o carro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have a problem with the car.

definitions.note: Plural of "problema".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Temos muitos problemas para resolver.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have many problems to solve.

definitions.note: Diminutive of "problema"; often used to downplay the seriousness of a problem or sometimes ironically.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Não se preocupe, é só um probleminha.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t worry, it’s just a small problem.

definitions.note: Augmentative of "problema"; often used informally to emphasize that a problem is serious.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Isso é um problemão para a empresa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This is a big problem for the company.

definitions.note: Often used in formal contexts (e.g., instructions, legal or administrative language).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vamos proceder com a reunião.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let’s proceed with the meeting.

definitions.note: Often used with “bem/mal” to talk about someone’s conduct.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele costuma proceder bem em situações difíceis.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He usually behaves well in difficult situations.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este é o procedimento padrão para abrir uma conta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This is the standard procedure for opening an account.

definitions.note: Often used in a medical context to mean a treatment or operation.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O médico explicou o procedimento antes da cirurgia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The doctor explained the procedure before the surgery.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O hospital atualizou os procedimentos de segurança.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The hospital updated the safety procedures.

definitions.note: Often used for a computer CPU.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este computador tem um processador rápido.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This computer has a fast processor.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O processamento dos dados demorou mais do que o esperado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The data processing took longer than expected.

definitions.note: Gerund form (used like “-ing” in English).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O computador está processando os dados.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The computer is processing the data.

definitions.note: Often used for handling data, paperwork, or steps in a procedure.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O sistema vai processar os dados automaticamente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The system will process the data automatically.

definitions.note: In legal contexts, it means to bring a lawsuit against someone.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela decidiu processar a empresa por danos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She decided to sue the company for damages.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O processo foi arquivado por falta de provas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The case was dismissed due to lack of evidence.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O computador processou os dados rapidamente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The computer processed the data quickly.

definitions.note: In legal contexts, "processar" means to take someone to court.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela processou a empresa por discriminação.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She sued the company for discrimination.

definitions.note: Usually refers to a religious procession.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A procissão passou pela praça ao entardecer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The procession passed through the square at dusk.

definitions.native: to procrastinate; to put off (doing something)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu costumo procrastinar quando tenho um trabalho difícil.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I tend to procrastinate when I have a difficult assignment.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Há muita procura por apartamentos no centro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is a lot of demand for apartments downtown.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A polícia continua a procura do suspeito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police continue searching for the suspect.

definitions.note: Often translated as “look for.” It resembles English “procure,” but Portuguese “procurar” usually means “to look for/search for,” not “to obtain.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela procura as chaves na bolsa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She looks for the keys in her bag.

definitions.note: Past participle of "procurar"; often used as an adjective (e.g., someone wanted by the police).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele é procurado pela polícia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is wanted by the police.

definitions.note: Often used for people who are being searched for by the police (e.g., “wanted”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os criminosos ainda estão procurados.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The criminals are still wanted.

definitions.note: Third-person plural (they/you all) present tense of "procurar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles procuram um lugar para morar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are looking for a place to live.

definitions.note: Often followed by an infinitive (e.g., "procuram ajudar" = "they try to help"). Third-person plural present tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles procuram ajudar sempre que podem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They try to help whenever they can.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Procuramos um restaurante perto daqui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re looking for a restaurant near here.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estou procurando minhas chaves.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m looking for my keys.

definitions.native: to look for; to search for
definitions.note: In Brazilian Portuguese you may also hear/see “procurar por”, but “procurar” without “por” is very common.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu vou procurar minhas chaves.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to look for my keys.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito perfeito), 3rd person plural: “they” (or “you all” in some contexts).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles procuraram as chaves por toda a casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They looked for the keys all over the house.

definitions.native: we will look for, we will search for
definitions.note: First-person plural ("we") in the future tense of "procurar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Procuraremos um hotel perto da praia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We will look for a hotel near the beach.

definitions.native: would look for, would search for
definitions.note: Conditional tense (eu/ele/ela/você/a gente).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu procuraria um emprego novo se tivesse mais tempo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would look for a new job if I had more time.

definitions.note: Imperfect past (used for an ongoing/habitual action in the past).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu procurava minhas chaves quando você ligou.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was looking for my keys when you called.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Procure suas chaves na gaveta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Look for your keys in the drawer.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Procure chegar cedo amanhã.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Try to arrive early tomorrow.

definitions.native: I looked for, I searched for
definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito perfeito) of "procurar" in the "eu" form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Procurei minhas chaves, mas não encontrei.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I looked for my keys, but I didn’t find them.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to save the rest for tomorrow.

definitions.note: Imperfect (past) form; often used to describe what was still available/possible at that time.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Only one chair remained in the room.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O resto do bolo ficou na geladeira.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I threw the leftovers in the trash.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The agreement resulted in a quick solution.

definitions.note: Often used in math to mean an infinite straight line.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A retirada de dinheiro no caixa eletrônico foi rápida.

definitions.note: Often used for lines, posture, or directions (masculine singular form: reto).

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela retornará ao trabalho na segunda-feira.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Olhe no retrovisor antes de mudar de faixa.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The story had a twist at the end.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Just wait a second, please.

definitions.note: Ordinal meaning “second” (2nd); agrees in gender/number (segundo/segunda/segundos/segundas).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este é o segundo dia da viagem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This is the second day of the trip.

definitions.note: Used before a noun/pronoun to introduce a source or viewpoint (e.g., “according to Maria”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Segundo o professor, a prova vai ser fácil.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: According to the teacher, the test will be easy.

definitions.note: Used to introduce a source, opinion, or reference (e.g., “according to the news/police/my friend”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Segundo o jornal, vai chover amanhã.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: According to the newspaper, it’s going to rain tomorrow.

definitions.note: Often used to cite a source or someone’s opinion (e.g., “segundo ele”, “segundo o jornal”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Segundo o médico, você precisa descansar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: According to the doctor, you need to rest.

definitions.note: Unit of time (1/60 of a minute).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espere um segundo, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Wait a second, please.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espere dois segundos, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Wait two seconds, please.

definitions.note: In Portuguese, "segundo" can mean the main course of a meal (after the first course).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No restaurante, os segundos são servidos ao meio-dia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At the restaurant, the main courses are served at noon.

definitions.note: Often used with an object (e.g., a hand, a bag) to mean physically holding or keeping something in place.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela segura a minha mão.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She holds my hand.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form of the adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A ponte é segura.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bridge is safe.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele seguramente vai chegar a tempo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He will surely arrive on time.

definitions.note: Present participle (gerund) of "segurar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estou segurando a sua mão.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m holding your hand.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A segurança do bairro melhorou muito este ano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The neighborhood’s safety improved a lot this year.

definitions.note: Plural form; often used to refer to people working security at places or events.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os seguranças estão na entrada do prédio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The security guards are at the entrance of the building.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Você pode segurar a minha mão?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you hold my hand?

definitions.native: to keep, to keep (something) from happening
definitions.note: Often used with "segurar" meaning to hold back or stop something (e.g., tears, laughter).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tentei segurar o riso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I tried to hold back my laughter.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: As crianças estão seguras em casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The children are safe at home.

definitions.note: Imperfect past tense (ongoing or repeated action in the past).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela segurava a mão do filho enquanto atravessavam a rua.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She was holding her son's hand while they crossed the street.

definitions.note: Often used as a command (imperative) or in the present subjunctive, depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Segure a minha bolsa, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Hold my bag, please.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito perfeito) of "segurar" for "eu".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu segurei a sua mão durante a travessia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I held your hand during the crossing.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (also used for affirmative commands with vocês).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Segurem bem a corda, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Hold the rope tightly, please.

definitions.note: Verb form of "segurar". Not to be confused with the adjective "seguro" meaning "safe/secure".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu seguro a sua mão.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hold your hand.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este bairro é seguro à noite.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This neighborhood is safe at night.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tenho certeza de que é assim, mas não estou seguro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m sure that’s how it is, but I’m not certain.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu preciso de um seguro para o carro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need insurance for the car.

definitions.note: Plural form of the adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os documentos estão seguros na gaveta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The documents are safe in the drawer.

definitions.note: Plural form of the adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles estão seguros de que vão chegar a tempo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are sure that they will arrive on time.

definitions.note: Plural form; often used to talk about insurance policies/types of coverage.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os seguros do carro e da casa estão mais caros este ano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Car and home insurance are more expensive this year.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela segurou a minha mão durante o filme.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She held my hand during the movie.

definitions.note: Common Brazilian Portuguese contraction of the infinitive “segurar” before an object pronoun (e.g., “segurá-lo/segurá-la”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vou segurá-la para você.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to hold it for you.

definitions.note: Present tense form of "saber" used with the meaning "to know" (facts, information).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu sei a resposta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I know the answer.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Não sei onde ele mora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't know where he lives.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela usou um sutiã que oferecia mais suporte aos seios.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She wore a bra that offered more support to her breasts.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu tenho seis livros.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have six books.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O museu recebeu seiscentos visitantes ontem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The museum received six hundred visitors yesterday.

definitions.note: Usually used for religious or ideological groups seen as extreme or controlling.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles acham que aquela organização é uma seita.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They think that organization is a cult.

definitions.note: Usually the present subjunctive form of "ser" (often used after expressions like "Espero que...", "Embora...", etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que seja verdade.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope it’s true.

definitions.note: used in the present subjunctive of ser
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que seja uma boa ideia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope it is a good idea.

definitions.note: used as the formal singular imperative of ser
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Seja gentil com os outros.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Be kind to others.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (vocês/eles/elas) of “ser”; often used after expressions of desire, doubt, or necessity.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que eles sejam pontuais.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope they are punctual.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (3rd person plural) of "ser"; used after expressions of desire, doubt, or necessity.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que eles sejam felizes aqui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope they are happy here.

definitions.note: 1st person plural present subjunctive of "ser"; often used after expressions of desire/necessity or in "sejamos + adjective" meaning "let’s be ...".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sejamos honestos: precisamos de ajuda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let’s be honest: we need help.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (tu) form of "ser"; used after expressions of doubt, desire, or uncertainty.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que sejas feliz.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you are happy.

definitions.note: Past participle of "selecionar"; often used like an adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O item selecionado aparece em azul.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The selected item appears in blue.

definitions.note: Past participle of "selecionar"; commonly used as an adjective or in passive/compound tenses.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os alunos selecionados vão receber um e-mail amanhã.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The selected students will receive an email tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A seleção de filmes deste ano está ótima.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This year’s selection of movies is great.

definitions.note: Often used in sports, especially to refer to Brazil’s or another country’s national team (e.g., futebol).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A seleção brasileira jogou muito bem ontem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The Brazilian national team played very well yesterday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tirei uma selfie na praia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I took a selfie at the beach.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Preciso de um selo para enviar esta carta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need a stamp to send this letter.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Preciso de dois selos para enviar estas cartas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need two stamps to send these letters.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A selva amazônica é muito rica em biodiversidade.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vimos um cavalo selvagem na montanha.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We saw a wild horse in the mountains.

definitions.note: Often used to describe a person’s behavior or an attack as very violent or cruel.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Foi um ataque selvagem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It was a savage attack.

definitions.note: Plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os animais selvagens vivem na floresta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Wild animals live in the forest.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can’t live without you.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I work five days a week.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I go to the gym weekly.

definitions.note: plural of "semana"

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We will stay here for two weeks.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles têm ideias semelhantes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They have similar ideas.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They have similar ideas about the project.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Há uma grande semelhança entre as duas fotos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is a big similarity between the two photos.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Plantei uma semente no jardim.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I planted a seed in the garden.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Plantei sementes de tomate no jardim.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I planted tomato seeds in the garden.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este semestre tenho aulas de português duas vezes por semana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This semester I have Portuguese classes twice a week.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are traffic lights on every corner on this avenue.

definitions.note: Common math abbreviation for “seno” in Portuguese, used in formulas (e.g., sen(30°)).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The senator gave a speech in parliament.

definitions.note: Gerund of "ser" (to be).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Being honest, I didn’t like the movie.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Qual é a senha do Wi‑Fi?

definitions.note: used as a polite form of address or before a man's surname
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bom dia, senhor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Good morning, sir.

definitions.note: a polite or formal way to refer to an adult man

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That gentleman lives near here.

definitions.note: used formally or politely for an adult woman

definitions.note: Plural of "senhora"; also used as a polite way to address a group of women (e.g., in speeches).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Senhoras e senhores, bem-vindos ao evento.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Boa noite, senhoritas. Posso ajudá-las?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Good evening, ladies. Can I help you?

definitions.note: Commonly used as a command (imperative) or with “você/ele/ela” in the present tense.

definitions.note: Feminine form; used to describe a woman or feminine noun.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are sitting on the sofa.

definitions.note: Often used as an adjective to describe someone’s position (can also function as the past participle of “sentar”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele está sentado no sofá.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is sitting on the sofa.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles estão sentados no sofá.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are sitting on the sofa.

definitions.note: Common in informal speech as a shortened form of “sentamos” (Brazilian Portuguese).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A gente sentamo ali e conversou um pouco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We sat down there and talked a bit.

definitions.note: Can mean present (we sit) or simple past (we sat), depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Depois do almoço, sentamos na sala para conversar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After lunch, we sat in the living room to talk.

definitions.note: Often used with the reflexive pronoun: sentar-se = “to sit down.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vou sentar aqui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to sit here.

definitions.note: Third-person plural simple past (preterite): “they” (or “you all” in some regions) sat down.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles sentaram perto da janela.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They sat down near the window.

definitions.note: Imperfect subjunctive of "sentar"; often used after expressions like "se" (if) or "queria que" (wanted (someone) to).

definitions.note: Imperfect past: can mean an ongoing action in the past (“was sitting”) or a habitual past action (“used to sit”), depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele sentava perto da janela todos os dias.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He used to sit near the window every day.

definitions.note: Often used as a polite command with você (e.g., “Sente-se”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sente-se aqui, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Sit here, please.

definitions.note: Present tense form of "sentir"; can also mean "smells" depending on context.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito perfeito) of "sentar" for "eu".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu me sentei no sofá.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I sat down on the couch.

definitions.note: Affirmative command for vocês (you all) from the verb “sentar”. Often used with “por favor” or “sentem-se” (sit down).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sentem, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Sit down, please.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They feel very cold in the winter.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele foi sentenciado a dez anos de prisão.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was sentenced to ten years in prison.

definitions.note: In everyday Portuguese, this most often means a grammatical sentence (in writing/speech).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The judge read the sentences at the end of the trial.

definitions.note: Feminine singular possessive; it agrees with the thing possessed (e.g., sua casa = 'your/his/her/their house'). Can also mean 'your' in formal address (equivalent to 'your' for você).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela perdeu a sua carteira.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She lost her wallet.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estou suando muito hoje.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m sweating a lot today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu começo a suar quando está muito quente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I start to sweat when it's very hot.

definitions.note: feminine plural form of "seu"; it agrees with the noun possessed, not with the owner
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela esqueceu suas chaves em casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She forgot her keys at home.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form of the possessive pronoun (agreeing with the thing possessed, not the owner).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Onde estão suas chaves?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Where are your keys?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este tecido é muito suave ao toque.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This fabric is very soft to the touch.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Fale suavemente para não acordar o bebê.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Speak softly so you don't wake the baby.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gosto da suavidade deste tecido.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like the softness of this fabric.

definitions.note: Usually a command (imperative) or present subjunctive form of "subir".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Por favor, suba as escadas com cuidado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please go up the stairs carefully.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (or affirmative command for “vocês”) of “subir” (to go up).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que vocês subam as escadas com cuidado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you go up the stairs carefully.

definitions.note: Often used as a command (imperative) or in the present subjunctive (e.g., after expressions like "é possível que" or "não quero que").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Não subestime a dificuldade deste exame.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t underestimate the difficulty of this exam.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele subestimou o tempo necessário para terminar o projeto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He underestimated the time needed to finish the project.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito perfeito) of "subir" (1st person singular).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Subi as escadas bem devagar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I went up the stairs very slowly.

definitions.native: was going up, used to go up
definitions.note: Imperfect form of "subir"; describes an ongoing/repeated action in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu subia a escada devagar porque estava cansado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was going up the stairs slowly because I was tired.

definitions.note: Past participle of "subir"; often used with "ter" (e.g., "tem subido") to talk about something that has been increasing/going up over time.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O preço tem subido muito este ano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The price has gone up a lot this year.

definitions.native: we went up, we climbed, we got on
definitions.note: Usually means “we went up / climbed” (past tense) or “we go up / climb” (present tense), depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ontem nós subimos a montanha bem cedo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday we climbed the mountain very early.

definitions.note: Present participle/gerund of "subir"; often used with "estar" to mean "to be going up / climbing / rising."
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O preço está subindo de novo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The price is going up again.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vou subir as escadas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to go up the stairs.

definitions.note: Common with transport: subir no ônibus/trem/avião.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela vai subir no ônibus agora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She’s going to get on the bus now.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito perfeito), 3rd person plural of “subir” (they/you all went up).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles subiram a escada rapidamente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They went up the stairs quickly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele saiu da sala subitamente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He suddenly left the room.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito perfeito) of “subir” for he/she/it/you (formal).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O preço do café subiu muito este mês.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The price of coffee went up a lot this month.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A vista do topo da montanha é sublime.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The view from the top of the mountain is sublime.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O submarino mergulhou rapidamente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The submarine dove quickly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os submarinos são usados pela marinha.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Submarines are used by the navy.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O mergulhador vai submergir lentamente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The diver is going to submerge slowly.

definitions.note: First-person singular (eu) present tense of "subir".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu subo as escadas todos os dias.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I climb the stairs every day.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O suboficial falou com os recrutas antes do treino.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The non-commissioned officer spoke with the recruits before training.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele tentou subornar o funcionário para conseguir o documento mais rápido.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He tried to bribe the employee to get the document faster.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O policial aceitou um suborno para ignorar a infração.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police officer accepted a bribe to ignore the violation.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele subornou o guarda para passar sem problemas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He bribed the guard to get through without problems.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O subsolo do prédio tem vagas de estacionamento.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The building's basement has parking spaces.

definitions.note: Refers to the layer below the surface of the ground.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O subsolo desta região é rico em minerais.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The underground/subsoil in this region is rich in minerals.

definitions.note: Present tense form of “substituir” (also used for the affirmative “you” command: “Replace!”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela substitui o professor hoje.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She replaces the teacher today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Preciso substituir esta lâmpada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to replace this light bulb.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela substituiu o açúcar por mel na receita.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She replaced the sugar with honey in the recipe.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A substituição do jogador foi no segundo tempo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The player substitution was in the second half.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O substituto vai dar a aula hoje.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The substitute is going to teach the class today.

definitions.note: Past tense (pretérito perfeito), 1st person singular.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu substituí o açúcar por mel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I replaced the sugar with honey.

definitions.note: past participle of "substituir"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O computador foi substituído por um modelo mais novo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The computer was replaced with a newer model.

definitions.note: past participle (masculine plural)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os arquivos foram substituídos por versões mais recentes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The files were replaced with more recent versions.

definitions.note: Past simple (pretérito perfeito), 3rd person plural: “they replaced” / “you (plural) replaced”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles substituíram o computador antigo por um novo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They replaced the old computer with a new one.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Não sabemos que substância está no frasco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We don’t know what substance is in the bottle.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Há um túnel subterrâneo sob a cidade.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is an underground tunnel under the city.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles se mudaram para um subúrbio tranquilo perto da cidade.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They moved to a quiet suburb near the city.

definitions.note: Often used with an indirect object to mean “happen to (someone)” (e.g., “O que te sucedeu?”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O que pode suceder amanhã?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What can happen tomorrow?

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito perfeito) form of “suceder.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O acidente sucedeu de repente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The accident happened suddenly.

definitions.note: Often used as part of the expression “bem-sucedida” (“successful”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A apresentação foi sucedida e o público aplaudiu.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The presentation was successful and the audience applauded.

definitions.note: Often used in the phrase “bem-sucedido” (“successful”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele é um profissional muito sucedido.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is a very successful professional.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O projeto foi um sucesso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The project was a success.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O sucessor do diretor será anunciado amanhã.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The director’s successor will be announced tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O livro teve muitos sucessos ao longo dos anos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The book had many successes over the years.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu quero um suco de laranja, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d like an orange juice, please.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O vento vem do sudeste.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The wind comes from the southeast.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A minha casa fica a sudoeste do centro da cidade.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My house is southwest of the city center.

definitions.note: Feminine form (used with feminine nouns or a woman).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My Swedish colleague lives in Lisbon.

definitions.note: usually refers to a male person from Sweden; for a female, use "sueca".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Meu colega é sueco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My coworker is Swedish.

definitions.note: refers to a person from Sweden
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O sueco mora em Estocolmo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The Swede lives in Stockholm.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu falo sueco um pouco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I speak Swedish a little.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tenho dinheiro suficiente para comprar o bilhete.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have enough money to buy the ticket.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Já é suficiente por hoje.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It's enough for today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Não tenho dinheiro suficiente para comprar isso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't have enough money to buy that.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O quarto é suficientemente grande para duas pessoas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The room is big enough for two people.

definitions.note: Plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Temos recursos suficientes para terminar o projeto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have enough resources to finish the project.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vou fazer um suflê de queijo para o jantar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to make a cheese soufflé for dinner.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Com essa fumaça, estou sufocando.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: With this smoke, I'm suffocating.

definitions.note: Can be literal (lack of air) or figurative (to feel overwhelmed/oppressed).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A fumaça começou a sufocar as pessoas dentro do prédio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The smoke started to suffocate the people inside the building.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O bebê suga o dedo para se acalmar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The baby sucks his thumb to calm down.

definitions.note: Often used for sucking something into the mouth (e.g., candy) or sucking liquid (e.g., through a straw).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A criança gosta de sugar o pirulito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The child likes to suck on the lollipop.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela sugere um restaurante perto daqui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She suggests a restaurant near here.

definitions.note: Past tense (pretérito perfeito) of “sugerir” for “eu” (I).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sugeri um restaurante italiano para o jantar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I suggested an Italian restaurant for dinner.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela está sugerindo um restaurante novo para o jantar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is suggesting a new restaurant for dinner.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Posso sugerir um restaurante perto daqui?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can I suggest a restaurant near here?

definitions.note: Conditional form (used for polite suggestions or hypothetical situations).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu sugeriria começar mais cedo para evitar trânsito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would suggest starting earlier to avoid traffic.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito perfeito) of “sugerir”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela sugeriu um restaurante perto daqui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She suggested a restaurant near here.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tenho uma sugestão para melhorar este projeto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a suggestion to improve this project.

definitions.note: Plural of "sugestão".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Você tem sugestões para melhorar este texto?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you have suggestions to improve this text?

definitions.note: First-person singular (eu) present tense of "sugerir".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sugiro que você fale com o professor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I suggest that you talk to the teacher.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele estava com pensamentos suicidas e procurou ajuda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was having suicidal thoughts and sought help.

definitions.note: In Portuguese it’s most commonly used with a reflexive pronoun: “suicidar-se” / “se suicidar”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele tentou se suicidar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He tried to commit suicide.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele se suicidou no ano passado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He committed suicide last year.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O suicídio é um problema de saúde pública.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Suicide is a public health problem.

definitions.note: feminine singular form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A camisa está suja.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The shirt is dirty.

definitions.note: feminine singular form of "sujo"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A camisa está suja.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The shirt is dirty.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Não quero sujar a camisa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't want to dirty my shirt.

definitions.note: feminine plural form (used with feminine plural nouns)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: As mãos dela estão sujas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Her hands are dirty.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form of “sujo”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: As mãos dela estão sujas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Her hands are dirty.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tem muita sujeira no chão da cozinha.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is a lot of dirt on the kitchen floor.

definitions.note: Often used with "a" to mean "subject to" (e.g., "sujeito a").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O contrato está sujeito a alterações.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The contract is subject to changes.

definitions.note: Often used in grammar (the subject of a sentence) and in more formal contexts (e.g., “subject to” rules or conditions).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O sujeito da frase é “ela”.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The subject of the sentence is “she”.

definitions.note: More informal; can sound a bit dismissive depending on context (like “that guy”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Aquele sujeito está esperando do lado de fora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That guy is waiting outside.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O chão está sujo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The floor is dirty.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os sapatos estão sujos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The shoes are dirty.

definitions.note: Past tense (preterite), 3rd person singular of “sujar” (to dirty).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A camisa sujou durante o almoço.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The shirt got dirty during lunch.

definitions.note: Often used in expressions like “do sul” (“from the south”) or “ao sul de” (“to the south of”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O sul do Brasil é conhecido pelo frio no inverno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The south of Brazil is known for the cold in winter.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O sul do Brasil é conhecido pelo clima mais frio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The south of Brazil is known for its colder climate.

definitions.note: Form of the verb “sumir” used in the present subjunctive (eu/ele/ela/você) and also as a (você) command.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que ele suma daqui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope he disappears from here.

definitions.note: Usually used with "que" after expressions of desire, doubt, or possibility (present subjunctive). It can also be a formal plural command meaning "(you all) disappear!"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que eles sumam logo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope they disappear soon.

definitions.note: Often used as the past participle of “sumir” (“to disappear”), or as an adjective meaning someone/something has been missing.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Meu celular está sumido desde ontem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My phone has been missing since yesterday.

definitions.note: Present participle/gerund form of "sumir"; often used with "estar" (e.g., "está sumindo" = "is disappearing").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O sol está sumindo atrás das nuvens.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The sun is disappearing behind the clouds.

definitions.note: In Brazil, it’s also often used informally to mean “to stop showing up / stop answering” (e.g., in messages).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Meu celular vai sumir se eu não tomar cuidado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My phone will disappear if I’m not careful.

definitions.note: Third-person plural (they/you all) in the simple past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: As chaves sumiram da mesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The keys disappeared from the table.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite) form of “sumir” (often used for people/things suddenly not being there).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Meu celular sumiu ontem à noite.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My phone disappeared last night.

definitions.note: Often refers to fruit juice.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quero um sumo de laranja, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d like an orange juice, please.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele gosta de ver sumo na televisão.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He likes to watch sumo on TV.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Depois da corrida, ele estava coberto de suor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the run, he was covered in sweat.

definitions.note: Informal.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O filme foi super!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The movie was great!

definitions.note: Informal; used to intensify adjectives or express enthusiasm.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O filme foi super legal!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The movie was super cool!

definitions.note: Third-person singular present tense of “superar” (can also be used with “você”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela supera as dificuldades com calma.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She overcomes difficulties calmly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela conseguiu superar o medo de falar em público.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She managed to overcome her fear of speaking in public.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A análise dele foi superficial.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His analysis was superficial.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A superfície da mesa está molhada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The surface of the table is wet.

definitions.note: Often used for someone who oversees a department or organization (e.g., in a company or public administration).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A superintendente reuniu a equipe para discutir o novo projeto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The superintendent gathered the team to discuss the new project.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este produto é superior ao outro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This product is superior to the other one.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Preciso falar com o meu superior.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to talk to my superior.

definitions.note: Plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os andares superiores têm uma vista melhor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The upper floors have a better view.

definitions.note: Plural form; refers to people in a higher position (e.g., at work).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tenho de falar com os meus superiores antes de decidir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to talk to my superiors before deciding.

definitions.note: Used for people with higher rank/authority, especially at work.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Preciso falar com os meus superiores sobre este problema.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to talk to my superiors about this problem.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vou ao supermercado comprar frutas e pão.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to the supermarket to buy fruit and bread.

definitions.note: Simple past (ele/ela/você) of “superar”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela superou o medo de falar em público.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She overcame her fear of speaking in public.

definitions.note: Simple past (ele/ela/você) of “superar”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O atleta superou o recorde do ano passado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The athlete surpassed last year's record.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele não acredita em superstição.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He doesn't believe in superstition.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Fale com o supervisor, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please speak with the supervisor.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A supervisão do projeto ficou com a Ana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Ana was in charge of supervising the project.

definitions.note: Present tense (eu) of “suplicar”; often used for an urgent or emotional request.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu suplico que você me perdoe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I beg you to forgive me.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Supondo que chova, vamos ficar em casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Assuming it rains, we’re going to stay at home.

definitions.note: Often used to introduce a hypothetical situation; can be used as a command (“suppose...”) or in phrases like “suponha que...” (“suppose that...”).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Suppose it rains tomorrow: what are we going to do?

definitions.note: First-person singular ("I") present tense of "supor".

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I suppose he’ll arrive early.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu vou supor que ele esteja em casa.

definitions.note: Can mean emotional/financial support (“supports”) or enduring something unpleasant (“tolerates/puts up with”), depending on context.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She tolerates the pressure at work very well.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Não consigo suportar esse calor.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't want such a thing in my house.

definitions.note: Often used to refer back to something mentioned ("like that") or to mean "such" before a noun (e.g., "tal coisa" = "such a thing").

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He did it just like I said.

definitions.note: Often used to refer to something/someone previously mentioned or implied (like “such a…”).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I've never seen such a thing!

definitions.note: Can be used before a noun in expressions like “tal pessoa” (“such a person”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele não é tal pessoa.

definitions.note: Often used to refer to someone or something previously mentioned or identified (like “such-and-such”).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The tanks are full of water.

definitions.native: so much, so many, such a (great) amount of
definitions.note: Feminine singular form of "tanto"; used before feminine singular nouns.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has so much patience with the children.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: So many people came to the party!

definitions.note: Feminine plural form, used with feminine plural nouns or implied feminine plural things.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Conheço tantas pessoas aqui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I know so many people here.

definitions.note: Often used in comparisons (tanto... quanto = as much... as) or with 'quanto' to ask/answer about quantity.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't like coffee that much.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was so tired that he went to sleep early.

definitions.note: Used in the correlative structure “tanto … como/quanto …” to connect two parallel elements (like “both … and …”).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Both João and Maria like coffee.

definitions.native: so much, so many; as much, as many

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t have so much money.

definitions.note: Refers to an amount or degree; can also be used for countable nouns as “so many/as many” (then it often changes form: tanta, tantos, tantas).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu não quero tanto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t want that much.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form; used before a masculine plural noun (often implies a large number).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are so many books in this room!

definitions.note: Masculine plural form; used with masculine plural nouns (or on its own as a pronoun).

definitions.note: Also commonly means “lid/cover” in Portuguese, but “slap” is the more common everyday meaning for beginners.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Comprei dois tapetes para a sala.

definitions.note: Offensive/derogatory term for someone seen as sexually inappropriate; avoid in polite conversation.

definitions.note: Often used with "ser/estar" to talk about the time (e.g., "É tarde" = "It’s late").
