definitions.example_sentence_target_language: As tartarugas vivem no mar e também em rios.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Turtles live in the sea and also in rivers.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela fez uma tatuagem no braço.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela tem duas tatuagens no braço.

definitions.note: Informal spoken form of “estava” (imperfect of estar), often used as an auxiliary (e.g., with a gerund).

definitions.note: Imperfect past; often used for ongoing/habitual actions in the past. Commonly used with musical instruments.

definitions.note: Imperfect past; often used for ongoing/habitual actions in the past.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele tocou violão na festa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He played guitar at the party.

definitions.note: Often used with "a campainha" (doorbell) or "o alarme" (alarm).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The phone rang twice.

definitions.note: Informal/colloquial spelling/pronunciation of "tocar" (common in Brazilian Portuguese, dropping the final -r).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu sei tocá violão.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I know how to play the guitar.

definitions.note: Informal/colloquial spelling/pronunciation of "tocar" (common in Brazilian Portuguese, dropping the final -r).

definitions.note: Informal/colloquial spelling/pronunciation of "tocar" (common in Brazilian Portuguese, dropping the final -r).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vai tocá a campainha, por favor.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form; used before a feminine singular noun (e.g., “toda a cidade”).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She spent the whole afternoon studying.

definitions.note: Used before a feminine singular noun, often with the article: toda a...
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela passou toda a tarde estudando.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She spent the whole afternoon studying.

definitions.note: Used before a feminine singular noun without an article.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela caminha toda manhã.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She walks every morning.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form of "todo"; it agrees with a feminine singular noun (e.g., "toda a casa").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela passou toda a tarde estudando.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She spent the whole afternoon studying.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Todas as portas estavam abertas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: All the doors were open.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form of "todo"; used with feminine plural nouns/pronouns.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu conheço todas as minhas vizinhas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I know all my neighbors.

definitions.note: Adjective meaning “entire/complete.” Often changes to agree in gender and number (todo/toda/todos/todas).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu li o livro todo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I read the whole book.

definitions.note: As an adverb, it often means “entirely/fully” or “all the way,” depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Fiquei todo molhado na chuva.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I got completely soaked in the rain.

definitions.note: Before a singular noun without an article, it usually means "every" or "each".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Todo dia eu estudo português.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I study Portuguese every day.

definitions.note: With an article, as in "todo o" or "todo a", it usually means "all" or "the whole".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Li todo o livro em dois dias.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I read the whole book in two days.

definitions.note: Usually agrees in gender/number with the noun (todo/toda/todos/todas).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Todo mundo quer descansar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Everyone wants to rest.

definitions.note: Often used before a definite article, as in "todos os..." = "all the..."
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Todos os alunos chegaram cedo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: All the students arrived early.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form; it can refer to a group of men or to a mixed-gender group.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Todos chegaram cedo à reunião.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Everyone arrived early to the meeting.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu gosto de tofu grelhado com legumes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like grilled tofu with vegetables.

definitions.note: feminine singular form of "tolo".

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She thought the idea was silly.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form of "tolo".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elas fizeram perguntas tolas durante a reunião.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They asked silly questions during the meeting.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela é muito tolerante com os erros dos outros.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is very tolerant of other people's mistakes.

definitions.note: plural form (more than one person/thing)

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My neighbors are very tolerant about the noise.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can’t tolerate lies.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Não tolerarei esse tipo de comportamento.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will not tolerate that kind of behavior.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Isso é uma tolice.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Não seja tolo!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don't be silly!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele é um tolo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is a fool.

definitions.note: Plural masculine form of "tolo".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles são tolos às vezes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are silly sometimes.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles são tolos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are fools.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gosto do tom da sua voz.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like the tone of your voice.

definitions.note: Also used as an informal way to say “here you go” when giving something to someone.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele toma um café todas as manhãs.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He takes (has) a coffee every morning.

definitions.note: Used with beverages in Portuguese where English often says “drink” rather than “take.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela toma água depois do treino.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She drinks water after the workout.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tem uma tomada perto da cama?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Is there an outlet near the bed?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A tomada do poder aconteceu rapidamente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The takeover of power happened quickly.

definitions.note: Past participle of "tomar" used in the feminine singular (often in passive voice or as an adjective).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A decisão foi tomada ontem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The decision was made yesterday.

definitions.note: Past participle (feminine plural) of "tomar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: As decisões já foram tomadas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The decisions have already been made.

definitions.note: Past participle of "tomar"; often used with auxiliaries like "ter/haver" (e.g., "tinha tomado") or as an adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu já tinha tomado o remédio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I had already taken the medicine.

definitions.note: Present tense (they/you all) form of "tomar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles tomam café todas as manhãs.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They drink coffee every morning.

definitions.note: From the verb “tomar.” Often used for having food/drinks (e.g., coffee).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nós tomamos café todas as manhãs.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We drink coffee every morning.

definitions.note: Present participle/gerund of "tomar"; often used to describe an action in progress (e.g., "estou tomando...").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estou tomando um café agora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m having a coffee now.

definitions.note: Often used with drinks/medicine (e.g., tomar café, tomar um remédio).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vou tomar um café agora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to have a coffee now.

definitions.note: Common with transport: tomar o ônibus, tomar o metrô.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela vai tomar o ônibus todos os dias.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is going to take the bus every day.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito perfeito) of “tomar” for “they/you all” (vocês/eles/elas).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles tomaram o ônibus cedo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They took the bus early.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito perfeito) of “tomar” for “they/you all” (vocês/eles/elas), often used with drinks (e.g., café, água, suco).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elas tomaram café da manhã às sete.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They had breakfast at seven.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tomarei o ônibus às oito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll take the bus at eight.

definitions.note: Usually used as “if/when they take” (future subjunctive) or “for them to take” (personal infinitive), depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se eles tomarem o remédio, vão se sentir melhor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If they take the medicine, they’ll feel better.

definitions.native: we will take, we will have
definitions.note: First-person plural (nós) in the simple future.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Amanhã tomaremos uma decisão importante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow we will make an important decision.

definitions.note: Conditional form of "tomar"; often used to express a hypothetical or polite idea.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu tomaria um café agora, se tivesse tempo.

definitions.note: Conditional form of "tomar"; commonly used with drinks/medicine (e.g., coffee, water, medicine).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela tomaria o remédio, mas esqueceu.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She would take the medicine, but she forgot.

definitions.note: 3rd-person singular (ele/ela/você) future tense of “tomar”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele tomará o remédio depois do almoço.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He will take the medicine after lunch.

definitions.note: Imperfect subjunctive form of "tomar", often used after "se" (if) to talk about hypothetical situations.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se eu tomasse esse remédio, eu me sentiria melhor.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought tomatoes at the market.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Comprei tomates no mercado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought tomatoes at the market.

definitions.note: Imperfect past (ação habitual/contínua no passado).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu tomava café todas as manhãs.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I used to have coffee every morning.

definitions.note: Often used as a formal command (for você) or in the present subjunctive.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tome este remédio duas vezes por dia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Take this medicine twice a day.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito perfeito) of "tomar"; often means "I drank" when talking about beverages, and "I took" with medicine or objects.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ontem eu tomei um café e depois tomei o remédio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday I drank a coffee and then I took the medicine.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (vocês/eles/elas); also used as the affirmative imperative for vocês.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tomem este remédio depois do almoço.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Take this medicine after lunch.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu tomo o ônibus às oito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I take the bus at eight.

definitions.note: Often used with beverages and also medicines (e.g., "tomo um café", "tomo um remédio").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu tomo um café de manhã.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I drink a coffee in the morning.

definitions.note: Commonly used for taking something (e.g., medicine) or having a drink/meal, depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela tomou o remédio depois do almoço.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She took the medicine after lunch.

definitions.note: Informal/colloquial spoken form of “tomar” (dropping the final -r), common in some Brazilian dialects.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vou tomá um café antes de sair.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to have a coffee before leaving.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The truck carries a ton of sand.

definitions.note: Feminine form of the adjective (used with feminine nouns or for women/girls).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Não seja tonta; é só uma brincadeira.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t be silly; it’s just a joke.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Foi tonto da minha parte esquecer a chave em casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It was silly of me to forget the key at home.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estou tonto depois de levantar muito rápido.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m dizzy after standing up too quickly.

definitions.note: Common in everyday speech; can be mildly insulting depending on tone.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Não seja tonto!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t be a fool!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Senti tontura quando me levantei rápido.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I felt dizzy when I stood up quickly.

definitions.note: Common in informal Brazilian Portuguese to mean accepting an invitation or proposal.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Você topa ir ao cinema hoje?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele topa com um velho amigo na rua.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He runs into an old friend on the street.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm up for going to the movies with you guys.

definitions.native: I run into, I come across

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I always run into him at the market.

definitions.note: Often used for the highest point of a mountain or hill; also used for the top part of something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Chegamos ao topo da montanha ao amanhecer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We reached the top of the mountain at sunrise.

definitions.note: Often used as a (formal) command: “Don’t touch.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Por favor, não toque nisso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please, don’t touch that.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que ela toque violão na festa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope she plays guitar at the party.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Não gosto do toque desse tecido.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't like the feel of this fabric.

definitions.note: Past (pretérito perfeito) form of "tocar" for "I"; it can mean physically touching or playing an instrument.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ontem, toquei piano pela primeira vez.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday, I played the piano for the first time.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (also used for negative commands) of "tocar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Por favor, não toquem no vidro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please, don’t touch the glass.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele torce a toalha para tirar a água.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He twists the towel to remove the water.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She cheers for Brazil in the World Cup.

definitions.note: Often also used figuratively to mean “rooting/cheering for” a team or person, depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele está torcendo a toalha para tirar a água.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is twisting the towel to get the water out.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Preciso torcer a toalha antes de pendurá-la.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to wring the towel before hanging it up.

definitions.note: Often used with por/pelo: torcer por alguém/algum time.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vou torcer pelo Brasil no jogo de hoje.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to root for Brazil in today’s game.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele torceu o tornozelo jogando futebol.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He sprained his ankle playing soccer.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I sprained my ankle playing soccer.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele torna para casa tarde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He returns home late.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A situação torna-se perigosa rapidamente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The situation becomes dangerous quickly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O tornado causou muitos danos na cidade.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The tornado caused a lot of damage in the city.

definitions.note: Past participle of "tornar" (often used with "ter" + "se": "tem se tornado" = "has become"). Not the weather word "tornado" in English (that in Portuguese is usually "tornado" as a noun, but this entry is the verb form).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele tem se tornado mais confiante com o tempo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He has become more confident over time.

definitions.note: 3rd-person plural (they/you all) present of “tornar”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: As folhas tornam-se amarelas no outono.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The leaves turn yellow in the fall.

definitions.native: we make, we turn (into), we become
definitions.note: Commonly used with an adjective or noun (e.g., "tornar-se" = "to become").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Com o treino, tornamos o processo mais fácil.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: With practice, we make the process easier.

definitions.note: Often used with "estar" to express an ongoing change or effect (e.g., "está tornando...").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O barulho está tornando a aula difícil.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The noise is making the class difficult.

definitions.note: Often used with “-se” (tornar-se) meaning “to become.” Without “-se,” it can mean “to make/turn something into” (tornar algo + adjective/noun).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A situação pode tornar complicada a decisão.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The situation can make the decision complicated.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito perfeito), 3rd person plural: “they/you (plural) became.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles tornaram-se amigos depois da viagem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They became friends after the trip.

definitions.note: Often used with the reflexive pronoun: "me tornarei" = "I will become". Slightly formal compared to "vou ficar" or "vou virar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Um dia, eu me tornarei médico.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: One day, I will become a doctor.

definitions.note: More formal/literary; in everyday speech, "voltarei" is more common.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tornarei amanhã à tarde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will return tomorrow afternoon.

definitions.note: Most commonly means “will become” (future tense). In some contexts it can mean “will make/turn (something) into.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele se tornará médico no próximo ano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He will become a doctor next year.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que você se torne médico.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you become a doctor.

definitions.note: Often used with a reflexive pronoun: “tornei-me …” = “I became …”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Depois do curso, tornei-me mais confiante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the course, I became more confident.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Com a reforma, tornei o quarto mais aconchegante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: With the renovation, I made the room cozier.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O torneio começa amanhã de manhã.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The tournament starts tomorrow morning.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A torneira da cozinha está pingando.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The kitchen faucet is dripping.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O enfermeiro colocou um torniquete no braço do paciente para estancar o sangramento.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The nurse put a tourniquet on the patient’s arm to stop the bleeding.

definitions.note: a machine used to shape materials (like wood or metal) by rotating them

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O médico vai tratar a infecção.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles trataram o cachorro com muito carinho.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles trataram do problema ontem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They dealt with the problem yesterday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: É melhor esperar para eles voltarem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s better to wait for them to come back.

definitions.native: we will return, we will come back
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voltaremos para casa depois do jantar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We will come back home after dinner.

definitions.note: Conditional form of "voltar".

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would come back earlier, but I have a meeting.

definitions.note: Form used for “we” in the personal infinitive or the future subjunctive, often after words like se (“if”) or quando (“when”).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If we return early, we'll have dinner at home.

definitions.note: Third-person singular future tense of “voltar” (can also be used with “você”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele voltará amanhã de manhã.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He will return tomorrow morning.

definitions.note: 3rd person plural (they) in the future tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles voltarão amanhã de manhã.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They will come back tomorrow morning.

definitions.note: Plural of "volta"; often used for turns around a track or repeated cycles.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele deu três voltas no parque.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He did three laps around the park.

definitions.note: Imperfect subjunctive of "voltar"; often used after "se" (if) or to express a wish/possibility in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se ele voltasse hoje, eu ficaria muito feliz.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If he came back today, I would be very happy.

definitions.native: was coming back, used to come back
definitions.note: Imperfect past of "voltar".

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He used to come back home every day at six.

definitions.note: Used in the present subjunctive (e.g., “que eu/ele volte”) and also as an affirmative command for “você” (e.g., “Volte!”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que você volte amanhã.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you come back tomorrow.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito perfeito) of "voltar" for "eu".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voltei para casa cedo ontem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I came back home early yesterday.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (or affirmative command) form of “voltar” for “vocês” (you all).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que vocês voltem amanhã.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you all come back tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Volto amanhã.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll be back tomorrow.

definitions.note: Simple past (ele/ela/você form) of “voltar”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela voltou para casa ontem à noite.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She came back home last night.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O volume da música está muito alto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The volume of the music is very loud.

definitions.note: Often used for numbered books in a series (e.g., Volume 1).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu comprei o segundo volume da coleção.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought the second volume of the collection.

definitions.note: Usually used with "para" (to volunteer for) or "em" (to volunteer at/in).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela se voluntariou para ajudar na arrecadação de alimentos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She volunteered to help with the food drive.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form of the adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela participou de uma ação voluntária no fim de semana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She took part in a voluntary activity over the weekend.

definitions.note: In Portuguese, this form can also be used as a noun meaning a female volunteer, depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A voluntária ajudou a organizar o evento.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The volunteer helped organize the event.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O trabalho voluntário ajuda muitas pessoas.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele é voluntário em um abrigo aos fins de semana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is a volunteer at a shelter on weekends.

definitions.note: Plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os voluntários ajudaram a organizar o evento.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The volunteers helped organize the event.

definitions.note: Less common than “voltar” in modern everyday Brazilian Portuguese; more frequent in European Portuguese and in fixed expressions (e.g., “voltar a” is usually preferred in Brazil).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I promise to come back tomorrow.

definitions.note: This use is more typical in Spanish; in Portuguese, “virar” is usually preferred for “flip/turn over,” but “volver” may appear in older/literary usage or regional varieties.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele vomitou depois do jantar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He threw up after dinner.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tenho vontade de viajar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I feel like traveling.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My flight leaves at eight in the morning.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The flights to Lisbon are delayed.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I thank you all for the help.

definitions.note: Formal (used with "você", "o senhor", "a senhora"); feminine singular form (e.g., "vossa casa").

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Your house is very beautiful.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Your bags are already in the car.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os vossos amigos já chegaram?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Have your friends arrived already?

definitions.note: Plural form of "vosso". Used with "vós" (you-plural) in European Portuguese; in Brazilian Portuguese it’s more common to use "seu/sua/seus/suas" instead.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Onde estão os vossos livros?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Where are your books?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela vota sempre nas eleições.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu vou votar amanhã.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to vote tomorrow.

definitions.note: 3rd person plural (they/you all) in the simple past (pretérito perfeito).

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Meu voto vai para a candidata mais experiente.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os votos foram contados no fim da eleição.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The votes were counted at the end of the election.

definitions.note: Often used in fixed expressions like "votos de casamento" (wedding vows).

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela votou nas eleições ontem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She voted in the election yesterday.

definitions.note: Used before an infinitive to express the near future.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My grandmas live in the same city.

definitions.note: Affectionate/informal term (especially used by children) for one’s grandfather.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Meu vovô mora perto da praia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My grandpa lives near the beach.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gosto da sua voz.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like your voice.

definitions.note: Plural of "voz".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ouvi várias vozes no corredor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I heard several voices in the hallway.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O vulcão entrou em erupção ontem à noite.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive / imperative form of "ir"; used for commands ("Go!") and in expressions like "Que você vá...".

definitions.note: feminine singular form

definitions.note: feminine plural form; used before feminine plural nouns

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tenho vários amigos em Lisboa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have several friends in Lisbon.

definitions.note: Plural masculine form; often used before a noun (e.g., “vários livros”).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have several friends in Lisbon.
